You can now add videos and other embedded media into Job listings (Recruit) and into tasks (Onboard).

Choose the following links for more information:

- Embedding Video in Recruit

The layout of the Reports tab has been adjusted and divided into two sections. The first section is labeled Dashboard Reports. These reports are turn-key reports that display various recruiting metrics. The Dashboard Reports consist of:

1. Source Performance - The number of applicants and hires from each source
2. Time in Stage for Active Candidates – The average number of days active candidates have been in the workflow. You can use this report to determine if candidates are getting "stuck" in any of the stages of your workflow.
3. Hire Metrics - The summary of hire metrics for your jobs or departments. You can use this report to track hire metrics like % Hired and determine what percent of candidates are still Active in your workflow.
4. Stage Conversion - The number and percent of candidates that passed key stages of your workflow. You can use this report to determine where candidates are dropping out of your workflow.

These reports are custom tailored to your account and cannot be customized. You can filter these reports based on various categories.

The second section is My Reports and contains account level reports that can be altered as well as reports that you have created.

[Screenshot]

You can now send documents in Recruit and have the applicant sign them. This feature can be used for Offer Letters as well as any other documents that you create in ApplicantStack Recruit that may need an applicant’s signature.

We start with creating a document in ApplicantStack. To do this see [Library - Documents](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Documents). Once you have created this document, you can assign or attach it to your desired candidate. Click the candidate’s name. You will see the Candidate’s Summary Tab. Look for an option on the right menu labeled “Create Document”. Clicking this option will present you with the following screen:

[Screenshot]

Select the document that you wish to assign to and have the candidate sign. Click submit. If your document has any document fields, you will be able to supply answers to those fields at this point. Once you have supplied your answers (if any), click Next and you will be presented with the following screen:

[Screenshot]

On this screen you can rename the document as well as make any edits to the document. Once you click Save, a PDF of your document is generated and will appear on your candidate like below:

[Screenshot]

You will notice that the newly created document has a status of Not Sent. When you are ready to send your document, click the email icon.

[Screenshot]

This opens up the Email Candidate screen, but there is a very important addition. This section is titled “Include Documents”. In this section you can include additional documents that have been attached to the applicant as well as select whether you want the document to have an electronic signature. If this box is checked, then the email will contain a link to view and sign the document online. If not checked, the document will be attached as a PDF to the email. Also any documents that have already been signed by the candidate will be sent as an attachment (including their signature), and will not ask for a signature.

**Note: Documents created prior to July 16th, 2018 will not be eligible for electronic signature. Please create a new document in the system to require signature.**

[Screenshot]

Click Send and the email will be sent to the candidate. The status of the document will change to pending. [Screenshot]

When the candidate receives the email, they click the link supplied and are able to read the document and sign it through their web browser using either their desktop or mobile device.

[Screenshot]

Once the document has been signed, you will receive an email confirmation of the signature and will see the following on the Candidate Summary Tab.

[Screenshot]

You now have the ability to add fields to the hire portal.

For more information see [New Hire Portal](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/New-Hire-Portal)

[Screenshot]

We are pleased to announce that we have partnered with Namely for integration to their payroll and benefits platform.

See the following article outlining how to set up the integration within your ApplicantStack account:

[Namely Integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Namely-Integration)

We have launched an integrations page in ApplicantStack Recruit to make it easier for Administrators to add integrations to our wonderful partners.

**Integrations are free to use within ApplicantStack but require an account and/or subscription directly from the individual partners.**

[Screenshot]

See [https://help.applicantstack.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000205293-Partners-](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/topic/0TO0P000000olO8WAI/partners) for the individual user guides.

We have added improvements to workflows in both Recruit and Onboard.

For Recruit we have altered the "Set Stage" button on both the Job and Candidate Detail pages. You'll notice that the button is now green and, instead of "Set Stage", the button is labeled with the very first action "Pass" action from its drop down menu. Also you will notice a red button has been placed beside the former "Set Stage" button and it's label is knock out action, such as "Fail Review" or "Withdrawn from Process".

[Screenshot]

We have also made some improvements in the workflow setup. These include:

1. Added Expand All and Collapse All buttons for Stage panels
2. Added a "Add New Stage to Workflow" button to the top of the screen, which will allow users to instantly add a new stage to the current workflow
3. Clicking "Edit Workflow Stage" on the Stage panel opens a modal allowing you to make your changes without leaving the current workflow screen.
4. If you create a stage and it is not part of the existing workflow, you will have a notification over the button "Add New Stage to Workflow". Clicking this notification will list the stage(s) that is missing from the workflow and allow you to select and add the stage to the current workflow.

[Screenshot]

*Edit Application Workflow screen in Recruit*

[Screenshot]

*Edit Application Workflow screen in Recruit with Edit Workflow Stage modal.*

We improved our Onboard workflow experience by adding multiple workflows! Now your hires can have different workflows based on their employee type, state they reside, etc. Also when you move a candidate to the Hired stage in recruit, the stage change dialog box allows you to select the new hire's workflow as well as their Onboard Manager! Note that the Onboard product is required for this option to appear.

In Onboard on the Hire Details page, you will notice that the Hire Workflow Actions button has been replaced with the Stage Action name that will move the hire to the next stage. The button has been moved from the right side of the screen to the left and has had its orange color changed to green.

[Screenshot]

In the example above, clicking Begin Paperwork will move the Hire to the Paperwork stage that was set up in the Hire Workflow. See [Configure Hire Workflow in ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Hire-Workflow-in-ApplicantStack) for more information.

When adding a new hire manually to Onboard, you will notice that you now have the capability to set that hire's workflow on the Add Hire screen. If you only have one workflow or are using the system default workflow only, the system will use that workflow for the Hire.

t: 2019-11-07 Texting Enhancement Features - Email Notifications and Bulk Texting (Recruit)
b:
## 2019-11-07 Release Texting Enhancements Features - Email Notifications & Bulk Texting

In this update, we are adding two new features to enhance our texting feature:

- Email Notifications - to receive an email notification when a text message is received
- Bulk Texting - to send the same message to multiple candidates

NOTE: The texting feature must be enabled by an Administrator on the Settings page. For more information on how to set it up, see the following article: [Activate Texting for ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack).

### Email Notifications:

We have added an email notification option for all incoming text messages.

To enable this new feature go to your account settings page by clicking on your avatar:

[Screenshot]

Then select "My Account":

[Screenshot]

To turn on the Text Email Notifications, select "Edit Account":

[Screenshot]

Then Set the Text Email Notifications to "On" or "Off":

[Screenshot]

[Screenshot]

This is what a sample email notification will look like. You will notice the message as well as a convenient link to reply to the conversation:

[Screenshot]

### Bulk Texting:

From the candidate view table, you can now select multiple candidates by selecting several at a time or the top most checkbox (this will select ***all*** of the candidates in the current view table page). You will also notice a new column "P" which will indicate which candidate(s) have a mobile phone available for a text message:

Note: Only mobile numbers can receive the text message. If you send a text message to a non-mobile number you will receive an error message.

[Screenshot]

Once you select multiple candidates, you will need to select "Text Candidate" from the right-side menu:

[Screenshot]

Then begin typing your message, include any questionnaires, and hit "Send"

IMPORTANT: Each candidate will receive their own unique text message and will be unaware of any other individual on the list. This is **NOT** a group text message!

If you try to send a text message to a non-mobile number, you will see the following error message:

[Screenshot]

Close up to the error message:

[Screenshot]

You can continue with the message, knowing that there will be no message sent to the above candidates.

You can also send text messages to an individual candidate by selecting the checkbox next to their name and selecting "Text Candidate":

[Screenshot]

For more information about texting and how to enable it in your account, see the following article: [Activate Texting for ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack)

## 2021-10-21 Texting Compliance

This ApplicantStack release includes notifications and tools related to text messaging compliance. Cell phone service providers now require any company sending texts with a ten-digit phone number (referred to as a 10-digit long code or “10DLC”) to document their company contact information and provide recipients a way to opt-out of text messaging. To address this, ApplicantStack now collects your company’s information, including your EIN, through a *Carrier Compliance Form* which is filled out when activating the text messaging feature. Also, candidates and new hires now have the ability to opt-out of text messaging by replying with “STOP” to any text message.

**If your company was already using texting,** then your carrier compliance form was automatically completed for you. This compliance information can be viewed and changed by Administrators in the account setup. Also, when you log into ApplicantStack, a pop-up notifies users that candidates and new hires can now opt-out of text messaging.

[Screenshot: Text Compliance Pop Up]

Opt-Out of texting notification pop-up

Also, as part of this release, the ability to *activate* texting has been moved to the **Billing** area of the account setup. A wizard walks you through the process, which includes the carrier compliance form. The *settings* associated with texting, like the incoming text notifications, are still configured in the **Settings** area of account setup.

Finally, if a candidate or new hire opts-out of texting with “STOP”, then you are notified of that when trying to send them a message. A recipient can re-start messaging by texting “START” to the text messaging number.

## 2021-11-09 Acknowledgement of Text Compliance

In this release, companies using ApplicantStack’s texting feature are asked to acknowledge compliance with recently enacted regulations related to text messaging. These regulations include a requirement that businesses identify themselves with the various phone carriers and that text recipients are given an option to opt-out of texting. This acknowledgement appears as a pop-up upon logging in. There is no action that needs to be taken other than acknowledging the message; the required company information was collected automatically from the ApplicantStack account information. To learn more about this requirement, see the topic [Carrier Compliance](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack#carrier-compliance) in the article [Activate Texting for ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack).

## 2022-05-26 Indeed Integration Updates

ApplicantStack's integration with Indeed has changed. You still have the ability to post your jobs to Indeed's Organic and Sponsored feeds, but the process now looks a little different and you can now access your Indeed account and Indeed support through ApplicantStack. The article [Indeed Sponsored Jobs Integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Sponsored-Jobs-Integration) has been updated to show the new process.

*IMPORTANT:* Sponsored jobs posted *prior* to update are still active and still appear in the *Indeed Sponsored* section of your Launch page. However, you can no longer manage these campaigns from within ApplicantStack, instead, you need to manage them from within Indeed.

## 2022-10-05 Premium Texting

An additional tier of features has been added to ApplicantStack's texting functionality. The new **Premium Texting** plan offers the features of Basic Texting, plus the following:

- **Text-to-Apply** - Candidates can receive a link to your selected job postings by texting a code word to your ApplicantStack texting number.
- **Automate texts in Application and New Hire workflows** - Choose a text message template from your library and have it sent to candidates and new hires automatically as they move through the workflow. For example, when a candidate is moved to the *Phone Screen* stage, they can be sent a text requesting they schedule a time for the screening.

The monthly cost of Premium Texting is shown when upgrading your plan on the billing page.

The ApplicantStack API provides a way for developers to build easy, secure integrations between ApplicantStack and other systems, such as payroll systems or HRIS. The API is intended for your internal IT staff and trusted third-parties only. Your data is secured using a private API key.
This document is designed for developers building integrations to ApplicantStack.

The API uses a REST interface with JSON as the input and the output. The API can be accessed using GET commands to read data and PUT commands to update it.

### Authentication

You will need an access token and username to access the API. The access token is specific to each ApplicantStack customer. It can be found on the Settings --> Edit Settings. You will send the access token in the token parameter of the header.

```
“Token: mytoken”
```

Each access token may only be used in conjunction with its specific domain. Domain information is also available on the settings page. You will not send the domain information in a header. Instead, you will put the domain in the subdomain of the url.

```
MYDOMAIN.applicantstack.com
```

A Publisher name should be passed in as well. This helps the ApplicantStack customer to see who is making the changes to their account through the API. This should be the name of your software so that the customer will recognize it. The Publisher name is not configured anywhere, and you may use whatever you like. You will send the Publisher name through the Publisher parameter of the header.

```
“Publisher: MyName”
```

See the examples for more information.

### Candidate/Application Records

To access candidate records use the following URL. This will bring you 100 candidates, including their field data. This will not include a candidate’s cover letters or resumes. The total number of pages will also be returned.

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/api/candidates
```

To access more records continue to make the above call with the additional getpage parameter. You can get all candidate records by repeating this process through all of the pages.

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/api/candidates/2
```

You may also filter your results.

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/api/candidates?stage=hired
```

### Available Candidate Filters:

```
**stage** Receive only candidates that are at this stage
```

```
**score<** Receive only candidates who score less than a given amount, including knockouts
```

```
**score>** Receive only candidates who scored higher than the given amount
```

To access an individual candidate record you will need the candidate serial. This is returned as part of the candidates objects above. This will return all of the candidate fields including the cover letter and questionnaire answers. In the example below a45a0b8q3afc is this candidate’s serial number.

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/api/candidate/a45a0b8q3afc
```

### Job Records

You may access jobs in the same way you accessed candidates. This will bring you 100 jobs, including their field data. This will not include a job’s listing, questionnaires, or scoring rules. The total number of pages will also be returned.

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/api/jobs
```

A call to jobs will only return 100 results. If there are more than 100 jobs, you must call specific pages up to the total number of job pages available. Just like with candidate records, the number of jobs available will be returned with every call to jobs as NumPages:1

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/api/jobs/2
```

To get an individual job use the following. Note that a25a0b8ygups is the job serial number.

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/api/job/a25a0b8ygups
```

### Hire Records

If you subscribe to the Onboarding product you can use the api to access hires in a similar way to jobs and candidates. The URL below will bring you 100 hires, including their field data. This will not include a hire’s questionnaire or form data. The total number of pages will also be returned.

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/o/api/hires
```

A call to hires will only return 100 results. If there are more than 100 hires, you must call specific pages up to the total number of pages available. Just like with candidate and job records, the number of hires available will be returned with every call as NumPages:1

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/o/api/hires/2
```

To get an individual hire use the following URL. Note that e2g2xo659jvz is the hire serial number.

```
yourdomain.applicantstack.com/o/api/hire/e2g2xo659jvz

```

Note that the hire and hires method URLs include '/o/' in the path to designate that they use the onboarding product.

### Example

This is a sample candidates request using cURL

```
curl –H “Token: mytoken” https://mydomain.applicantstack.com/api/candidates
```

The following code is a working example that may be used to make a call to the API in PHP using cURL. This example is geared specifically to the candidates operation of the API. In order to get a single candidate you can set the operation to candidate and replace the code for setting the page number with code to insert the candidate serial number. The final variable $result is an object containing all of the returned data. Try var_dump($result); during development for a simple way to see the returned data.

```
function php_applicantstack_api(){
    $accesstoken = 'your_api_token';
    $publisher = 'ApplicantStack Jeff';

    $headers = array(
        "charset=\"utf-8\"",
        "Token: $accesstoken",
        "Publisher: $publisher "
    );
    $mydomain = "yourdomain";
    $action = 'GET';
    $operation = 'candidates';
    $pagenumber = '1';
    if($pagenumber){$operation .= '/'.$pagenumber;}

    $operationurl = "https://$mydomain.applicantstack.com/api/$operation";

    $curl = curl_init($operationurl);
    curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
    curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);

    $res = curl_exec($curl);

    if (curl_errno($curl)) {
        print "Error: " . curl_error($curl);
    }
    curl_close($curl);
    $result = json_decode($res);
}
```

## PUT Commands

PUT commands allow you to update job, candidate and hire fields through the API.

You will be passing in a JSON encoded string representing an array of fields to be changed. You only need to pass fields that you wish to change. In a PUT, the serial number may be passed in the URL in the same way it is when getting a job or candidate. Alternatively, you may pass it in with the fields to change with the key ‘serial.’

To update a field for a job, candidate or hire you will need to get the name of the field and the value you wish to set. If the field you are changing is a dropdown, the value may be set by name, and a warning will be returned if the option specified was not found, and therefore not set.

### Example

The sample PUT command below sends a new last name to the candidate specified by serial. Notice that the question marks are escaped. This is necessary to represent a json_encoded string properly. Also notice the publisher name, which will be noted in the candidates history.

```
curl –X PUT –H “Token: mytoken” –H “Publisher: yourname” –d {\”serial\”:\”a45a0b8ao86b\”,\”lastname\”:\”Smith\”} https://mydomain.applicantstack.com/api/candidate
```

The following PHP example expands the previous example to include optional puts. Notice the $requestarray.

```
function php_put_applicantstack_api(){
    $accesstoken = 'your_api_token';
    $publisher = 'ApplicantStack Jeff';

    $headers = array(
        "charset=\"utf-8\"",
        "Token: $accesstoken",
        "Publisher: $publisher"
    );
    $mydomain = "yourdomain";
    $action = 'PUT';
    $operation = 'candidate';

    $operationurl = "https://$mydomain.applicantstack.com/api/$operation";
    $curl = curl_init($operationurl);
    curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
    curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);
    if($action == 'PUT'){
        $requestarray = array(
            'serial'=>'a45a0b8x7wfk',
            'source'=>'Facebook',
        );
        $request = json_encode($requestarray);
        $requestlength = strlen($request);
        $fh = fopen('php://temp', 'r+');
        fwrite($fh, $request);
        rewind($fh);
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_PUT, 1);
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_INFILESIZE, $requestlength);
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_INFILE, $fh);
    }
    $res = curl_exec($curl);

    if (curl_errno($curl)) {
        print "Error: " . curl_error($curl);
    }
    curl_close($curl);
    if($action == 'PUT'){fclose($fh);}
    $result = json_decode($res);
}
```

## POST Commands

POST commands allow you to create new candidates or hires through the API. You will need to pass in a JSON encoded string representing an array of fields. When posting you will need to provide a value for all required fields for the object to be successfully created. If the field you are changing is a dropdown, the value may be set by name, and a warning will be returned if the option specified was not found, and therefore not set. Any fields set as required from the user interface will be required by the API. Any missing required fields will return an error message listing the fields that are missing.

When posting new candidates, you must also provide the "Job Serial" for the job you wish to attach the candidate to.

When posting new hires, you must also provide the "Manager" for the hire, which must match the full name of one of the users of your account.

### Example

The PHP sample below will post a new candidate into the account with all required fields set.

```
function php_post_applicantstack_api(){
    $accesstoken = 'your_api_token';
    $publisher = 'ApplicantStack Jeff';
    $headers = array(
        "charset=\"utf-8\"",
        "Token: $accesstoken",
        "Publisher: $publisher "
    );
    $mydomain = "yourdomain";
    $action = 'POST';
    $operation = 'candidate';
    $operationurl = "https://$mydomain.applicantstack.com/api/$operation";
    $curl = curl_init($operationurl);
    curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
    curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);
    if($action == 'POST'){
        $requestarray = array(
            'Job Serial'=>'a2k0xovpgg1e',
            'First Name'=>'Jeff',
            'Last Name'=>'Schaefer',
            'Address 1'=>'2500 Regency Pkwy',
            'City'=>'Cary',
            'State'=>'NC',
            'Zip'=>'27518',
            'Phone'=>'919-508-6155',
            'Email'=>'jeff.schaefer@applicantstack.com',
            'Source'=>'Facebook',
        );
        $requestdata = json_encode($requestarray);

        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POST, 1);
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $requestdata);
    }
    $res = curl_exec($curl);
    if (curl_errno($curl)) {
        print "Error: " . curl_error($curl);
    }
    curl_close($curl);
    $result = json_decode($res);
}
```

### Posting Files

You may also pass in a resume or other attachment to be added to the candidate. To do this you must put your fields inside of the key 'json', and the file under the key 'file'. In php we will use the realpath function to pass the file into the POST. The example below is a copy of the example above with the file added to it. Note the difference in the assignment of $requestdata. It is also important to note that the json_encode is within the 'json' key, since the 'file' is not meant to be encoded.

```
function php_post_file_applicantstack_api(){
    $accesstoken = 'your_api_token';
    $publisher = 'ApplicantStack Jeff';
    $headers = array(
        "charset=\"utf-8\"",
        "Token: $accesstoken",
        "Publisher: $publisher "
    );
    $mydomain = "yourdomain";
    $action = 'POST';
    $operation = 'candidate';
    $operationurl = "https://$mydomain.applicantstack.com/api/$operation";
    $curl = curl_init($operationurl);
    curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
    curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);
    if($action == 'POST'){
        $requestarray = array(
            'Job Serial'=>'a2k0xovpgg1e',
            'First Name'=>'Jeff',
            'Last Name'=>'Schaefer',
            'Address 1'=>'2500 Regency Pkwy',
            'City'=>'Cary',
            'State'=>'NC',
            'Zip'=>'27518',
            'Phone'=>'919-508-6155',
            'Email'=>'jeff.schaefer@applicantstack.com',
            'Source'=>'Facebook',
        );
        $requestdata = array(
            'json'=>json_encode($requestarray),
            'file'=>'@' . realpath('robots.txt'),
        );
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POST, 1);
        curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $requestdata);
    }
    $res = curl_exec($curl);
    if (curl_errno($curl)) {
        print "Error: " . curl_error($curl);
    }
    curl_close($curl);
    $result = json_decode($res);
}
```

## Responses

Once you send your request through cURL you will get a JSON encoded string response. Included in this response will be a ‘Method Result’ item that will display either success or failure. If the result is failure you should get an error item as well. If your request was a candidates or jobs GET then you will receive a list of up to 100 items in response. You will also get a numpages indicating how many pages may be accessed. If you try to reach a page out of range, the system will simply return no results. If you request a candidate or job GET you will receive more detailed information about the candidate or job requested. PUTs or POSTs will only respond with a Method Result and Errors or warnings as applicable.

### Sample Candidates Response

```
stdClass Object
(
    [Method Result] => Success
    [Page] => 1
    [NumPages] => 2
    [TotalCount] => 167
    [Candidates] => Array
        (
            [0] => stdClass Object
                (
                    [Candidate Serial] => a45a0b8x7wfk
                    [Job Serial] => a25a0b8ygups
                    [Job Name] => Account Manager [SAMP-1001]
                    [First Name] => Michael
                    [Last Name] => Turner
                    [Address 1] => 3128 Queensferry Lane (Sample)
                    [Address 2] =>
                    [State] => NC
                    [City] => Raleigh
                    [Zip] => 27616

## Stage Change Notifications

With the stage change notification mechanism you can develop real-time systems that work with your ApplicantStack data. For example, you could develop a method that looks for Hired candidates and then loads their information into your internal or third-party HRIS or Payroll system.

You can subscribe to stage change events by entering an endpoint URL in Setup->Settings. When you are subscribed to stage change events, the system will post to your endpoint each time a candidate or hire (in Onboarding) is moved to a new stage. The post will include the name of the new stage, the candidate or hire serial, the user who initiated the stage change (if applicable), and the date of the stage change.

If a user initiated the stage change, the "User Serial" field will contain the ID of the user and the "User Type" field will be "USER". If the stage change was initiated by the system, the "User Serial" field will be blank and the "User Type" field will be "SYSTEM".

For performance reasons, the stage change notification will only include summary information, not the full candidate or hire record. Typically when you receive the notification you would then use the candidate or hire serial to pull the full candidate or hire information from the system.

The stage change notification will contain a "secret" value that is unique for your ApplicantStack account. You can specify this secret in Setup->Settings or have the system generate it for you. The secret is sent with all notification posts so you know that they originated from ApplicantStack.

### Sample Stage Change Notification

```
stdClass Object
(
    [Object Type] => candidate
    [Event Type] => stagechange
    [Domain] => mycompany
    [Secret] => m58hqrje1xx5w4ku
    [Event Date] => 2016-09-08T15:58:13-04:00
    [Stage] => Interview
    [Candidate Serial] => a4g2xo6ji234
    [User Serial] => a1g2xo6xoezu
    [User Type] => USER
)

```

### Errors

**Request type error while fetching data** Indicates that there was a problem getting the GET or PUT data. This often occurs with PUTs when characters are not escaped properly.

**No Job/Candidate found with serial given** Indicates that the serial number you passed in did not match an object within the account.

**Job/Candidate does not belong to this account** Indicates that the serial number refers to a job that this account does not have access to.

**Error while writing job/candidate record** This is an internal error. Please contact ApplicantStack.

**Candidate job does not exist**

### Warnings

**Field with name NAME does not contain option OPTION.** The option that you passed in is not available for this field. Usually this is caused by a spelling error.

**Field with name NAME was not found.** The field you are trying to change does not exist. Check your spelling.

### Notes

In the php examples above we use json_decode($result) and we get a stdClass object. It is often preferable to use the optional second parameter json_decode($result,true) to get an associative array instead.

## Activate Texting for ApplicantStack

Candidates and new hires can be messaged via text in both ApplicantStack Recruit and ApplicantStack Onboard. With it, users can send SMS messages from the app using the small cell phone icon.

[Screenshot: Candidate tab mobile icon]

Texting icon on the Candidate tab

Texting services are provided by a third-party vendor that must approve each company requesting this feature. This process can take up to three weeks. This feature also incurs a monthly fee (which is shown when activating) and is only available to US customers.

If you already have texting activated for your company and are looking for instructions on how to *use* it, see the article [Texting Candidates and New Hires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Texting).

### Activate Texting

An Administrator can activate texting with the following steps:

1. Click your avatar in the upper right corner and select **Setup**.
2. Choose **Billing** from the setup menu on the left of the page.
3. In the card labeled *Current Texting Plan Details* , click **Get Texting**.
  [Screenshot: Get Texting button on the billing page]
4. Choose from the available texting plans. (See Texting Plans for more information.)
5. Fill in the *Carrier Compliance* fields with your company information. (For more on why this step is necessary and what fields are required, see the following topic titled *Carrier Compliance* .
  [Screenshot: Carrier Compliance form filled in]
6. Click **CONTINUE** once you’ve completed Carrier Compliance.
7. Review the user agreement and select **Agree & Activate**.

The request for a toll-free number is forwarded to our SMS provider and you will be emailed when the status of your request changes. The status is also reflected on the Settings page. Submission of the form is no guarantee of approval and approval can take up to three weeks.

#### Incoming Text Notifications

If you or any other users in ApplicantStack want to receive an email when a candidate or hire responds to a text, you can enable **Text Notifications**.

To enable Text Notifications:

1. Click your avatar in the upper right corner and select **Setup**.
2. Choose **Settings** from the setup menu on the left of the page.
  [Screenshot: Settings navigation]
3. Click **Edit Settings** on the right side of the page.
4. Under *Candidate Texting Settings* , set **Text Notifications** to “On”.
5. Click **Save**.

Individual users can now choose whether to enable or disable this notification through **My Account**, found under their avatar.

#### Texting Plans

There are two texting plan options:

- **Basic Texting** - Text individual candidates and hires (for ApplicantStack Onboard) through the Candidates tab. This includes the ability to add questionnaires and attachments to a text and create text templates in your message library.
- **Premium Texting** - All the features of *Basic Texting,* plus the ability to use text messages in application and hire workflows, as well as [Text to Apply](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Text-to-Apply) functionality.

### Carrier Compliance

A requirement for texting is to register your organization with the service providers and cell phone carriers. This requirement not only applies to accounts new to texting, but also those accounts that were using texting *prior* to the requirement. Filling in this compliance form is part of the setup.

In addition to your contact information and company address, you'll need to provide the following:

- Legal Business Name
- EIN
- Organization Website URL
- Business Type
- Business Industry

**Legal Business Name** has to be the legal company name associated with your EIN.

Administrators can go to **Setup ⇒ Settings** and view their compliance information under *Candidate/New Hire Texting Settings* .

As part of this compliance, anyone you text through ApplicantStack can opt-out of texting by replying with “STOP”. When a recipient opts-out of texting, and you or another manager tries to text them, you will be notified that the candidate has opted out of texting. The candidate can resume receiving text messages by texting "START" to the number.

## Add Onboarding Forms to Your ApplicantStack Library

ApplicantStack Onboarding offers you the capability to upload your own PDF forms. In order to upload your PDF forms, click the library tab, then forms on the left. On the right menu find the Add Form button.

[Embedded video: https://player.vimeo.com/video/661015554]

Once you click the **Add Form** button you will be presented with the *Add Form* screen. Enter the name of the form in the Form Name field. Next click **Choose File** to locate the form you wish to upload on your hard drive. When you are ready, click **Next**.

[Screenshot]

[Screenshot]

Now you are presented with the *Edit Form* screen. From this screen you can enter the following information:

- Name: You can change the name of the form
- Instructions: You can create instructions for your form
- Form Type: From this drop down you can select who should be able to fill out the form and the order that they should complete the form when you assign the form. Your options are:
  - Hire only: Only the Hire completes the form
  - Employer only: Only the employer completes the form
  - Hire, then employer: The hire completes their section first and then the employer will complete their section next
  - Employer, then hire: The employer completes their section first and then the hire will complete their section next
- Send Email Reminder: You can choose to send a reminder to complete the form to the assignees. The reminders will send until each assignees section has been completed. For example, if you selected Hire, then employer, a reminder is sent to the hire to complete the form. Once the hire completes their section, they no longer receive a reminder and then a reminder is sent to the employer to complete their section.

[Embedded video: https://player.vimeo.com/video/661015519]

[Screenshot]

You should notice a menu bar on the left side of your screen. This menu bar provides a variety of fields that you can add to your forms.

[Screenshot]

Simply click the field you want and then place it on the form. These fields are:

- Single-Line Text: Creates a text field that allows the assignee to enter text on a single line.
- Multi-Line Text: Creates a text field that allows for wrap around text and multiple lines.
- Signature: Creates a field that allows the assignee to enter a signature.
- Date: Creates a field with the date type and a date selector.
- Dropdown: Allows you to create a drop-down field that contains selectable options that you determine.
- Multiple Choice Fields: This allows you to create a radio button or multiple choice field. This is useful for fields that have Yes/No answers or answers that allow the user to select one out of X options. To create these type of fields, drag your first multiple choice field to the desired location. Next, drag your other multiple choice field to the desired location. You will need to double-click the second field and make sure that it is named the same as your first multiple choice field. For more information, see editing fields below.
- Checkbox: Allows the creation of a single click checkbox.
- Label: You can create a non-fillable label for your form.

Note that the form above has all the fields created. Our forms feature allows you to upload a pdf form with existing form fields into your Onboarding account. This is useful as you will not need to create the form fields using the tools above. Of course, if your form does not have existing form fields or you upload a scanned PDF, you can create the form fields that you need using the tools above.

To edit a form field, click the field and you will be presented with a summary dialog. Alternatively, you can double-click the field and open the edit field dialog box.

Clicking the delete button will remove the field. Clicking edit will open the following dialog box:

[Screenshot]

This box contains the following options:

- Name: Allows you to change the name of the field. Note this will change the name internally and not on the actual pdf. If the field is required and the assignee does not answer the question, the validation system will use this name to inform the assignee that the question is required. The name should be something that is informative and unique. For multiple choice fields, this field must be the same for each field option in the group.
- Type: Allows you to change the field type.
- Required: Check this box to indicate that the field is required.
- Validation: There are currently four options that the system uses:
  - Number: value must be numeric
  - Phone: value must be in the format of a phone number (###) ###-####
  - SSN: value must be in the format of a social security number ###-##-####
  - Email: value must in the format of an email address
- Comb: This allows you to set a numeric value for the amount of characters in a comb field.
  - For example, your social security field is formatted like the following image:
  - [Screenshot]
  - Notice that each field has vertical lines. In the first field, you will see 3 vertical lines. You would set the comb value to 3. This will limit the characters in the field to three and will space each character between the vertical lines. See below:
  - [Screenshot]
- Autofill: You can use this field to autofill the form field with text you enter or you can click Merge Codes and use dynamic text to populate the field with data contained in your Hire fields (like name, address, start date, pay rate, etc.).
- Tooltip: This option allows you to add a tooltip to your form field that will appear when the assignee clicks the field.
- Form Group: Use this option to assign a field to a particular group that you selected under Form Type above. You can assign the field to the hire or the employer.
- Position: This allows you to move the field on the page using the fields x and y values as well as change the height and width of the field. This is useful for precision placement that you are not able to achieve using the mouse.

Additional options are available for the following field types:

Multiple Choice:

- Value: For Multiple Choice fields, enter a unique value for the field. The value doesn't change what is displayed on the form and is only used for reports and autofill.

Dropdown:

- Options: For Dropdown fields, enter the options for the drop-down list, one per line

Label:

- Text: For Label fields, this will be the text that is displayed in the label on the form

When you are finished editing your form, click save.

b:
## Applicant Tracking Messaging and Notification FAQ

The following are some common question and answers related to emails, texts, and notifications in ApplicantStack.

### Email FAQ

Candidates are not receiving emails from our organization because they are going to their spam folders. Is there any way that I can stop this from happening?

ApplicantStack™ is not blacklisted by any ISPs. Technically, it is not possible for us to know if an email to a candidate went into their spam folder. We also cannot determine if they have whitelisted our emails. Spam filters do not provide feedback on what actions they take on an email. We recommend that you communicate on your application that applicants whitelist any emails that are sent from your organization and / or ApplicantStack™ and periodically check their spam folders.

I need to know how to send, for example, an automated "Application Received" response to candidates. Is that even possible?

Yes, create an email for this purpose under the Library tab (or select an existing email). Then, in your Application Workflow, set the email to trigger once the applicant enters the *New* stage.

I made a change to an applicant’s stage and I didn’t receive a notification of that stage change.

If you make a change to an applicant’s stage and are the Job Owner/Hiring Manager for that stage, you will not receive a notification as you were the one to make the change. If any other users are associated with the stage for that job/applicant, *they* will receive the notification. The notification will still be logged in the candidate’s history.

How do I shut off the notification emails that I get when a new candidate applies to the job?

Go to Setup and click Configure on the left. Select **Application Workflow Stages**. Select the **New** stage and click the edit icon. Uncheck "Notify" and click **Save**.

Can I use my email client to send/receive emails from ApplicantStack™?

We do not do anything proprietary with any email client, so you can use any email client to send and receive emails from ApplicantStack.

### Text FAQ

I am reading about options to text candidates, but I don't see that option in my account. What do I need in order to text candidates?

Texting is a feature that needs to be enabled. It is available for an additional monthly fee and has two tiers: Basic and Premium. The article [Activate Texting for ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack) has more on how administrators can enable it for their account.

Can I include attachments in a text message?

Yes, attachments and questionnaires can be added to text messages, but they are converted into a clickable link. Images, however, are not supported in texts.

Why are texts to my candidates being cut off or sent in the wrong order?

This may be due to character limits on the message. ApplicantStack's texting service *does* support messages greater than 160 characters, however, it is recommended to keep text messages brief. Wireless carriers and the devices themselves can handle longer messages differently, and a large texts may be broken into segments.

Why are candidates not receiving messages.

Make sure they haven't opted out of messaging. All recipients of a text from ApplicantStack can halt messages by texting "STOP" to your ApplicantStack texting number. If they want to restart this service, they simply text "START". Also, you can see whether they have stopped or started text messaging by checking the text thread in ApplicantStck.

Is there a way I can be notified when ApplicantStack receives a text message?

Yes, you can receive an email that your ApplicantStack account received a text message. Your Company Settings page has a **Text Notifications** option that must be turned on. Then, individuals within your company can then enable email notifications for themselves in *My Account* .

Can texts be delayed

No, unlike emails, you cannot set a delay on text messages.

## Create an Anonymous Job Post

Many of our customers have posted blind job ads by creating a brand new ApplicantStack account just for their blind posting. Since there is no contract and you can pay monthly, you can just keep the account open for the month or two needed to collect your applicants and then close the account without any other fees.

Note, most job boards such as Indeed will require you to sponsor the job posting. Please contact your Indeed (or other job board distributor) for more information. - **Create Candidate** - Manually create a new candidate in the system. See Create Candidate later in this article for more on the process.
- **Upload Resume(s)** - Upload resume files directly from your hard drive for the selected job.
- **Upload Emails** - Upload resume files by emailing them to the system for the selected job. This function opens a new message in your email client.

- **Search -** Search all candidates in the system based on a variety of criteria.
- **Run Report -** Generate reports on the applicants per month, EEOC Summary, or Active Candidate Details. For more information see [Reports Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Reports-Tab).
- **Export -** Export selected candidates to a csv file; includes any attachments associated with the candidate(s).
- **Email Candidate** - Send selected candidates an email; can create an original email or use one of your company's templates.
- **Text Candidate** - Send selected candidates an text; can create an original text or use one of your company's templates. *Requires a Basic Texting plan.*
- **Create Task** and **Schedule Event -** Takes you to each item's respective tab where you assign tasks to internal users or create events, such as holding an interview or candidate review. #### Candidate Table Filters

There are a variety of filters to choose from, which will enable you to customize your Candidate Listing Grid to suit your organization’s needs. Those filters are accessible by selecting the "Expand Filters" and are as follows:

- **Job**
  - **My Active Jobs** – Only candidates for My Active Jobs (i.e. jobs where the current user is a Job Owner or Hiring Manager).
  - **All Jobs** - Available to Administrators and Recruiters.
  - ***Select a job*** – Only show candidates that are linked to a specific job.
- **Candidate**
  - **Active Candidate -** Show only candidates in an active stage, like New, Manager Review, etc.
  - **All Candidate Stages** – Show candidates in any candidate stage, including those set to *Do Not Pursue* or *Withdrawn* .
  - Inactive Candidates – Showing only candidates in an inactive stage like *Do Not Pursue, Withdrawn* , etc.
  - ***Select a stage*** – Show all candidates in the selected Stage.
- **Scores**
  - **All Scores** – All candidates regardless of score.
  - **KO or Not KO** – Based on whether the candidate received a *knockout* score.
  - **N/A or Not N/A** – Based on whether the candidate has a score (Not N/A) or not (N/A).
- **Source** - Filters the candidates based on how they applied for the job; includes each third-party job board you use and, if enabled, text-to-apply.
- **Rating** – Filters on the *Rating* field which is filled out by Job Owners and/or Hiring Manager when moving the candidate through the Application Workflow.
- **Disposition** – Filters on the selected disposition.

You can also filter by any single-select custom application fields you have added to your account.

## Candidates

When a candidate submits an on-line application through your ApplicantStack™ system, a variety of information is collected in the form of contact and demographic data as well as data that helps you process your applications internally. Not only do the applications collect data at the time of submission, they can also be configured to collect data during the hiring process in the form of scores entered by managers, manager reviews, and other internal data collection. This information is collected by **Candidate** and **Application Fields**. This information is different than the information that is submitted by attached questionnaires like employment applications. Unlike questionnaires, candidate and application fields can be used by the system to help you filter candidates as well as guide you through your hiring process.

The **Candidate Fields** are available for all candidates and are asked for whenever a candidate is created. They are used to collect a candidate’s contact and demographic information, such as phone number, cell phone number, country, etc. The **Application Fields** are available for every application in the system and are prompted for whenever a candidate applies for a job. They are used to categorize information internally, such as the source of the application (Monster, CareerBuilder, Your Public Job Board, etc), was the applicant referred by someone, or maybe store additional internal information about an application including Rating, Reviewing Manager, Manager Score, etc.

This guide will show you how to add, modify, and remove **Candidate Fields**, **Application Fields** and **Application Workflow Stages**. We will also cover how to associate actions with **Application Workflow Stages**.

## Configure the *Application Workflow*

The Application Workflow is the framework that manages candidates for your jobs in ApplicantStack Recruit. A basic version of this workflow comes with every ApplicantStack account and facilitates the evaluation of candidates. This article instructs you on modifying a workflow and creating additional workflows.

*NOTE:* Not all accounts have the option for multiple workflows.

[Screenshot: the steps in this article apply to Administrators]

Any user with the Administrator role can modify and add workflows through the account configuration page. This page is accessed from the Home page through the click-path: **Update Settings** **⇒ Configure**.

[Screenshot: click path to the configuration page]

The account configuration page can also be accessed from *any* page in ApplicantStack through your avatar menu. Click your image/icon in the upper right of the page and select **Setup ⇒ Configure.**

Once you are on the **Configure Account** page, select **Application Workflow** to see the workflows available for the application process. There will likely only be one workflow listed, the *Default Application Workflow* . Each workflow has a pencil icon to modify what occurs at each stage in the process. There are also options to duplicate and delete a workflow.

[Screenshot: Application Workflows page with a single workflow]

To create a new workflow, select **Create Workflow** from the action menu on the right (shown below) and name the workflow.

[Screenshot: option in the right-side menu to create a new workflow]

### *Status* and *Default*

Each workflow has a dropdown for *Status* , which can be either **Draft** or **Active**. **Draft** allows you to edit a workflow without making it available to current jobs.

The **Set as Default** button automatically selects that workflow for every new job. When a job requisition is set up, the Hiring Manager cannot change the workflow, but the Recruiter may change it later when approving the job.

*NOTE:* If the workflow is currently set as your default, you cannot set it to draft until you set a different workflow as the default

### Workflow Stages

Each workflow is made up of stages, and when you select a workflow to edit, a summary of the steps in each stage are visible. The **Expand All** and **Collapse All** options at the top of the page allow you to expand or collapse all the stage panels in the workflow. The application workflow that comes with your account should already have stages within it. Configuring what happens *within* each stage is done by editing the stage with the **Edit Workflow Stage** button. That's how to define what managers and candidates do as candidates move through the workflow.

[Screenshot: workflow settings at the top of the page]

Can I Add Stages?

Yes, new stages are created on the *Application Stages* page, which you can access with the button near the top of the page. Once you have done that, return to the workflow and select the green **Add New Stage to Workflow** button to choose the new stage and select which stage it follows.

When editing a stage, the following items can be configured. Once you have made changes to any stages, select **Submit** to save the changes.

#### Message Settings

Use the message settings to send an email or text* message to the candidate when they move to a new stage. When editing the stage, select the plus "+" button under Message Settings to select a message template from your library.

[Screenshot: Message Settings]

Templates with an email and text version send *both* messages to the candidate. If you want to restrict the message to a single format (email-only or text-only), then you need to edit the template and remove the version you don't want sent—there is no way to select one or the other when configuring the workflow stage.

Once you add a message, **Triggering Stage** sets the conditions for sending the message. You can choose to send the message regardless of what stage the candidate is advancing from (Any Stage) or specify that the message is only sent when advancing from a particular stage.

A stage can include multiple messages, and messages are removed from the stage with the trash can icon. If you select multiple templates for a single stage, the order in which the templates appear determines which message is sent first.

**NOTE:* Text messaging in workflows requires an [upgrade to Premium Texting](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Upgrade-to-Premium-Texting).

Can I Edit a Message Template from the Workflow page?

Yes, from the workflow overview, any messages included with a stage can be previewed by hovering over **View Message**. The preview also includes a pencil icon which allows you to edit the message template itself.

#### Task Settings

Tasks, such as an evaluation questionnaire to be completed by a Hiring Manager, can be associated with a stage. Tasks are created and stored in your library. If there is nothing to select in this section of the workflow configuration, then you do not have any tasks available in your library. More on creating tasks can be found in the article [Library - Tasks Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Tasks-Templates).

When you select a task template from the list, the task is assigned to the user specified in the template. This happens as soon as candidates reach this stage.

#### Event Settings

To request a user schedule an event associated with the stage, select an event template in the *Event Settings* section. Events are created and stored in your library. If there is nothing to select in this section of the workflow configuration, then you do not have any tasks available in your library. More on creating events can be found in the article [Library - Events Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Events-Templates).

When you select an event template from the list, the event scheduling is assigned to the user specified in the template. This happens as soon as candidates reach this stage.

#### User Settings

Select which user group (*Job Owner* or *Hiring Manager* ), or *individual* user owns the stage, as well as whether they receive a notification when a candidate enters the stage.

If you have five or more users in your company, the user selection list changes from a checkbox list to a search field. You can start typing the name of the user in this field and select them from a list that populates with all users matching your criteria.

The Job Owners and Hiring Manager groups are set at the job level. More on the Job Owner and Hiring Manager groups can be found in the article [Jobs Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Jobs-Tab).

#### Field Settings

Select **Show** for any fields that you want a user to fill in when they move a candidate to this stage. You can also choose to make completion of these fields required.

If you have five or more fields, the field selection list changes from a checkbox list to a search field. You can start typing the name of the field and select it from a list that populates with all fields matching your criteria.

Can I Create Fields?

Yes, the fields shown in this section are created by selecting **Application Fields** near the top of the page.

### Stage Order and Deleting Stages

Select the three horizontal lines at the right of each stage to click-and-drag a stage to a new spot in the workflow.

[Screenshot: reordering stages]

## Configure the *Hire Workflow* in ApplicantStack

The Hire Workflow is the framework that onboards new hires in ApplicantStack Onboard. A basic version of this workflow comes with every ApplicantStack account and facilitates the paperwork process and other orientation tasks. This article instructs you on modifying a workflow and creating additional workflows for different job types.

[Screenshot: this article is intended for administrators]

Any user with the Administrator role can modify and add workflows through the account configuration page. This page is accessed from the Home page through the click-path: **Update Settings** **⇒ Configure**.

[Screenshot]

The account configuration page can also be accessed from *any* page in ApplicantStack through your avatar menu. Click your image/icon in the upper right of the page and select **Setup ⇒ Configure.**

Once you are on the **Configure Account** page, select **Hire Workflow** to see the workflows available for the new hire process. There will likely only be one workflow listed, the *Default Hire Workflow* . Each workflow has a pencil icon to modify what occurs at each stage in the process. There are also options to duplicate and delete a workflow.

[Screenshot: the basic, default workflow on the Hire Workflows page]

To create a new workflow, select **Create Workflow** from the action menu on the right (shown below) and name the workflow.

[Screenshot: create a new workflow from the right-side menu]

### *Status* and *Default*

Each workflow has a dropdown for *Status* , which can be either **Draft** or **Active**. **Draft** allows you to edit a workflow without making it available for onboarding.

The **Set as Default** button automatically selects that workflow for every new hire.

*NOTE:* If the workflow is currently set as your default, you cannot set it to draft until you set a different workflow as the default

### Workflow Stages

Each workflow is made up of stages, and when you select a workflow to edit, a summary of the steps in each stage are visible. The **Expand All** and **Collapse All** options at the top of the page allow you to expand or collapse all the stage panels in the workflow. The hire workflow that comes with your account should already have stages within it. Configuring what happens *within* each stage is done by editing the stage with the **Edit Workflow Stage** button. That's how to define what managers and employees do as a new hire moves through the workflow.

[Screenshot: workflow settings at the top of the page]

Can I Add Stages?

Yes, new stages are created on the *Hire Stages* page, which you can access with the button near the top of the page. Once you have done that, return to the workflow and select the green **Add New Stage to Workflow** button to choose the new stage and select which stage it follows.

When editing a stage, the following functions can be configured. Once you have made changes to any stages, select **Submit** to save the changes.

#### Message Settings

Use the message settings to send an email or text* message to the hire when they move to a new stage. When editing the stage, select the plus "+" button under Message Settings to select a message template from your library.

[Screenshot: Message Settings]

Templates with an email and text version send *both* messages to the new hire. If you want to restrict the message to a single format (email only or text only), then you need to edit the template and remove the version you don't want sent—there is no way to select one or the other when configuring the workflow stage.

Once you add a message, **Triggering Stage** sets the conditions for sending the message. You can choose to send the message regardless of what stage the hire is advancing from (Any Stage), or specify that the message is only sent when advancing from a particular stage.

A stage can include multiple messages, and messages are removed from the stage with the trash can icon. If you select multiple templates for a single stage, the order in which the templates appear determines which message is sent first.

**NOTE:* Text messaging in workflows requires and [upgrade to Premium Texting](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Upgrade-to-Premium-Texting).

Can I Edit a Message Template from the Workflow page?

Yes, from the workflow overview, any messages included with a stage can be previewed by hovering over **View Message**. The preview also includes a pencil icon which allows you to edit the message template itself.

#### Checklist Settings

A checklist is a collection of assigned tasks and forms which is added to a stage in the workflow. Checklists, in addition to tasks and forms, are created and stored in your library. If there is nothing to select in this section of the workflow configuration, then you do not have any checklists available in your library. More on creating checklists can be found in the article [Library Tab in ApplicantStack Onboard](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Tab-in-ApplicantStack-Onboard).

#### User Settings

Select which user group or *individual* user owns the stage, as well as whether they receive a notification when a hire enters the stage.

If you have five or more users in your company, the user selection list changes from a checkbox list to a search field. You can start typing the name of the user in this field and select them from a list that populates with all users matching your criteria.

#### Field Settings

Select **Show** for any fields that you want a user to fill in when they move a hire to this stage. You can also choose to make completion of these fields required.

If you have five or more fields, the field selection list changes from a checkbox list to a search field. You can start typing the name of the field and select it from a list that populates with all fields matching your criteria.

Can I Create Fields?

Yes, the fields shown in this section are created by selecting **Hire Fields** near the top of the page.

#### Action Buttons

Action Buttons appear on a hire's record and move them to different stages in the onboarding process.

[Screenshot: action buttons on the employee record]

When configuring the workflow, choose one or more action buttons to appear at this stage. The dropdown contains existing buttons, as well as the option to create a new button. Once you select a button, associate it with one of the stages in the workflow, as shown in the image below.

[Screenshot: selecting action buttons]

You can have multiple buttons for a single stage, and the order of these buttons can be changed with the arrow buttons.

### Stage Order and Deleting Stages

Select the three horizontal lines at the right of each stage to click-and-drag a stage to a new spot in the workflow.

[Screenshot: reordering stages]

You also have the ability to remove any non-system workflow stages by selecting the trash can. This does not delete the stage but just removes it from this workflow.

Rename a workflow with the pencil icon near the name.

[Screenshot: renaming option on a worklow]

If your **Add Stage to Workflow** button has an overlay of a number in a yellow circle, it means that you have stages that are not in the current workflow. This may be intentional, but clicking the button produces a drop down listing the available stages. You can also create a new stage from this dropdown. See below:

You can create a **Layout Template**, for a Questionnaire, to customize the way the questions in the questionnaire are displayed. A Layout Template is optional. If you don't create a layout template, the questionnaire will be displayed in the standard way, i.e. one question after another, vertically. Specifying a Layout Template can be a good way to make a questionnaire easier for your users to answer, as well as align to your company's forms. > Creating a Layout Template is an advanced task, that requires a knowledge of HTML. If you would like us to create a layout template for one of your questionnaires, please contact us for a quote. ### Example Consider the following questions, created in the standard way, using the questionnaire builder and displayed using the default layout (i.e. no Layout Template). [Screenshot] Now consider the same questionnaire with a custom Layout Template applied. [Screenshot] ### Technical Details A Layout Template is nothing more than HTML code, that specifies the layout of the questions in the questionnaire. In the Layout Template you use special codes to indicate where the questions should appear in the layout. The following codes are available: | CODE | DESCRIPTION | | --- | --- | | {QT} | Insert the Text of the next question in the questionnaire. | | {QI} | Insert the Input of the next question in the questionnaire, using the standard display settings. Answer options will be displayed horizontally. | | {QI width:40} | Insert the Input of the next question in the questionnaire, with a width of 40 characters (applies to Text questions). | | {QI layout:vertical} | Insert the Input of the next question in the questionnaire, and show the Answer Options vertically (applies to Yes/No, Select Many and Multiple Choice questions). | | {QI layout:dropdown} | Insert the Input of the next question in the questionnaire, and show the Answer Options in a drop-down menu (applies to Yes/No, Select Many and Multiple Choice questions). | | {QI layout:listbox} | Insert the Input of the next question in the questionnaire, and show the Answer Options in a listbox (applies to Yes/No, Select Many and Multiple Choice questions). | ### Sample Layout Template The following is a sample layout template, which corresponds to the layout in the example above. ```
PERSONAL INFORMATION
{QT}:{QI}
{QT}:{QI}
{QT}:{QI width:40}

REFERENCES List three references (not relatives or former employers)

Name Relationship Phone Number
{QI width:20} {QI width:20} {QI width:20}
{QI width:20} {QI width:20} {QI width:20}
```

## Deactivate Texting for ApplicantStack

If you want to deactivate ApplicantStack’s texting feature, you can do so through the *Billing* section of your account’s Setup page. Only users with the Administrator role can deactivate texting.

As diligent as ApplicantStack is in ensuring that all emails being sent to and from the candidates are delivered, there are times when emails might go to the spam/junk folder. Since spam filters are set at the email client level, we do not control what gets designated as spam.

One option to ensure that emails are being received from your end is to white-list any emails coming from "ApplicantStack.com". You might need to contact your email administrator to set this rule up.

We have also discovered that some email clients automatically designate certain keywords as spam. These words can be "Job Offer, Employment, Earn Money..."

Here are some articles that might be beneficial to avoiding these issues:

- [CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business](https://www.ftc.gov/tips-advice/business-center/guidance/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business)
- [Gmail Bulk Sender Guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126)

Unfortunately, there is no complete list of spam trigger words. You can search the Internet, but here is a list of some common trigger words:

- [HubSpot List of Common SPAM Trigger Words](https://blog.hubspot.com/blog/tabid/6307/bid/30684/The-Ultimate-List-of-Email-SPAM-Trigger-Words.aspx#sm.001y3ek80154deu5qd921f7gcgg9p)

We have a bounce back setting on our email server, and while we monitor the list for false positives, if you feel you are not receiving emails please create a ticket.

## Emails Tab

The **Emails tab** in ApplicantStack Recruit contains all the mail that you have sent and received through ApplicantStack™. It has a variety of filters which can be applied, and you can mark your messages as "read" and "unread".

[Screenshot: Email messages listed on the Emails tab]

The the following filters are available by selecting **Expand Filters**:

- **Jobs** - Show emails associated with a specific to a job opening.
- **Recipient Types** - Show only messages sent to either candidates or internal users.
- **Read Status** - Filter and show those that are **Read** or **Unread**.
- **Receipt Status** - Show those that are **Received** or **Sent**.
- **Dates** - Narrow the volume of emails to those from the last three months.

To change the status of an email to Read or Unread, select the messages with the checkboxes and use the corresponding buttons in the right-side menu. You can set the Read status using the buttons in the Actions column. The open envelope corresponds to Read and the closed envelope corresponds to Unread.

To view the details of an email, select the open folder icon in the Actions column. Alternatively you can click the **[View Details]** link in the message column as illustrated below:

[Screenshot: View message details with the open folder icon or view details link]

The details of the email includes the text from the original email, any included attachments and questionnaires, as well as any subsequent replies. You are also able respond to emails from this screen by entering the text in the provided text box. You can also attach files to the email. When finished, click **Send** and the reply is sent. The screen then refreshes and your reply will now be the last message on the screen.

For more information about emailing, see the article [Candidates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Candidates).

### Viewing Messages in an Email Client

You can receive email responses from the candidate in your email client so that you don't have to log into ApplicantStack. When viewing these messages, there are links that take you back into ApplicantStack where you can view more details on the candidate and respond to the email.

[Screenshot: An ApplicantStack email shown in an external email client with a link to the candidate's page called out]

The link to access ApplicantStack, like the one indicated in the image above, appears if the email was originally sent to the candidate from a **User**, not the *System* . Also, if the email also contains a *reply back* link, you can click that to be taken into ApplicantStack where you see the following screen:

[Screenshot: email response pages in ApplicantStack]

On this screen, you can reply back to the candidate, view the full email history, and also have access to any attached questionnaires and attachments. You'll also be able to attach files to the reply, view the candidate’s details, and download their resume. The candidate, however, only sees the original email correspondence and not their candidate record.

You can also reply directly to the email through your email client without using the *reply back* links.

If the email was sent from **System**, as opposed to *User* , it will not contain a *reply back* link. You also cannot attach questionnaires to an email sent using **System**, but you can attach files.

[Screenshot: files attached to an email]

Note About Attachments

Attachments are an effective way to send and request documents when managing applicants. When a candidate attaches a document to an email it is saved to the candidate record under Attachments and accessible as part of the candidate’s Summary.
