## Event Scheduling

*Job* and *Candidate* Events have scheduling options which assist in coordinating meeting times with all involved parties. When creating an Event, select **Check Available Times** under the *Event Date* field to see what works best for all assigned users.

[Screenshot: Link on scheduling portion of Event page that says Check available times]

The resulting pop-up shows the availability of each user and lets you pick a date an time.

[Screenshot: A user's schedule availability grid]

This availability calendar checks the user’s *Availability Settings* (details later in this article) and also accounts for any ApplicantStack Events that have already been scheduled. The availability calendar can also check a synced calendar from [Office 365](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Office-365-Calendar-Integration) or [Google Calendar](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Google-Calendar-Integration).

### Invite the Candidate to Schedule a Time

Candidate Events include an option to let the *candidate* select a date and time. This is done through the *Schedule Type* dropdown when creating the event.

[Screenshot: The option on the candidate event creation screen to let the candidate pick a time]

Choosing **Invite candidate to select a time**, changes the scheduling options, and you’ll select a meeting **Duration** and the **First Available Date** on which the candidate can schedule. Once the Event is saved, ApplicantStack sends an email requesting the candidate choose a date and time for the event. This is done through a link to your company’s job board where they can browse dates and select an available time according to your availability.

[Screenshot: The page where candidates can select times and dates for an event]

The *User Availability Length* setting in *My Account* determines how far into the future the candidate can pick a date. For example, if your Availability Length is set to “2 weeks”, then the candidate only has two weeks from the first available date from which to choose.

Once the candidate selects a time, you’ll get both an email notification and an update on your Home page’s Events tab. Also, if your *Availability Settings* in My Account have **Approve Candidate Proposed Times** set to “Yes”, then that email instructs you to approve date and time. Once approved, a you are given an option to send a confirmation back to the candidate.

### Set Your *Event User Availability Settings*

Event scheduling uses preferences that you define in *My Account* . To set or adjust these settings, select your avatar menu in the upper right corner and choose **My Account**. There, your current settings are visible under *Event User Availability Settings* .

[Screenshot: Account Settings with the User Availability section called out]

To change these settings, select **Edit Account** from the right side menu.

- **User Availability Hours Start** and **End** are the times you’re available—typically your work-day hours.
- **Availability Length** defines how long of a date range a user or candidate can view your availability.
- **Include Weekends** lets you choose if users or candidates can choose Saturday or Sunday.
- **Approve Candidate Proposed Times** applies to instances where you allow a candidate to select a date and time for an event. When set to “Yes”, once a candidate schedules the event, you’ll have a chance to review and approve the date and time.

## Events Tab

An *Event* in ApplicantStack Recruit schedules meetings which are associated with either a Job or Candidate. For example, users from your company can be invited to an Event regarding the creation of a job posting or evaluation of a candidate. Events can also be used to schedule a candidate interview or recruitment event.

Some example Events include:

- Job Review Meeting
- Job Kickoff Meeting
- Job Fair
- Interviews
- Candidate Selection Meeting

An additional feature of an Event is the collection of *User Feedback* . That’s where users assigned to the Event are required to provide comments or related input. For example, a Hiring Manager can be asked to complete a post-interview questionnaire.

This article shows you how to create and manage events for both the *Job* and *Candidate* objects, as well as how users submit feedback.

### Schedule a Job Event

Each Job has an **Events** tab where you can view any existing Events or schedule a new one with the dedicated button. There’s also a **Schedule Event** option in the right-side contextual menu.

[Screenshot: Events tab on a job with the Schedule Event options called out]

You can schedule an Event on a Job's Events tab.

Once you select **Schedule Event**, the following page asks for some basic information:

- Assigned To
- Event Name
- Event Description
- Internal Note
- Event Location

The **Assigned To** field could be yourself or any other ApplicantStack user. Assign multiple users to an Event with **Add Row**.

[Screenshot: Schedule event screen filled in with Add Row called out]

Multiple users are assigned to an Event with Add Row.

**Event Location** is optional, but any location you add is stored and can be retrieved in the future through the dropdown.

In the *Scheduling* section, set the date, start, and end time for the Event. Use **Check Available Times** to review the availability calendar of the assigned users and choose a time that works best for all involved.

*NOTE:* The availability calendar is explained in further detail in the article [Event Scheduling](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Event-Scheduling).

The *User Feedback* section is where you can require assigned users to submit feedback once the Event is over. This can include a questionnaire from the Library and an email reminder sent to the user at selected intervals.

Once you click **Save**, the Event is added, and assigned users are notified via email. They’ll also see it in the Events tab on their Home page.

Use a template for frequent events.

Instead of repeatedly creating an event for every job, create an Event *template* . They are built on the *Library* tab in the same manner described here. Then, you can select the template when scheduling the Event. Event templates can also be added to your Job Workflow if you want them to be a standard part of the job posting process. Learn more in the articles [Library - Events Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Events-Templates) and [Configure - Job Workflow](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Job-Workflow).

### Schedule a Candidate Event

Each Candidate record has an **Events** tab where you can view any existing Events or schedule a new one with the dedicated button. There’s also a **Schedule Event** option in the right-side contextual menu.

[Screenshot: Events tab on a candidate with the Schedule Event options called out]

You can schedule an Event on a Candidate's Events tab.

Once you select **Schedule Event**, the following page asks for some basic information:

- Assigned To
- Event Name
- Event Description
- Internal Note
- Event Location

The **Assigned To** field could be yourself or any other ApplicantStack user. Assign multiple users to an Event with **Add Row**.

**Event Location** is optional, but any location you add is stored and can be retrieved in the future through the dropdown.

In the *Scheduling* section, the **Schedule Type** dropdown has two options: **Select a time** and **Invite candidate to select a time.**

[Screenshot: Schedule Type Options dropdown]

The Schedule Type on a Candidate Event has an option for letting the candidate select a time.

**Select a time** is when you are choosing the date and time for the Event. Use **Check Available Times** to review the availability calendar of the assigned users and choose a time that works best for all involved.

[Screenshot: Check available times link on the Event setup page]

An assigned user's availability can be checked when scheduling an Event.

**Invite candidate to select a time** is where the *candidate* selects a time. With this option, you choose a *Duration* and *First Available Date* , then the candidate is sent an email with a link where they can select a date and time.

[Screenshot: Page where a candidate can select the time for an event]

Candidates are emailed a link where they can select the date and time for an Event.

*NOTE:* Both the availability calendar and candidate scheduling option are explained in further detail in the article [Event Scheduling](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Event-Scheduling).

The *User Feedback* section is where you can require assigned users to submit feedback once the Event is over. This can include a questionnaire from the Library and an email reminder sent to the user at selected intervals.

Once you click **Save**, the Event is added, and assigned users are notified via email. They’ll also see it in the Events tab on their Home page.

Use a template for frequent events.

Instead of repeatedly creating an event for every candidate, create an Event *template* . They are built on the *Library* tab in the same manner described here. Then, you can select the template when scheduling the Event. Event templates can also be added to your Application Workflow if you want them to be a standard part of the candidate review process. Learn more in the articles [Library - Events Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Events-Templates) and [Configure the Application Workflow](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Workflow).

### View an Event and Submit Feedback

Each Job and Candidate in ApplicantStack has an Events tab where you can view and edit any scheduled Events associated with that instance. Events are also visible on the main *Events* tab found in the navigation tabs at the top of every page.

[Screenshot: Events tab with two interview events displayed]

All Events are displayed on the main Events tab.

If you aren’t seeing an Event in this view, check your filters at the top of the page. The Event list can be filtered by the Job as well as the assigned user. Adjust the filters with the **Expand Filters** button.

[Screenshot: Event filters expanded on the Events tab]

The Event list can be filtered.

The Events filter also has an *Upcoming* filter which hides any Events in the past. The filter typically only displays events within 6 months of the current date, but if you want to view an Event outside of that range, change the filter to *more than 6 months* .

The Event tab has an *Actions* column with icon buttons to *View Details, Edit* and *Delete* . You can also click the *Name, Job* and *Candidate* links to view the details for each respective item. Candidate Event details also include the candidate’s resume.

If you change the Event’s date or time, ApplicantStack sends the assigned user an email notification with the updated appointment and add it to the user’s calendar.

Upcoming events are also visible on the Home page.

The *Home* page/tab of ApplicantStack includes a tile in the notification section with two tabs: **Tasks** and **Events**. Selecting the Events tab shows your upcoming assigned events.

[Screenshot: Upcoming Event tab on the Home Page]

Your upcoming Events are visible right on the Home page.

#### Event Feedback

User feedback can be assigned as a Task associated with the Event. This could be in the form of a *Comments* field (where the assigned user makes a simple text entry), or by having the user fill out a questionnaire from your Library. These items are all set up under the *User Feedback* section of the *Schedule Event* page.

[Screenshot: User feedback section on the Event Creation tab]

User feedback is enabled when setting up the Event. It can use a questionnaire and have an email reminder.

Once the event date has passed, email reminders are sent according to the schedule in the Event setup. These emails include a link which the assigned user can use to submit the feedback. Users can also complete the assigned feedback through the *Tasks* tab on their Home page notification tile.

[Screenshot: Task tab on the Home page with Event feedback called out]

Once an Event is complete, assigned users can find the feedback tasks on their Home page.

Completing feedback for an Event is technically a Task—it is not visible in the Event details.

[Screenshot: The feedback field on a task associated with a Candidate Event]

The feedback comments are entered as a Task associated with the Event.

Once the feedback is complete, the Task is removed from the Home page and the user who created the Event is notified it has been completed. All feedback can then be viewed on the object’s Tasks tab.

Any emails that were sent related to the feedback task are visible by selecting **View Emails** from the right-side contextual menu.

t: Fix Repeated Prompts to Reset Password in Applicant Tracking
b:
When users have experienced this in the past, it's typically localized to the specific browser- so the best way to address this is to complete the steps below:

1. Log out of ApplicantStack

2. Clear your browser's cache and cookies

You can view instructions for different browsers below:

- Chrome: [https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?hl=en](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050)
- Firefox: [https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-clear-firefox-cache](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-clear-firefox-cache)
- Internet Explorer: [https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/products/internet-explorer](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-clear-firefox-cache)
- Safari: [https://support.apple.com/kb/PH21411?viewlocale=en_US&locale=en_US](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-clear-firefox-cache)
- Opera: [http://help.opera.com/opera/Mac/2393/en/private.html#deleteData](http://help.opera.com/opera/Mac/2393/en/private.html#deleteData)

3. Reset your password one last time.

4. Log in

This should help to alleviate the login issues you are experiencing. If the above steps do not resolve the issue, please feel free to reach out to us via the support portal.

For more information on passwords see the following article:

[Reset Your Password in Applicant Tracking](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Reset-Your-ApplicantStack-Password)

## FAQ: Candidates

Why can't I see my candidates that are in Do Not Pursue stage (or any inactive stage)?

The default setting for the Candidate's tab is to show only the active candidates for your active jobs. You can change this by using the filters at the top of the page.

Is there a way for application readers/reviewers to go back and alter their scores and/or comments once they have submitted them?

If you go under the **Feedback Tab** under Candidates, you will see all the submitted Questionnaires. Go to the **Candidates Tab**, then click on **Application Submitted** under the column Stage for the candidate you want to change the Questionnaires. Click the **Feedback Tab**. Scroll down to find your Questionnaire then click the edit icon on the Questionnaire (it will be located on the right of the box beside the x). It will take you to the completed Questionnaire and allow you to change your answers and resubmit the Questionnaire.

Sometimes we have a need to apply a stage, send an email, or delete a group of candidates. Is there any other way to capture these groups short of clicking each individual box next to each name?

Selecting them individually by checkbox is the only method that is available. You can also apply a filter by using the filters at the top of the page to narrow your selection and then select them all by using the checkbox located in the top left corner of the Candidates Grid or select each candidate individually.

Is it possible to re-arrange the order in which the columns appear under the Candidates Tab?

Currently we do not offer a way to rearrange the columns in ApplicantStack™.

Is there a way to point to a help file of my creation to help my Recruiter’s when they are creating job fields?

Yes. You can upload the help file to a web server and in the description field for the candidate field, you can insert a hyperlink to the help file.

I had an applicant apply for one position but then want to apply for a different one as well. Is there any way they are able to create an account that keeps their information so they won’t have to keep filling out the same information?

There are two ways of accomplishing this. You can turn on the logins on the job board which will require every applicant to create an account. You can find this under settings and then click the Job Board button on the left hand side of the screen. For more information about this feature see [Configuration Guide: Job Boards][Configuration-JobBoards].

Or you can copy their application to another job. Go to the candidates tab and select the candidate that you want to copy the application by clicking in the check box by his/her name. Look at the right side navigation menu and click “Add to Job”. Select the job that you want to add the candidate to from the list. This keeps them in their previous applied for position as well as puts them in another position that you select.

I changed a candidate’s stage by mistake. How do I get them back to their previous stage?

Navigate to the Candidates tab. Click the second drop down, which should be displaying all the active candidates. You can either select the stage that your candidate was sent to or choose "--All Candidate Stages--". Select the candidate that had the stage change by clicking the checkbox by their name. From the right side navigation menu select "Set Stage", change the candidate to the stage that you want them in and click submit.

Is there a way to merge duplicate candidate applications into one?

We do not offer a way to merge the applicants together. We do display a duplicate note if there is more than one application for the candidate. Also when you are making notations about a candidate through our Add Note feature, you can set it to global and notes that you make will appear on all instances of the candidate.

## FAQ: Job Boards

The following are some frequently asked questions related to job boards in ApplicantStack.

Can a candidate apply for a job more than once?

By default, a candidate cannot apply for a job more than once with the same email address. If a candidate uses a different email address, they could apply for a job more than once.

How do I add a different application to my Internal Board than what is on the Public Job Board?

1. Make sure your internal job board is active. Click **Setup->Job Board**. Select internal job board by clicking **Edit Settings**. Set the Status field to active and click save.
2. Go to your library and select questionnaires from the left. If you need to change wording on your current application, then clone your current application by selecting the green cross in its row on the right. Name it something like Employment Application Internal. Otherwise locate the questionnaire that you wish to use for the alternate internal application.
3. Go to your job that you want to post internal. Click the questions tab. Add the first Public application by clicking Add from Library on the right hand side. Add the alternate internal application by clicking Add from Library on the right hand side.
4. Click the edit icon for the application that you want for the public and make sure that only Show on Public Application is checked. Click Save.
5. Click the edit icon for the application that you want for the internal board and make sure that only Show on Internal Application is checked. Click Save.

I noticed in our demo we saw a search page for a job board. How do we use that page as our main landing page for our job boards and how do we configure that page with the search options that we want to use?

The address for this page is [http://yourdomainname.applicantstack.com/x/search](http://help.applicantstack.com/kb/recruiting-user-guide/frequently-asked-questions-job-boards). The page uses job fields that have the picklist type as search fields. You can add fields to this page by going to settings, then configure, and then click configure job fields. You can take any field that is a picklist/dropdown and change their visibility from private to public. They’ll appear on the search page, but they’ll also appear as columns on the openings page. If you want to remove fields, change their visibility from Public to Private. This will also remove their entries on the job openings page.

I need to edit a job listing/modify a job. How do I send these changes to our Job Board?

When you modify a job in ApplicantStack, the changes will appear automatically on your **Public Job Board** as well as your**Internal Job Board** (if active). The changes also appear automatically in the feed that is sent to Indeed and SimplyHired and should appear their within 24 hours, if not earlier. If your job is on CareerBuilder, Monster, or any other third party job board as well as social media sites, you will need to launch your job again to those respective sites to have your changes / modifications appear there.

Does ApplicantStack have automated candidate source tracking available? We've been using the feature of adding a drop down for candidates to select where they heard about the position, but is there an automated way to track this that might be more accurate than a self-report?

Yes, ApplicantStack has automated source tracking. You just need to generate the Apply link for the site from the job’s Launch tab by selecting the Source under the manual links section, and then use the Apply URL that it gives you, which will have a 4 letter code on the end. ApplicantStack uses this code to set the Source field of the applicant record. Alternatively, you can use the Apply URL and type the source value at the end of the URL. For example if your Apply URL was[http://somesite.applicantstack.com/x/apply/a2fv471z86di](http://somesite.applicantstack.com/x/apply/a2fv471z86di), you would go to the end of the URL, enter a backslash and then your source. If you wanted to use CareerBuilder, your new Apply URL would look like[http://somesite.applicantstack.com/x/apply/a2fv471z86di/CareerBuilder](http://somesite.applicantstack.com/x/apply/a2fv471z86di/CareerBuilder). Note that your source at the end of the URL should match the spelling and punctuation of the source in the source value drop down.

I want to use SSL for my ApplicantStack account. Are there any special considerations to doing so?

Yes. If you use a custom job board domain, you cannot use the SSL feature for ApplicantStack. You will need to use the default ApplicantStack domain to enable the SSL feature.

## FAQ: Jobs

How many attachments may I attach to a job?

You can attach up to ten attachments to each job.

I am trying to delete a Job Workflow Stage, but when I attempt to do so I am told that Job “XXXX” is in this stage. What do I do?

You need to move the jobs out of the stage that you are trying to delete before you can delete the stage.

How do I make my ApplicantStack™ job openings page become a search page and then list positions based on the criteria from the search page?

Go to settings, configure, and then click configure job fields. You can take any field that is a picklist/dropdown and change their visibility from Private to Public. They’ll appear on the search page as filters that you can use to search for open positions. Keep in mind these same fields will also appear as columns on the openings page. You can access the search page with this address: [http://yourdomainname.ApplicantStack.com/x/search](http://yourdomainname.applicantstack.com/x/search)

I need to include a link to a help file on how to effectively utilize a particular job field. I do not see any where to do this.

You can enter a hyperlink to a file in the description field of your job field. This file will need to be located on a web server before users would be able to access it.

When I enter a new user into our ApplicantStack™ system why can they not see any jobs?

You need to make sure that you have assigned jobs to the new user. You can do this by editing the job and selecting the new user as a Job Owner or Hiring Manager.

Can I change the stage on multiple jobs at once?

Currently you can only change the stage on one job at a time.

I created a new Job Workflow Stage. Now I don’t see any buttons to advance my job out of this stage. Why can’t I move past my stage?

The buttons are Workflow Actions and they reason that you do not see any on your stage is that this stage has no actions assigned to. Go to Configure and then click Configure Job Workflow Actions to make sure that your stages have an action assigned to them.

How do I add a new column that is not listed under the “Columns” button to the Jobs Grid?

Go to configure and click Configure Job Fields. Click Create Field to create a new job field, enter the requested information and click save. The new field is now in your Jobs Grid. Note that you may need to return to the Jobs Tab and click the button labeled "Columns", then check your field name(s) and click submit.

## FAQ: ApplicantStack Users

I am being notified of every stage change for every candidate on jobs that are not mine. How can I turn this off?

When users were checked off to be notified in each stage or the stage in question, they were checked off by name, which will cause the users to be notified of every candidate that enters the stage regardless of whether it is for one of their jobs. Typically you would assign the Job Owner or the Hiring Manager as the user that would be notified by the stage change, which would notify whomever is the Job Owner/Hiring Manager of the candidate’s job and no one else.

How do I change my *password* ?

Select **My Account** from the top right corner. Select **Edit Account** from the right side menu. Enter a new password in the **Password** field. Enter your new password again in the **Confirm Password** field. Click **Save**.

t: Gathering Candidate Feedback from Hiring Managers
b:
Using ApplicantStack™ you can request feedback from Hiring Managers and other stakeholders to facilitate a collaborative review of Candidates. Feedback can be simple comments or more structured with a questionnaire. All feedback for a candidate is stored with their candidate record and can be viewed on their Feedback tab.

### Create a Candidate Review Task

In most scenarios the preferred way to solicit feedback from a user on a candidate is to create a new Candidate Review Task by clicking **Create Task** for the candidate. Note that you can do this for a single candidate or select multiple candidates from the table at once. Clicking Create Task brings up the Create Task screen where you can fill in the task details, set up automatic email reminders to the user, and optionally select a Questionnaire to include as part of the feedback request.

[Screenshot]

When you click Submit the assigned user(s) will receive an email which contains the task details and a link to complete the task.

[Screenshot]

When the user clicks the link in the email they will be taken to the View Task page where they can view all the candidate information and at the bottom submit feedback for the candidate.

[Screenshot]

For more details on creating a Candidate Review task see the [Tasks Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Tasks-Tab).

### Enter Candidate Feedback from the Feedback Tab

Users who have a login to your system can also enter candidate feedback by going directly to the Feedback Tab for the candidate and selecting the appropriate Questionnaire from your Library:

[Screenshot]

### View all Candidate Feedback

Regardless of which mechanism is used to collect candidate feedback, the feedback is displayed on the Feedback Tab of the candidate record.

[Screenshot]

## ApplicantStack *Recruit* Getting Started Guide

ApplicantStack Recruit is where you can create job listings and post them to public and third-party job boards. As prospective employees apply, you and members of your team can manage the candidate review process through the Application Workflow. This *Getting Started* guide walks you through the *basics* of using ApplicantStack Recruit, but it also contains links that explain some of the more advanced functionality of the system.

If you want to jump a particular topic, you can use the index below:

- Create a Job
- Launch a Job
- Manage Candidates
- Hire a Candidate

Recruit's *Home* page includes dashboard elements (which you can read about in our help center) and the *Pipeline Summary* , which lists your company's open jobs. (For users with the *Hiring Manager* role, Pipeline Summary is limited to jobs visible to them.) The Pipeline Summary also shows a count of the applicants in the various stages of the Application Workflow.

[Screenshot: The ApplicantStack Dashboard with the Pipeline Summary called out.]

Note, the menu items and options shown in this article may differ from your account based on your role and configuration.

[Screenshot: icon of a play button]

**Watch how it's done.**
A video on getting familiar with ApplicantStack is found in the article [Recruit "Getting Started" Video](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Recruit-Getting-Started-Video).

If your company has just started using ApplicantStack, then your Pipeline Summary may already contain some sample jobs and candidates which you can use to get familiar with the system. However, if you're ready to create your own new job posting, you can use the instructions in the next topic.

### Create a Job

Adding a new job listing to your ApplicantStack account is done from the **Jobs** tab. It's one of the functional tabs which appears at the top of the page throughout the system. Once selected, you'll see a list of the current active jobs and a contextual menu on the right side of the page. Select **Create Job** from that menu to create a new listing.

[Screenshot: The Jobs tab in ApplicantStack listing various open job listings, the Create Job menu item is called out]

After selecting *Create Job* , a pop-up asks you to choose if you want to create a job with a blank form or use a template. Unless you've been instructed to use a specific template, you can just select *Blank Form* for now. However, you can learn more about job templates in the article [Library - Job Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Job-Templates).

[Screenshot: icon of a play button]

**Watch how it's done.**
A video on creating a job is found in the article [Create a Job - VIDEO](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Create-a-Job-VIDEO).

On the subsequent page, fill in some basic information about the position. *Job ID* , a required field, is auto-populated, but you can enter your own unique identifier for the job if you choose. All these fields can be used for filtering and sorting your various jobs throughout the system.

[Screenshot: The job information fields filled in while creating a job.]

Each job field includes a brief description of its purpose; and while not every field is required, filling them all in makes for a more effective recruitment process. Administrators can also add new fields and customize the existing job fields. Instruction on this is found in the article [Configure - Job Fields](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Job-Fields).

In addition to filling in the job fields, you'll be asked to complete the following for a new job:

- **Job Description** - Use the rich text editor to write a summary of the job for your candidates. This editor also includes a *Paste from Word* option that carries over basic formatting from your Word documents. However, not all formatting from Word is supported in ApplicantStack and you may find that the appearance doesn't match what was in your original Word document. To avoid this, use *Paste as Plain Text* instead and use the formatting options in the ApplicantStack styling bar.
- **User Access** - Determine which staff members have access to the job and its candidates. Their role can be either as a *Job Owner* or *Hiring Manager* , both of which are explained on the page. For more on adding users, check out the article [Setup - Users](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Setup-Users).
- **Workflow** - Select a specific Job and Application Workflow to be used with this job. Most companies use the default workflows, but if you want to learn more about how to customize workflows, check out the articles [Configure - Job Workflows](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Job-Workflow) and [Configure the Application Workflow](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Workflow).

After you save the job, it is in the *Draft* stage, which is indicated under the job title. Draft jobs are not visible on your job board.

[Screenshot: The Listing tab of a draft job with the Edit Job menu item called out]

A series of tabs show the details you entered in the previous steps. The job fields from the previous step are found on the *Summary* tab while the job description is found on the *Listing* tab. You can also utilize some of the advanced tools, like [Questions](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Questionnaires) and [Scoring Rules](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Creating-Scoring-Rules) through their respective tabs.

Once you have set up the job, the next step is to launch it to your job board.

### Launch a Job

Each job can be posted to your public and internal job boards as well as any third-party job boards you have set up. The third-party sites (which may require additional configuration), include paid job boards like Monster and CareerBuilder (account required), free sites like Indeed (with Indeed's approval), and social media sites like LinkedIn and Twitter.

*NOTE:* Posting a job to Indeed is not available to accounts in a trial period.

[Screenshot: icon of a play button]

**Watch how it's done.**
A video on launching a job is found in the article [Post a Job - VIDEO](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Post-a-Job-VIDEO).

In the previous topic, the job was left in *Draft* status, so in order to post the job, the status has to be changed to *Open* . This is done with the green button to the right of the Job Title. The button's label indicates which stage the job will be moved to.

[Screenshot: The summary tab of a job with the OPEN button called out]

Depending on your company's configuration, selecting the Open button may result in a pop-up asking you to confirm the stage change. This pop-up also has options for adding a note and notifying other members of your organization.

Once you've changed the job's status to Open, you can post it to your job boards. Select the job's **Launch** tab and you'll see all the possible job boards for your company. Select **Edit Launch Status**.

[Screenshot: The launch tab of for a job]

On the following launch page, select the sites with the checkboxes and click **Next**.

[Screenshot: The job site selection page with the checkboxes highlighted]

If any of the third-party boards require additional information, such as the job's city and state, you will be asked to add that information on an intermediate page. (For important information about Indeed, please see the article [Indeed Jobs - Sponsored vs. Organic](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Jobs-Sponsored-vs-Organic).) Next, confirm that you want to post the job and click **Submit**. The job is immediately posted to your public job board and you are ready to accept online applications!

*NOTE:* There can be a delay between the time you launch a job and when it actually posts to third-party job boards.

#### Share Your Public Job Board

Select **Open Job Board** from the Jobs tab menu to view your public job board and the posting. Your public job board is where applicants view the listing, upload a resume, and apply. If it hasn't been done already, copy the job board's web address (URL) from the address bar of your browser and add a link to it on your company's website. Once you do this, you and your team are ready to manage candidates.

Administrators have the ability to configure certain elements of a company's job boards in the *Setup* area of ApplicantStack. This includes options for enabling and setting up third-party job boards. For more on this, check out the article [Setup Job Boards - Public and Internal](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Setup-Job-Boards-Public-and).

### Manage Candidates

When candidates respond to your job posting, you'll receive a notification email (if enabled). This email contains a link which, if you are already logged into ApplicantStack, takes you directly to the candidate's record.

[Screenshot: New candidate notification email, callout link]

[Screenshot: icon of a play button]

**Watch how it's done.**
A video on managing candidates through the workflow is found in the article [Application Workflow - VIDEO](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Application-Workflow-VIDEO).

Another way to access new candidates is through the Pipeline Summary on the Home page. Just click the number (representing the number of candidates) in the *New* column for the corresponding job.

[Screenshot: Pipeline summary with new candidate number called out]

Both the email link and Pipeline Summary take you to the *Candidates* tab, which, like the Jobs tab, is one of the functional tabs that appears at the top of every page in the system. This is where you'll manage most of your hiring process. The candidate list on this page has filters for Job, Stage, Source, Score, and Rating. (You may need to click **Expand Filters** to modify the filters.) However, if you arrived at the page through the Pipeline Summary, then the Job and Stage filter are already applied to the list based on your selection.

[Screenshot: Candidate tab, highlight tab, show filters]

From the candidate list, select a new candidate by name to view their *Summary* tab. This includes contact information, a download link for their resume, the source of their application, any values entered in the candidate fields (like Score, Rating, and Referred By), and more. ApplicantStack also checks their email address to see if they have already applied for a different job in your company. If so, that job is listed under *Duplicate Candidates* .

[Screenshot: New candidate tab]

The applicant's resume can be previewed on the applicant's resume on the *Resume* tab.

When a candidate first applies, they are put in the *New* stage of your Application Workflow which is a series of defined intervals where you and other users evaluate the candidate. The candidate's current stage is indicated under their name.

[Screenshot: New candidate tab]

As mentioned earlier, the Application Workflow can be customized, but if you are using the *default* workflow, then the next stage for a candidate would be *Manager Review* , in which the Hiring Manager associated with the job reviews the candidate's qualifications. Moving them to this stage is done the green button to the right of their name (see image above). The button's label indicates which stage the candidate will be moved to.

*NOTE:* The down arrow on the green stage-change button allows you to advance the candidate to *any* stage in the workflow.

Most stage changes are followed by a *Stage Change Confirmation* pop-up where you can make notes, message candidates, add ratings, and notify other users that the candidate has advanced.

[Screenshot: stage change confirmation pop-up]

As a candidate moves through the Application Workflow, those users within your company that have been associated with each stage are asked to perform various tasks and decide whether to advance the candidate further. This process can also include automated notifications to both the users and the candidate. All these items are defined in the company's [Application Workflow configuration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Workflow).

In addition to the green button that advances a candidate through the Application Workflow, there is also a red, *Do Not Pursue* button. If you or another user determines that a candidate isn't a good fit for the job, you can use this button to remove them from that job's search. This only hides the candidate; they are NOT deleted from ApplicantStack. These *Do Not Pursue* candidates can still be found by changing the *Stage* filter on candidate list to **Inactive Candidate**.

[Screenshot: Candidate tab with stage filter dropdown showing Inactive Candidate]

As candidates move through the workflow, any updates to their information are collected on the various tabs on their record. These tabs include:

- **Answers** - Shows the candidate’s answers to any Questionnaires that are associated with the job.
- **Feedback** - Displays any [questionnaires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Questionnaires) or feedback submitted by your company's users that have evaluated the candidate.
- **Workflow** - Lists the dates when the candidate was moved to a stage and indicates which user is responsible for the next action in the workflow.
- **Tasks** - This tab allows certain [tasks](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Tasks-Tab) to be assigned to an internal user for each candidate. Examples include a background check or reference check. Once created, the tasks can be easily forwarded to the internal user for completion.
- **Events** - [Events](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Events-Tab) are similar to tasks except that they correspond to a particular scheduled event.
- **History** - An audit trail (date and time stamp) of everything that has happened related to the candidate.

Use Events to schedule an interview.

*Events* are a feature of ApplicantStack that facilitate scheduling a meeting related to a Job or Candidate. Scheduling interviews is a common use for Events and makes coordinating you and your staff's interview schedules easier. Events include email invites and confirmations, they can account for a user's availability, and can even ask the candidate themselves to choose a date and time. To learn more about scheduling interviews with Events, check out [Schedule a Candidate Event](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Events-Tab#schedule-a-candidate-event) in the *Events Tab* article.

#### Search Candidates

Search for a candidate by name with the *Search Candidates* field found at the upper right corner of every page in ApplicantStack. For a more robust search, which lets you search by additional fields and keywords, use the **Search** menu item on the Candidates tab.

[Screenshot: Candidate tab with name search field and advanced search menu item called out]

The Candidate tab Search includes additional parameters which can help you find candidates meeting select criteria as well as those that are in certain stages of the Application Workflow. For example, you can find one or more candidates for two Jobs that are in the Interview stage and live within so many miles of a selected zip code. You can also search for those that have certain keywords in their resume or cover letter.

[Screenshot: Advanced Search setup page with fields filled in]

The text fields (non-dropdown fields) and keyword fields support [boolean operators](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Using-Boolean-Logic-in-Search) for more advanced searches.

These searches can be saved using a checkbox at the bottom of the Search configuration. After you name and run the search, they are found in the right-side contextual menu under **Saved Search**.

#### Create and Edit Candidates

On the right side of the *Candidates* tab is a contextual menu. It includes multiple functions for managing candidates, including three methods for manually adding a candidate to a job.

[Screenshot: Candidate tab with create candidate menu options shown]

- **Create Candidate** - With this function, you select the job, fill in all the candidate fields, set the candidates stage, and attach a resume.
- **Upload Resumes** - Use this if you've received a resume directly from a candidate and want to upload it to ApplicantStack. The resume will be parsed to populate the candidate fields.
- **Upload Emails** - If you have received emails from one or more candidates, this option lets you attach those emails to a message sent directly to ApplicantStack. The system then creates individual candidates for the selected job.

To edit a candidate's record from the list view, use the pencil icon associated with their record. When viewing an individual candidate record, the edit option is found in the right-side menu.

It's also possible to associate candidates with *other* jobs in your company. The options to do this are found in the right-side contextual menu. **Add to Job** adds them to another job listing while also keeping them with the currently viewed job. **Set Job** moves them to another job and removes them from the currently viewed job.

#### Message Candidates

One advantage to ApplicantStack is that you can communicate with candidates without using your work email. A candidate's summary tab has a "mail" button to the right of their email address as well as an **Email Candidate** option in the right-side contextual menu.

[Screenshot: Candidate tab with message options highlighted]

You can also bulk email multiple candidates from the list view page of the Candidate tab. Use the checkboxes to select one or more candidates and then compose the message using **Email Candidate**. You can also create [templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Email-Templates) for these emails through the Library tab.

Text messaging candidates is also possible in ApplicantStack. This is a premium feature that must be enabled by an administrator. More info on texting can be found in the article [Activate Texting for ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack).

*NOTE:* Texting is not available to accounts in a trial period.

### Hire a Candidate

Once you've chosen a candidate for your job, use the *Job Offer* and *Hired* stages of the Application Workflow to conclude the hiring process. These stages are found on the green stage change button of the candidate record.

[Screenshot: Status change button with dropdown shown]

Email messages can be added during the Stage Change Confirmation, but eventually, you might consider adding an email template in your Message Library that is triggered automatically when a candidate is moved to a Job Offer stage.

For companies using ApplicantStack Onboard, the Hired stage confirmation also includes fields for selecting the new hire's onboarding workflow and manager.

[Screenshot: Hire stage change confirmation with onboarding items called out]

Offer letters can also be created in your [Documents Library](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Documents) and shared with the candidate using **Create Document** in the Candidate menu.

Once a candidate is hired, select the job on the Jobs tab and change the stage to *Filled* with the green stage-change button.

[Screenshot: Job with the filled button called out]

This sets the job to inactive and removes it from your public job board. The job is also removed from third-party job boards within 24 hours, but the actual time may vary depending on the board.

#### Manage Remaining Candidates

Once your job is filled, any remaining, un-hired candidates are still active and visible on the Candidates tab. They can remain in this state, but you can also change their stage to *Do Not Pursue* (which makes them inactive) or associate them with another job using **Set Job** in the candidate menu.

You can also send a bulk, "position filled" email through the Candidate tab. Just use the checkboxes to select the applicants and then click **Email Candidate** from the right-side menu.

[Screenshot: Multiple employees selected on the Candidate tab with Email Candidate highlighted]

You might consider creating a standard "position filled" message template in your library for this purpose.

## ApplicantStack *Recruit* Hiring Manager's Guide

The Hiring Manager’s Guide will take you through the core features and benefits of ApplicantStack™ and illustrate how they can be used during the hiring process.

As a hiring manager in the ApplicantStack™ Product, your company or recruiting firm wants you to be able to access candidate information, document information regarding the candidate, and move the candidate through the hiring workflow process.

### Log In

The administrator of ApplicantStack™ sets up users in the system. Users, depending on their configuration of the system, will receive login information either from the administrator directly or via an automatic email.

The email will provide the website URL, username and password.

[Screenshot]

By selecting the URL from the email, you will be presented with the login screen and prompted to enter the username and password information:

[Screenshot]

It is likely that the administrator has set up the system to prompt you to change your password the first time that you login to the system. In that case, you are presented with the following screen to change your password:

[Screenshot]

Select submit and you will be brought to the home page.

### Home Page

The home page is command central allowing you to view activities, navigate the system, and perform certain tasks directly from the navigation menu.

[Screenshot]

**Activity Summary** displays new emails or account notifications.

The **Pipeline Summary** displays jobs, number of candidates, and candidate status.

> 1.) Any Job where you are indicated as a Hiring Manager will display under the Job column. By selecting the Job Name link, you are brought to the Job Tab and the Job Summary page.
>
>
>
> 2.) Under the **Manager Review** column, the number of Candidates that have been submitted to you to review will display. Click on the *underlined* number and you will be brought to the Candidate tab and the Candidates will display. Clicking any of the columns will also bring you to the Candidate tab, with the correct filter (status) applied.
>
>
>
> 3.) Selecting the **Total Active** link will also be bring you to the Candidate tab, where all candidates associated with all jobs (where you are the Hiring Manager) will display.

### Candidate Tab

The **Candidate Tab** provides a complete view of all the Candidates that you, as a Hiring Manager, have access to. This candidate list will include any candidate that is associated with job(s) in the system where you are indicated as the Hiring Manager and they are in a stage where you are the owner.

[Screenshot]

Candidate List Columns The available fields provide a quick view of candidate information. Click each column name to sort by that field.

The default list of columns is as follows:

- **Name**: Name of the candidate. It also contains the city and state of the candidate.
- **R**: This stands for Resume. You can hover over the icon and if they have submitted a resume, a preview will be generated for you.
- **Job**: The name of the job and job id that the candidate applied for.
- **Source**: Where the candidate heard about the job from.
- **Rating**: Rating that is assigned based on qualifications of the candidate.
- **Disposition**: Items can be assigned designating whether the candidate has insufficient experience, insufficient education, or poor interview performance among many others.
- **Created**: Date candidate was created in the system.
- **Last Modified**: Last date that the candidate had their record modified.
- **Score**: Score candidate received based on their answers to a questionnaire(s). If no score is calculated then N/A will appear. If the candidate has been indicated as a Knockout, KO will appear.
- **Stage**: The current stage that the candidate occupies.
- **Actions**: From here you can open the candidate detail record.

*Source* and *Rating* are standard application fields, but your organization may have additional application fields configured. In that case, those additional fields may also display on this grid.

t: How do candidates find my jobs? Can I post my jobs to my website?
b:
If you have a company website, it is recommended that you add a link from your website to your ApplicantStack job board to direct your website visitors to view and apply to your jobs. Contact your webmaster to request that they add a link to the Openings page of your ApplicantStack job board.

If you are linking to your Job Board from your website, we can build a custom job board template to match your website and provide a branded, seamless experience for your users. Contact your ApplicantStack support representative for details.

In addition to linking from your website, you can post your jobs to other third-party job boards, such as Indeed™. On some sites, you can also create the job post according to that job board’s directions and then direct people to apply through ApplicantStack™ using the **Apply Online** link from the Launch tab of the job.

We've included Accessible Web Design requirements in the design of our ApplicantStack client career site / application. More information on Accessible Web Design can be found here: [http://www.washington.edu/doit/world-wide-access-accessible-web-design](http://www.washington.edu/doit/world-wide-access-accessible-web-design)

For example, a candidate who is blind or vision-impaired would use speech assistance device to "read aloud" a website, but there are some common things you see on some websites that make this difficult or impossible.

Here are some technical details of things that we take into consideration when designing ApplicantStack public sites (i.e. career sites and application):
- Use relative font sizes so text can be resized (using the browser) for people with vision impairment
- Don't use Flash or images for key information that can't be interpreted by screen readers and speech assistance devices
- Don't rely on audio or video for key information, unless subtitles are also provided
- Allow forms to be navigated using only the keyboard
- Use a simple layout and navigation for the site
- Support different screen sizes (including mobile screens)
- Include an "alt" tag for all images
- Limit the use of frames, which can be difficult for assisted devices to navigate

One thing to note is that since we base our client career site on the client's website (when we create a custom job board skin), the extent of accessibility is somewhat dependent on the client's main website. If the client makes any changes to their website to make it more accessible, we can update their career site (i.e. skin) to match.

t: Including a Questionnaire Link in a Message Template
b:
## Including a Questionnaire Link in a Message Template

When creating an message template, you can add a link to a questionnaire from your library. When the candidate clicks the link, and completes the questionnaire, the answers will be saved and linked to the candidate's record.

To do this, you'll first need to get the questionnaire's ID:

1. If you aren't already there, select the **Library** tab.
2. Select **Questionnaires** from the left-side menu.
3. Open the questionnaire by selecting the name.
4. In the address bar of your browser, select and copy the ID, which is a string of characters at the end of the URL. It will be in the form a7xxxxxxxxxx. (see example below)

[Screenshot: A questionnaire url with the ID highlighted]

The next step is to paste the ID into your message template with a specific merge code:

1. Select **Messages** from the left-side menu.
2. Edit the message by selecting the edit button in the *Actions* column.
3. Insert the ID into the body of the message and enclose it in the {!qelink_XXXXX} merge code, like this:

   **{!qelink_** *<questionnaire_id>* **}**

When you are done, your email template should look something like this:

[Screenshot: A questionnaire merge code in a message template]

It's always a good idea to send a test version to yourself first, to verify that the link is input correctly. If correct, the recipient should receive an email that looks something like this:

[Screenshot: An example of an email with a link to the questionnaire]

Can I include a questionnaire in a text message?

Yes, if you have texting enabled, a questionnaire link can be included in a text message template in the same way as was demonstrated for an email template. The questionnaire will be included as a clickable link that opens in the device's web browser.

## Indeed Job Posting Best Practices

The following are actions you can take to optimize your Indeed job postings through ApplicantStack. Employers who are having trouble with job visibility on Indeed should follow the recommendations in this article.

### Sponsor Jobs

Indeed recommends sponsoring job postings to attract more quality candidates, faster. An Indeed *sponsored* job is a paid listing that is displayed in relevant search results on Indeed. It increases the visibility of your posting and provides more quality applicants than a free, organic listing. Employers who do not sponsor their jobs should expect limited performance as compared to if they were sponsoring. However, employers are still able to post their jobs for free on Indeed. For more information on sponsoring jobs, see:

- [Indeed Jobs - Sponsored vs Organic](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Jobs-Sponsored-vs-Organic)
- [Indeed Sponsored Jobs Integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Sponsored-Jobs-Integration)

### Define Location

Adding a precise location to your job postings results in more clicks per posting and more applications from candidates in your job's location. For more information on how defining a job's location can improve your applications, see:

- [Location Flyer](https://nam02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/)
- [Appropriate Use of Location On Indeed](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/Appropriate-Use-of-Location-on-Indeed)

### Define Salary

Increase the number of job applicants by including a salary range in your posting. Seventy-five percent of job seekers are more likely to apply for a job if the salary range is listed in the posting. For more information about how including a salary range in your postings can improve your applications, see:

- [Salary Flyer](https://nam02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/)
- [Indeed Pay Transparency](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/Indeed-pay-transparency-salary-estimates)

### Earn An Employer Response Badge

When you update statuses for at least 50% of your Indeed candidates, a Responsive Employer Badge is automatically added to your jobs improving your hiring process and boosting your company’s brand visibility and appeal. See [What Is An Employer Response Badge](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/What-is-an-Employer-Response-Badge) for more information.

### Enable Disposition Sync

When you enable Disposition Sync, your ApplicantStack platform sends hiring signals to Indeed that helps fine tune candidate matching so you’ll get better matches for your roles. Disposition data is information related to or about the status of a job application and the decision taken by the employer or candidate on an application, such as whether a candidate was contacted, interviewed, given an offer, rejected, or hired. When a job seeker applies for a job on our platform or on certain third-party websites (for example, an applicant tracking system), Indeed may receive Disposition data from the employer to which they applied. Disposition data can also include a timestamp indicating when a job seeker application status is updated or changed.

See [Disposition](https://nam02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/) for more information.

#### EEO Questions

For any job postings based in the United States, questions that serve as equal employment opportunity questions for applicant tracking purposes (information about an applicant’s Race/Ethnicity, Sex, Disability, Veteran Status) must have metadata that labels them as such. It is important for employers to enable EEO questions in their Indeed Apply integrations.

### Avoid Duplicate Posts

Create *one* job post for each unique opportunity. Creating multiple posts for a single job may result in reduced visibility of job posts in search results, lower ranking or removal of job posts, or other penalties. For information about Indeed's policy on redundant job posts, see [Policies Regarding Reposted Content, Job Post Duplication, and Manipulation of Search Results](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/Policies-Regarding-Reposted-Content-Job-Post-Duplication-and-Manipulation-of-Search-Results).

### Avoid Asking for PII

Job posts should not ask for unnecessary personally identifying information (PII), including full date of birth, bank account information, or numbers from government-issued IDs. Posts requesting this information may be down ranked or removed by Indeed. See[Policy - Personally Identifiable Information](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/Policy-Personally-Identifiable-Information-PII) for more information.

### ApplicantStack Version of Indeed Integration Includes:

- Indeed Apply Sync
- Candidate Sync
- Disposition Sync

## Indeed Jobs - Sponsored vs Organic

ApplicantStack allows you to post jobs to Indeed.

### Organic

When you launch your job through ApplicantStack, by default you are posting your job organically (non-paid) and over time the job will lose its position on the search list which may result in fewer candidates. Indeed recommends sponsoring job postings to attract more quality candidates, faster. Employers who do not sponsor their jobs should expect limited performance as compared to if they were sponsoring. Employers whose jobs are no longer receiving organic visibility should sponsor their jobs on Indeed.

For more information about organic versus sponsored jobs, see [Sponsoring Jobs on Indeed](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/115001043926).

#### Bulk-posting Jobs (Refreshing Your Jobs)

Bulk automated reposting, also known as refreshing your jobs, is no longer accepted at any time-interval. Automatically reposting jobs may be subject to feed-level visibility penalties. Employers who continually repost jobs may no longer be able to post jobs organically and may be required to sponsor jobs.

### Sponsored

The only way to ensure your top spot is to sponsor (pay) for your job. You can do this by launching your job through ApplicantStack and selecting the option to sponsor your jobs. See [Indeed Sponsored Jobs Integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Sponsored-Jobs-Integration) for more information on how to sponsor your job. Sponsoring jobs will ensure that they display at the top of search results and will yield more candidates. Indeed charges begin when a candidate starts an application for your sponsored job.

According to Indeed's documentation:

*Every day, candidates come to Indeed to find the job that fits them best. They begin by entering the type of job they’re looking for and where they’d like to work.*

*The search results they see are a combination of organic job listings (jobs that are aggregated by our search engine) and sponsored jobs (jobs that are promoted by employers). These search results are matched to the search terms candidates entered and are sorted by relevance and the date the job was posted.*

*New jobs are added to Indeed every day. As these new jobs appear, organic listings fall in the search results. Jobs that are sponsored by employers remain high in the search results. They appear prominently at the top and the bottom of the page, even as time passes.*

*Sponsored Jobs are based on a pay for performance model. Employers set a monthly budget and only pay when a candidate clicks to view your job. You decide how much to spend and we deliver relevant, high-quality candidate traffic. In this way, you can craft recruitment campaigns, track your return on investment and reach the widest audience of qualified job seekers. While setting up your Indeed campaign, reach out to the Indeed team to answer any questions and help you make adjustments so you can reach your target audience.*

## 2022-06-29 Indeed Sponsored Job Budget Tools

Swipeclock has added more functionality to the Indeed Sponsored Job Integration. Now, when defining a budget for your campaign, the Campaign Details page offers both a suggested budget and a prediction of how many applicants you'll get for your defined budget. This analysis is based on Indeed's comparison of your posting to similar postings already on their site. The article [Indeed Sponsored Jobs Integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Sponsored-Jobs-Integration) has been updated to reflect these new tools.

Additionally, the Indeed Campaign Analytics link in ApplicantStack now shows select metrics right in ApplicantStack instead of taking you to Indeed.

## Indeed Sponsored Job Integration

An Indeed *sponsored* job is a paid listing that is displayed in relevant search results on Indeed. It increases the visibility of your posting and provides more quality applicants than a free, organic listing. In ApplicantStack, the Launch tab has an *Indeed Sponsored Jobs* section where you can add a job to the site's sponsored feed.

[Screenshot: Indeed sponsored job section on launch tab]

Sponsored jobs can be posted through ApplicantStack, but they are billed by Indeed. With sponsored jobs, you also get access to Indeed's reporting and analytics, so you can better understand and optimize your hiring campaigns.

Any job already posted to Indeed's organic feed can become a sponsored job, but you will need an Indeed account. If you don't have an account, you can create one when launching your sponsored job.

### Post a Sponsored Job

A job must be [posted to Indeed's organic feed](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Posting-Your-Jobs-to-Indeed) before it can be posted to the sponsored feed. Once you launch the organic post, allow *up to* 8 hours before sponsoring it. Once the **Sponsor Job** link is selectable on the Launch page, the job can be launched as a sponsored post.

[Screenshot: the Sponsor Job link for a job]

To launch a sponsored job, select **Sponsor Job** on the Launch page to access the Indeed landing page. If the **Sponsor Job** link is not selectable, not enough time has passed since you posted the job to the organic feed.

On the Indeed landing page, log in with your Indeed credentials. If you don't have an Indeed account, enter an email and Indeed creates one for you. The next step is to define your campaign.

*NOTE:* When logging into Indeed, two-step verification (email or text) may be required. Also, if your email is associated with multiple companies in Indeed, you will be asked to select a company.

#### Define Your Campaign

Sponsored job campaigns can be a one-time campaign that ends on a specific date (which is selected by default), or a monthly, recurring campaign.

**One-time campaigns** have a start and end date, and an option for either Fixed or Targeted Budget campaigns.

- **Fixed** campaigns end on the selected end date *even if you have budget remaining* .
- **Targeted Budget** campaigns can continue *beyond* the end date *if there is budget remaining.*

**Monthly campaigns** have a start date and an option to prorate the first month of your budget.

#### Choose a Budget

Each job campaign has its own budget amount which is entered on the Campaign Details page with no "$". If you aren't sure how much to allocate for your campaign, Indeed offers budgeting tools in the upper-right of the Campaign Details page.

[Screenshot: Campaign Details page, prediction tools outlined]

**Prediction** offers an optimal budget for your job based on the job description and location. It also displays an estimate of how many applicants your campaign may receive at that budget. If you want to use this prediction amount as your budget, select **Use Prediction Budget** above the budget field.

**Performance estimator** estimates how many applicants you may receive based on your budget amount.

If you change your campaign type, dates, or budget, the Performance estimator is updated in two ways, by clicking out outside the text fields or by selecting **Update Performance Estimator** above the budget field.

For more information on campaign budgeting, access Indeed's online help site with the **Indeed Support Form** link in the upper-right corner of the page.

#### Confirm and Submit Your Campaign

Once you've defined your campaign, select **Next** to advance to the campaign confirmation page and review your campaign settings. If you need to make any changes, select **Back** or **Edit**.

The confirmation page also reminds you that your sponsored campaign is not activated until billing is set up for your Indeed account. An Indeed login link provides access to the Indeed billing page in case you need to add or check your billing info, but this message does appear regardless of whether you have billing set up or not.

If the campaign settings are correct, and you are ready to launch the campaign, select **Sponsor on Indeed.** This sends the job to Indeed via the integration.

### Manage Your Campaign

The **Jobs** tab includes a **Sponsored** column which allows you to easily find your sponsored jobs. An Indeed icon in this column indicates the job is sponsored.

[Screenshot: Jobs tab, sponsored column]

If you need to change or end an existing sponsored job campaign, return to the Launch tab for the job and select **Edit Settings** in the *Indeed Sponsored* section. **If the job is filled prior to the completion of your campaign, make sure you change the job's Stage in ApplicantStack.** Indeed will see that the job is no longer in an *Open* stage and, within 24 hours, take the job down from their feed and stop reducing your budget.

#### Indeed Resources

Also available on the Launch page for a sponsored job is the **Account Settings** link which you can use to access Indeed and view your account information.

**Campaign Analytics**, also found on the Launch page, shows Indeed's performance metrics for the selected job. You'll see the following data for your campaign, including from the period during which it was an organic post:

- Apply Starts
- Clicks
- Impressions
- Conversions

More information on this can be found by selecting the **Indeed Analytics** link in the upper-right corner of the analytics page. Additional analytic data can be found in your Indeed account.

For more help from Indeed

If you can't find your post on Indeed, have additional questions, have problems with your sponsored job, contact Indeed Support through the **Indeed Support Form** links found in various places on the Launch page.

*NOTE:* This article reflects changes made to the Indeed integration on May 26, 2022. Sponsored jobs posted *prior* to that date are still active and still appear in the *Indeed Sponsored* section of your Launch page. However, you can no longer manage these campaigns from within ApplicantStack, instead, you need to manage them from within Indeed.
