## Enabling and Configuring Requisition Approvals

This feature might not be available in your account. Please contact your Customer Success Team to discuss options. This feature will provide customers the ability to automate, track and manage their job requisition process via ApplicantStack. Hiring Managers can create a job requisition and begin the approval process automatically with one simple click.

[Screenshot]

To enable the Job Requisition Approval functionality, Choose "Update Settings" from the Home Page:

[Screenshot]

Then Choose "Edit Settings":

[Screenshot]

and then check the Job Requisition Approvals box:

[Screenshot]

When you turn on Job Requisition Approvals for the first time the system will add the following new stages to the job workflow:

- Pending Approval (current user is owner/notify)
- Approved (current user is owner/notify)
- Denied

[Screenshot]

It will also add an Action Button from Approved to Open

[Screenshot]

Note: If you check the Start Approvals box then the approvals process will be automatically started with the job is moved to the Pending Approval. Otherwise, the user who is the Owner/Notify of the Pending Approval stage (initially the user who turned on the setting) will be notified when there is a new job to review and start approval.

Once you enable approvals you can go to Configure Job Fields and add the fields to capture requisition information (e.g. Preferred Start Date, Is this a Replacement Position?, Is this a New Position?, Name of person being Replaced, etc). Set Section to Requisition Information.

[Screenshot]

## Using Job Approvals

[Screenshot]

When job approvals are enabled then Hiring Managers will have a Create Job link on the Jobs tab. The Create Job form for managers will include the Job and Requisition fields and also include an Approvers section where they can enter the user(s) who will approve the job.

[Screenshot]

For Hiring Managers the User Access section - Job Owner(s) and Hiring Manager(s) - and any other advanced sections will be hidden. When the job is created there will initially be no Job Owners or Hiring Managers assigned to the job. The Administrator or Recruiter who moves the job from Approved to Open will need to assign the Job Owner(s) / Hiring Manager(s).

The user who creates the job is marked as the Requisition Submitter of the job. The job will appear in the My Jobs filter for the user and they will be notified when the job is Approved or Denied.

[Screenshot]

Once the manager saves the job, there will be a "Submit for Approval" stage available via the Set Stage dropdown.. When the manager clicks "Submit for Approval" the job will be moved to Pending Approval. ***If the Start Approvals Automatically setting is on for the account then the approval process will start automatically. Otherwise, the recruiter assigned to the Pending Approval stage will be notified and will need to go to the Approvals tab for the job and click Start Approvals.***

[Screenshot]

Choose "Start Approvals: here:

[Screenshot]

When approvals start the first approver in the list is notified. The email notification will include a link to the job as usual, or if the user logs in on the Home tab it will list the jobs that need their approval in the Tasks section.

[Screenshot]

On the Approvals tab there will be buttons for Approve and Deny. Clicking either will open a modal that confirms and asks for a comment. The comment is required for Deny but optional for Approve.

[Screenshot]

If the user clicks Approve, the next approver is notified. If this is the last approver then the job is moved to the Approved stage.

[Screenshot]

If the user clicks Deny, the job is moved to the Denied stage. The manager, the recruiter who started the approvals (if applicable), and anybody who approved the job is notified.

[Screenshot]

[Screenshot]

When the job is in the Denied stage the Manager who originally created the job will be able to Edit the job and can then click the Submit for Approval workflow button, which will move the job to Pending Approval, notify the Recruiter assigned to that stage to start approvals (or start approvals automatically) and the process starts again.

[Screenshot]

Then choose "Submit for Approval" to restart the approval process again:

[Screenshot]

Which starts the approval process again and retains the Job Approval History:

[Screenshot]

When the job is in the Approved stage, the user who is the owner of the stage (initially it will be the user who enabled the job approval functionality in settings) will see the job in their task list on the Home tab. The user will then need to review the job listing, assign Job Owner/Hiring Managers, and then Open/Launch the job.

t: Job Title Best Practices and ATS Quality Guidelines
b:
When posting a job to third-party job boards you should only use the common job title. A basic job title will result in more search hits than if you include the location and other details in the title.

Indeed has started to flag jobs that include other information in the job title, so there's a chance your job won't get posted if you do not follow the following guidelines or worse get flagged at an organization level and none of your jobs post). Note that this only changes the job title on third-party job boards and doesn't change the ApplicantStack job title.

**$!"?*** should not be included in the job titles.

Do not include location, salary, hours, and do not have your job title listed in all capital letters.

The following is Indeed's Best Practices article:

ATS Quality Guidelines
At Indeed we do what’s best for job-seekers and aim to provide the best job-seeker experience.
Our goal is to display unique, quality job postings that are as close to the original hiring source
as possible. The Search Quality team is constantly evaluating listings to ensure that our quality
guidelines are met.
The jobs we receive from various ATS’s must undergo a review process in order to be included
within our organic listings. Below are some of the general guidelines that our Search Quality
team looks for when reviewing jobs to include in our organic listings. Please note that these are
just general guidelines and they may vary per country. Indeed reserves the right to reject any
company or particular job for failure to meet our quality standards.

- Each posting should represent a real and currently available job
  - Simply put, the job should be a job. We do not allow postings such as product/service advertisements, training courses, business opportunities, or especially fraudulent listings.
- Detailed job descriptions
  - Clear titles and detailed job descriptions result in higher conversion rates. Job descriptions should contain more than a couple of sentences and preferably include items such as a company overview, day today responsibilities of the role, qualifications needed, etc.
- Unique, nonduplicate jobs
  - Duplicate listings, among multiple sources or within a single source, will not be approved for organic visibility. It’s confusing for jobseekers to see multiple versions of the same job from different sources. We do our best to filter out duplicate listings and highlight the single source that provides the best job seeker experience.
- Location specified
  - All jobs should contain both a city and state, and locations should not be included within job titles. If the job is posted outside of the United States, please include specific location information.
- General recruitment/location blasted jobs
  - General recruitment jobs typically include some of the following characteristics:
    - identical descriptions in multiple locations, mentions of hiring for multiple roles in one job posting, mentions of no experience necessary or flexible hours, and references self employment and commission only salaries. These types of jobs are not suitable for organic visibility on Indeed.
- Reposting of jobs
  - The longer the job stays posted, the further it will fall in our organic search results. Reposting the job very frequently to have it placed higher in our search results is not accepted. If the jobs start to see a significant decrease in traffic we recommend sponsoring the job.
- Short/easy apply process
  - In general, the application process should be short and simple. Jobs should not require the job-seeker to pay any registration, application, training, or signing fees.

Listed below are also some additional guidelines for Staffing firms:

- All new [to us] staffing firms default to sponsored only visibility. Staffing firms have the ability to sponsor their jobs, which will appear in Indeed’s sponsored search results.
- Duplicate listings will not be approved for organic visibility. There are many instances in which staffing firms post on behalf of direct employers and these employers often are already posting their jobs directly on Indeed.
- Jobs posted by the direct employers take precedence over those posted by the staffing firm. If the employer would rather their jobs be displayed from the staffing firm, written confirmation from the direct employer is required to begin the review process. The core requirements will still need to be met.
- Staffing firms should brand jobs with their company name as opposed to that of the direct employer they are hiring on behalf of. Job-seekers should be aware that they’re applying to a job posted by a staffing firm rather than one posted by a direct employer.
- We encourage staffing firms to specify within the job description which company they are hiring for.

Indeed is committed to improving the quality of our search results and ensuring that we continue
to be the world’s best job search engine. Please note that content posted on Indeed should be
compliant with our Terms of Service, which can be found [here](https://www.indeed.com/legal#indeedTerms).

## JobTarget Integration

The JobTarget integration expands the reach of your ApplicantStack job recruitment to include over 25,000 additional job boards. These boards include niche sites, those specializing in diversity recruitment and OFCCP compliance, and JobTarget's Programmatic posting option, which uses algorithms to analyze your job and select the most effective channels for recruitment.

[Screenshot: JobTarget Marketplace page]

### Post to Job Target

Posting a job to JobTarget can be done from a job's *Launch* tab. The Launch tab appears automatically whenever you move a job to the *Open* stage, but you can also select the Launch tab at any time when viewing a job.

[Screenshot: Launch tab on Job page]

Jobs must be in the *Open* stage to be posted on JobTarget.

Do I need to set up a JobTarget account?

No, the first time you post a job to JobTarget, an account is set up automatically for you. This account is linked to your ApplicantStack login. From that point forward, your JobTarget postings are managed from within the applicant tracking system; you do not need to log in to JobTarget separately.

To post a job to JobTarget:

1. Select the *Launch* tab for the job.
2. Under *Third-Party Job Boards,* click the **Post Job** link associated with JobTarget.

[Screenshot: Post Job link]

3. Enter the City, State, Zip, and Country of your job. JobTarget requires this information even if it's already included in your job posting.

[Screenshot: Additional fields for JobTarget]

4. Click **Launch Job Target.** A pop-up appears explaining that you are being redirected to JobTarget's site.
5. Click **OK** on the pop-up to proceed to JobTarget. You will remain on an ApplicantStack page, but JobTarget's Marketplace and interface are displayed within that page.
6. Agree to JobTarget's terms and conditions.
7. Choose your posting options from the Marketplace by clicking **Add to Cart**. If you are looking for a specific job board, use the *Search Sites* field at the bottom of the page.

[Screenshot: JobTarget search field]

| [Screenshot] | ***IMPORTANT:*** If you have already set up arrangements with certain job boards (free or paid) within ApplicantStack, it is suggested that you continue posting to them through ApplicantStack, not in JobTarget. For a list of these boards, see the section titled *Job Boards that Overlap with JobTarget* later in this article*.* |
| --- | --- |

8. After making your selections, click **Next Step** at the bottom of the page.
9. If any of your selected job boards require additional information (like industry type or categorization), you will be asked to fill that in next. In some cases, you may not need to enter any additional information.

[Screenshot: Categorization of a job post]

10. Click **Next Step – Review Order** to advance to the checkout page.
11. Enter your payment details and verify your order is correct.
12. Click **Confirm Payment** and a confirmation page, with an order ID, appears once the order is completed.

#### Returning to ApplicantStack

Once your order is complete, click **Done**, at the bottom of the page.

[Screenshot: Done button]

You will be asked to confirm that you want to return to ApplicantStack.

At any time during the JobTarget launch process, you can click the**Done** button to exit JobTarget, but doing so before completing your order means your job will not be posted. If you do return to JobTarget for the same job at a later time, you are notified that you have an incomplete order and will be given the option to complete the order or discard it.

[Screenshot: Incomplete order button]

#### Job Boards that Overlap with JobTarget

JobTarget includes several popular job boards that may already be configured on your ApplicantStack account. In cases where you have already configured these boards, it is strongly recommended that you continue to post to them through ApplicantStack and not in JobTarget. Pricing and other agreements you may have in ApplicantStack are not honored by JobTarget.

The boards that overlap between JobTarget and ApplicantStack are:

- **CareerBuilder**
- **Dice**
- **GlassDoor**
- **Google for Jobs**
- **Indeed**
- **LinkedIn Limited Postings**
- **Monster**

### View Details on Your JobTarget Post

Once you have posted your job to JobTarget, the *Launch* tab is updated to list the specific job boards underneath JobTarget. You can also get additional information, posting history, and effectiveness data by clicking **View Details**.

[Screenshot: View Details for JobTarget posts]

The items you'll see when clicking **View Details** include:

- Status
- Ordered Date
- Expired Date
- Retail Cost
- Savings
- Taxes/Fees
- Total Cost
- Views
- Visits
- Number of Applications Received

### Edit and Remove a Posting

If you need to make changes to your post or post to new boards, you can do so from within ApplicantStack using the **Edit Posting** link for JobTarget on the Launch tab. Clicking this link first takes you to the Job Information fields page (City, State, etc.)

- If changes are needed on this fields, make them and click **Update JobTarget**.
- If changes are not needed to these fields and you just want to post to new boards in JobTarget, click **Update Job Target**.

On the JobTarget Marketplace page, you can choose new job boards and follow the same process as your initial posting. Do notpost to boards that you have already posted to unless they have expired. If you only need to update the Job Information fields and aren't interested in adding or modifying your postings in JobTarget, just click the **Done** button at the bottom of the page and you will be returned to ApplicantStack.

You can also remove posts from the *Launch* tab in ApplicantStack. This can be done for both *all boards* and individual boards.

| [Screenshot] | ***IMPORTANT:*** JobTarget does not provide refunds for any postings that are removed, regardless of the listed expiration date. |
| --- | --- |

What happens when a job is filled or cancelled?

You do not need to manually remove the posting once you hire a candidate or set the job state to cancelled. When a job changes to an inactive stage, like *Filled* or *Cancelled* , the confirmation page pop-up in ApplicantStack includes a warning that the posting will be removed from JobTarget.

### Deactivate JobTarget

You can deactivate the JobTarget integration on your ApplicantStack Setup page with the following steps:

1. Click your avatar (upper-right corner) and select **Setup**.
2. Choose **Job Boards** from the left-side menu.
3. Click **Edit Settings** for JobTarget.

[Screenshot: Job board settings in ApplicantStack]

4. Set the Status to **Inactive**.
5. Click **Save**.

## Jobs Tab

The *Jobs* tab is where you create, view, and manage the current and historical jobs in your ApplicantStack account. It can be accessed from any page in the system through the main header navigation.

[Screenshot: Jobs page in ApplicantStack with the Jobs tab called out.]

All users can access the Job's tab, but only Administrators and Recruiters can create and edit jobs. Hiring Managers can only view the jobs to which they've been assigned as a Hiring Manager or Job Owner.

This article guides you through the various features of this page and includes links to more detailed articles.

If you want to jump a particular topic in this article, use the index below:

- View a Job
  - Job Stages
- Create a Job
  - Clone a Job
- Launch a Job
  - Internal Job Board
  - Third-Party Job Boards
  - Manual Posting Links
- Edit a Job
  - Edit the Job Listing
  - Add Attachments
- Fill a Job
- Change a Job to Inactive
- Delete a Job
- View Job Data and Run Reports

### View A Job

Selecting the **Job Tab** takes you to a list view of your company's jobs. To view a job, select the *Job Title, ID* or the folder icon in the *Actions* column.

[Screenshot: Job list view, indicate the ID, Title, and open links]

You can also open and view a job anywhere in ApplicantStack where the Job Title appears as a hyperlink, like on the Home page's Pipeline Summary and the Candidates tab.

[Screenshot: Home page with the Pipleine Summary highlighted and a Job's hyperlink called out]

Above the Jobs tab list view are controls for filtering and adjusting the displayed columns. By selecting **Expand Filters**, you can limit the visible jobs by user access, job stage, and any of the job fields. By default, the view shows jobs where you are the Job Owner or Hiring Manager, so if you are an Administrator and want to view *all* jobs, switch the filter from *My Jobs* to *-- All Jobs --* .

[Screenshot: Filters for job my jobs dropdown]

Administrators can also use this filter to view jobs assigned to other users.

The columns on the list view correlate to the fields related to the job object. You can customize the columns by selecting the **Adjust Columns** icon at the right of the list view header.

[Screenshot: Adjust columns icon]

This opens a modal where you can select and deselect the columns visible on the list view.

The Jobs tab list view also has a right-side contextual menu with a **Search** function where you can find a particular job or jobs.

[Screenshot: The search menu item]

This opens opens an advanced search page where you can find a job by campaign dates, stage (Filled, Open, Draft, etc.), any of the job fields, and keywords.

[Screenshot: The search fields field in the advanced job search page filled in]

#### Job Stages

The **Stage** field of a job indicates where it is in Job Workflow. These stages can be customized, but the common default stages and their typical purpose are:

- **Draft** - The initial stage when creating a job. In this stage, the job cannot be posted to a job board yet.
- **Open** - The job is ready to be launched to a job board.
- **Filled** - Used when a candidate has been hired for this job.
- **Cancelled** - Used when a job needs to be removed without being filled.
- **On Hold** - For jobs where the hiring process is put on pause.

Furthermore, these stages are classified as wither **Active** and **Inactive**. *Draft* and *Open* are considered Active while the rest are Inactive. The Jobs list view defaults to display only *Active* jobs, so if you need to view a job that has been filled, switch the stage filter from Active to Inactive, or to the specific Stage you are looking for.

When viewing jobs on the list view, the Stage column also includes icons indicating if the job has been posted to a job board.

[Screenshot: Stage column on the job board listview]

The blue, three-headed arrow, for example, indicates the job has been posted to your public job board.

### Create a Job

Create a new job by selecting **Create Job** from the right-side contextual menu on the Jobs tab.

[Screenshot: The Jobs tab in ApplicantStack listing various open job listings, the Create Job menu item is called out]

After selecting *Create Job* , you are first asked if you want to create an entirely new job or use a job template from your library. Once you've made that choice, fill in and edit the Job Information fields and Job Description.

[Screenshot: The job information fields filled in while creating a job.]

The Job Description, also referred to as the *Job Listing* in ApplicantStack, describes the company, the job and its responsibilities, and the requirements. The listing does not have to be completed at this time. Also, if you have a listing template in your library that you want to use instead of writing an entirely new listing, leave the listing blank at this point; you can edit the job later and use the template then. More on editing a Job Listing is found later in this article under the topic Edit the Job Listing.

The Create Job page also has sections for assigning users (which would be Job Owners and Hiring Managers that are involved with this particular job) and selecting a Job and Application Workflow. This and other steps are described in greater detail in the article [Create and Launch a Job](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Post-or-Launch-a-Job).

Once you've saved the job, the job's Summary tab is displayed and you can further edit the job using **Edit Job** in the right-side contextual menu.

[Screenshot: Jobs tab with a newly created job selected]

If there are any related documents you want associated with the job, use **Add Attachment(s)** in the right-side contextual menu.

In addition to the *Summary* and *Listing* tabs, the job contains a collection of functional and metadata tabs. Before you post the job, you may want to implement the following through their respective tabs:

- **Questions** - Associate a questionnaire with the job. This is filled out by the candidate, a user (Hiring Manager or Job Owner), or both. With this feature, you can include an application form with the posting. There is no limit to how many questionnaires can be associated with a job. More on questions can be found in the article [Questionnaires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Questionnaires).
- **Scoring** - Create a scoring rule for the job which evaluates answers to certain questions from the associated questionnaires or keywords found in the resume. This allows you to easily spot and rank those candidates that are qualified and unqualified. More on scoring candidates can be found in the article *Library - Questionnaires* under the topic [Scoring Rules](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Questionnaires#scoring-rules).
- **Tasks** - With tasks, you and other users can review or complete items related to the job itself. For example, a task could be assigned to a Hiring Manager to review the job description. Tasks, like Events, help streamline the job posting activities by providing a simple mechanism for users to view the job details and submit feedback. You can also set up automatic email reminders to make sure tasks get completed and run reports to determine which tasks are requiring the most time to complete. More on tasks can be found in the article [Library - Task Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Tasks-Templates).
- **Events** - Schedule a meeting with other users in the company related to this job. For example, you can have a discussion about the job requirements before posting the job. More on events can be found in the article [Events Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Events-Tab).
- **Approvals** (if enabled) - This optional feature is related to the Job Requisition Approvals feature, which enforces a review process of the listing before posting to job boards. More on approvals can be found in the article [Job Requisition Approval](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Job-Requisition-Approval).

Both Tasks and Events can be added to multiple jobs at once from the list view page. Select the jobs using the checkboxes and then select the function from the right-side contextual menu.

[Screenshot: Job tab list view, multiple jobs selected and show events and tasks in menu]

#### Clone a Job

If there is a job for which you have *two* openings, or if you just want to duplicate an existing job, use the clone function. For the desired job, use the two-square clone icon under the *Actions* column.

[Screenshot: Job tab list view, clone button]

This duplicates the job with a new, unique job ID. It copies the original's job information, listing, questionnaires, and scoring rules. It does NOT copy any tasks or events from the original job.

### Launch a Job

Posting a job is done through a job's *Launch* tab, but first, the job stage must be set to *Open* . A job's current stage is displayed in the Stage column on the list view or under the job title when viewing a job. To change a job from Draft to Open, view the job and select the green **Open** stage button.

[Screenshot: indicate current stage and the stage change button on the Job summary page]

If the stage change button says something other than *Open* , select the down-arrow to the right of the button and select Open from the dropdown.

Once a job is in the Open stage, you can post it to any of your job boards through the job's **Launch** tab.

[Screenshot: Individual job's Launch tab.]

The Launch tab serves as a point of reference for all the job boards that can be used to bring candidates into the system. The job boards are divided into categories:

- **Text-To-Apply** (if enabled) - Configure a code word that applicants can text to your ApplicantStack number and get a link to view the job listing. More on this feature can be found in the article [Text-To-Apply](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Text-to-Apply).
- **Your Job Boards** - These are your public and, if enabled, internal job boards.
- **Indeed Sponsored** (if enabled) - For companies that want to post the job to Indeed as a Sponsored (as opposed to Organic) posting. More on this is found in the article [Indeed Sponsored Jobs Integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Sponsored-Jobs-Integration).
- **Third-Party Job Boards** - Includes both free job boards, like Indeed Organic and LinkedIn Limited Postings, as well as paid job boards like Monster, ZipRecruiter, and CareerBuilder.
- **Social Media Sites** - Post your positions to your company's Twitter and LinkedIn feeds. In each case, you are prompted for a login to your company account.
- **Manual Posting Links** - These links are used to collect applicants through email or job boards that aren't listed above.

Settings related to job boards are found in ApplicantStack's *Setup* area. Administrators can access Setup from the Jobs tab by selecting **Configure** from the right-side menu and then selecting **Job Boards** from the options on the left. More details on job board configuration are found in the article [Setup - Job Boards - Public and Internal](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Setup-Job-Boards-Public-and).

Each listed board has a **Post Job** link that initiates the posting. Additionally, the **Edit Launch Status** button, near the top of the Launch tab, can be used to simultaneously post a job to select boards.

[Screenshot: Edit launch status button]

These boards include your public job board, Google, Indeed Organic, and LinkedIn.

[Screenshot: Launch status page]

Launching a job to these boards can also be initiated from the Jobs tab list view by selecting one more more jobs with the checkboxes followed by **Edit Launch Status** in the right side menu.

[Screenshot: Selected jobs with the Edit Launch Status highlighted]

For some third-party job boards, you may be asked to enter additional job information, like a location, before confirming the posting.

More details on the process of launching a job can be found in the article *Create and Launch a Job* under the topic [Launch a Job](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Post-or-Launch-a-Job#launch-a-job).

#### Internal Job Board

Your Internal Job Board needs to be enabled—it is not enabled by default. Instructions on this can be found in the article [Setup - Job Boards - Public and Internal](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Setup-Job-Boards-Public-and).

The Internal Job Board allows you to post your jobs internally for a number of days before they go live on your Public Job Board. When posting, click the checkbox labeled **Post this job internally first** and enter the number of days in the text box. For example, if you specify 14 days, when you click Submit, your job will initially appear on your Internal Job Board but NOT on your Public Job Board. Then, 14 days from posting, the job will automatically appear on your Public Board and also stay on your Internal Board. On any other sites, like Indeed or LinkedIn Limited Posting, the posting is also delayed for 14 days until the job is on your Public Job Board.

#### Third-Party Job Boards

Some of the third-party job boards do require additional configuration, job information, and an account with that job board itself. These requirements are called out when selecting the *Post Job* link on the Launch tab, but you can also check out these third-party job board articles to learn what's required:

- [Indeed](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Posting-Your-Jobs-to-Indeed)
- [ZipRecruiter](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Posting-Your-Jobs-to-ZipRecruiter)
- [Monster](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Posting-Your-Jobs-to-Monster)
- [Career Builder](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Posting-Your-Jobs-to-CareerBuilder)

#### Manual Posting Links

The *Manual Posting Links* section of the Launch tab is where you can add a job to sites and boards not listed under Third-Party Job Boards. It also contains email addresses that add a candidate's to the job through an email.

The following links are available in the Manual Posting Links:

- **Job Listing** - Takes candidates to the job listing page for this job on your Company’s Job Board.
- **Apply Online** - Takes applicants directly to the apply page to begin the online application for the Job.
- **Apply Email** - Allows candidates to apply to the job by sending an email to this address. The following rules apply for how the candidate is brought into the system:
  - The email address of the sender defaults as the candidate’s email.
  - If an attachment exists on the email, the system imports it as the resume and uses the email *body* as the cover letter.
  - If there is no attachment, the system uses the email body as the resume.
- **Recruiter Email** - Recruiters can send an email to address and attach resumes or emails from their candidates. Each email or resume becomes a separate candidate in the system. The sender’s email is NOT set as the candidate’s email, they are extracted either from the emails or attached resume.
- **Forward Email** - Recruiters and other stakeholders can forward emails from candidates to this email address. The system uses the same rules as the *Apply Email* , but the system recognizes that the email is not coming from the candidate and does not use the email's “From" Address as the candidate's email address

*IMPORTANT:* When using manual links, it's important to select the **Candidate Source** before copying these links. This is because the links do change based on the source selection, allowing the system to distinguish where the application was initiated.

*NOTE:* The Source values which you can choose are defined in Setup under the Application fields. Administrators can add values to this field. See [Configure Application Fields](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Fields) for details on how to set up the Source field.

### Edit a Job

Change a job's **Job Information** (the job fields), **User Access**, and **Workflow** by selecting the pencil icon in the *Actions* column on the Jobs tab list view.

[Screenshot: Jobs listview with the edit icon under the actions column called out]

Jobs can also be edited after they have been selected. In this case, use **Edit Job** from the right-side menu.

When editing a job, the *Workflow* section has additional fields that weren't there when it was originally created. The job's stage can be changed and you can set the Opened Date and the Filled Date. More on these fields are covered in the Fill a Job topic found later in this article.

In order to modify or add Questionnaires, Scoring Rules, Tasks, or Events, view the job and select the corresponding tab. There is also an **Info** tab for additional notes and details about the job. This tab contains information that is only visible internally. The Info tab has a rich-text editor, similar to the one used on the Listing tab, where you can add information that is shared with any users associated with the job.

#### Edit the Job Listing

To create or change a job's Listing (the job description), view the job and select the **Listing** tab. If the job doesn't have a listing, select either **Create Listing** or use a template from your library with **Select Template**.

[Screenshot: Listing tab on a job with no listing and create and template buttons called out]

If the job already has a listing and you want to modify it, select **Edit Listing**.

[Screenshot: Listing tab on a job with the Edit Listing button called out]

With the editor's toolbar, you can format text, insert links, and add images. You can also paste in text from another source or, for a new listing, select a template from your library by using the hyperlink under the tool bar.

[Screenshot: Create listing page with the template icon called out]

When pasting in from another source, like Microsoft Word, there are three "paste" option buttons in the toolbar:

**Paste (Ctrl+V)** - A straight copy and paste.

[Screenshot: Paste Ctl+V button on the toolbar]

**Paste as Plain Text** *(preferred)* - Pastes the text, but removes all the formatting. This option is recommended and works best for many job boards. You can reformat the text using the buttons in the toolbar.

[Screenshot: Paste as Plain text button on the toolbar]

**Paste from Word** - This option retains *some* formatting from Word, but it may also cause problems with how the listing is displayed on third-party job boards. For this reason, it's typically best to use *Past as Plain Text* when copying from Word.

When you are finished, click **Submit** to save your listing or **Cancel** to discard your changes.

#### Add Attachments

Attach documents, like a job description or notes about the job process, to a job with **Add Attachments** in the job's right-side contextual menu. Once the documents are uploaded, you can find them on the *Summary* tab.

[Screenshot: Document attached on the summary tab of a job]

### Fill a Job

When you have successfully hired a candidate, change the job's stage to **Filled**. This sets the job to inactive and removes it from your public job board. The job will also removed from third-party job boards within 24 hours, but the actual time may vary depending on the board.

To set a Job to *Filled* , view the job and change the stage to *Filled* with the green stage-change button.

[Screenshot: Job with the filled button called out]

This can also be done by editing the job selecting **Edit Job** from the right-side contextual menu. When you edit a job, the *Workflow* section has fields where you can change the stage and manually edit the job's Open and Filled information.

[Screenshot: Workflow section of a job being edited]

- **Stage** - The current Workflow Stage of the job.
- **Open Date** – The date the job was opened, which is used for report metrics.
- **Filled Date** – The date the was filled, which is used for report metrics.
- **Closing Date & Time** - The date the job should close automatically.

When you are finished, click Save to commit your changes.

### Change a Job to Inactive

When a job needs to be removed without being filled, change the stage to one of the following inactive job stages: *Cancelled* or *On Hold* . To do this, view the job and select the red **Cancelled** button for a one-click method of setting the job to inactive.

[Screenshot: Stage change button with dropdown and show red button]

You can also select the dropdown associated with the green stage change button and select **On Hold** if you want to classify the job differently from Cancelled because you may post it again in the future.

### Delete a Job

Deleting a job is not recommended because you lose all associated data with that job. Instead, consider changing the job's stage to one of the inactive stages, like *Cancelled* or *On Hold* . These stages essentially hide the job from your Active list views.

If you do wish to permanently delete a job, use the trashcan icon under the *Actions* column on the list view page or select one or more jobs from the list view and select **Delete** from the right-side contextual menu.

### View Job Data and Run Reports

## Message Templates

Message Templates are used to quickly compose commonly used email and text* messages to candidates. They can also be used in an application workflow to send a message to the candidate when the reach a certain stage. Message templates are created by selecting the **Library tab** and choosing **Messages** from the left navigation menu.

[Screenshot: Library tab]

The **Message Templates** list displays the following:

- **Name**
- **From** – Indicates whether the email is sent using the *System* or *User* identity.
- **Last Modified**
- **Actions** – Icons used to view, edit, or delete the template.

The ability to create a new template is available in the right-side action menu.

**NOTE:* Text messaging is an optional feature of ApplicantStack that incurs an additional monthly fee. It can only be enabled by an administrator. Details on enabling texting are found in the article [Activate Texting for ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack).

### Create a Template

To create a new template, select **Create Template** from the right-side action menu.

[Screenshot: Create Template]

Each template can have an email and, if enabled for your account, text message version.

Fill in the following fields for the template:

- **Name**
- **From** – The displayed sender of the message. This displays in the body of the message and is not the *actual* sender. **System**, an option that only applies to the email version of a message, does not allow the recipient to respond to the email. (For more on this, see the System Message Notes section later in this article.) Text message templates only have the **User** option.
- **Attachment** – Attach documents and files to the message. Files attached to a text template are converted into a clickable link.

The body field has separate tabs for composing email and text messages. If the *Delivery Method* doesn't include the text option, the **Text** tab is not selectable.

The email version of a message also includes limited formatting capabilities as well as a subject field.

A **Delay** can be set on email messages through the dropdown. The delay intervals are:

- 0-4 hours in 15-minute increments
- 1 to 7 days in single day increments
- 14 days
- 30 to 90 days in 30-day increments
- 180 days
- 1 year

[Screenshot: Email Template fields]

To create a text version of the template, select the **Text Message** tab. **Delays** are not available on text messages.

[Screenshot: Text Message Template]

You can copy the text from the email message field into the text message field using the link above the message text box or create an entirely new message specific to the text.

If either of the message types (email or text) are blank, then that format is not used.

Character Limits and Attachments

ApplicantStack's texting service *does* support messages greater than 160 characters, however, it is recommended to keep text messages brief. Wireless carriers and the devices themselves can handle longer messages differently, and a large texts may be broken into segments. Also, images are not supported through texting. Attachments are converted to a clickable link.

Select **Save** once you are finished and the template is now saved to the Library.

#### System Message Notes

The **System** option for a message's *From* field means the recipient of the email **CANNOT** respond. Use System when you don’t expect (or want) a response to the email, such as emails communicating that an application has been received or that you are not interested in the candidate.

By contrast, selecting **User** in the *From* field allows recipients to reply to the email. This should be used when you do want a reply, such as when sending a request for additional information or an interview.

### Insert Merge Codes

Merge codes can be used in both email and text messages, and they insert dynamic content from your ApplicantStack database. Select **Show Merge Codes**, below the text box, to view all the merge codes that are available for the message. You can insert a merge code by clicking it. ## Library - Questionnaires

Questionnaires collect data from either candidates or internal users *about* that aid you in your hiring process. Scoring rules can also be associated with these questionnaires to help filter your candidates between unqualified and top prospects.

This guide shows you how to create and edit questionnaires as well as how to apply scoring rules to the questionnaires.

**Topical Index**

- Access Questionnaires
- Create a New Questionnaire
- View Questionnaires
- Editing a Questionnaire
- Scoring Rules
- Questionnaire Actions

### Access Questionnaires

ApplicantStack™ comes with prebuilt questionnaires for your use. You can access these by selecting the **Library tab** and then the **Questionnaires** item on the left-side menu.

[Screenshot: library tab]

The **Questionnaires Grid** has three columns:

- Name
- Last Modified
- Actions - Icons representing view, clone, edit, and delete.

The page also includes a *Status* filter which allows you to display whether the questionnaire is *Active* or *Archived* in the system.

The right-side menu includes three buttons, which are **New Questionnaire**, **Archive**, and **Delete**.

### Create a New Questionnaire

Even though ApplicantStack™ includes prebuilt questionnaires for your use, you may need to create a questionnaire to capture the type of data that you need from a candidate. Select **New Questionnaire** from the right side menu to do this.

[Embedded video: https://player.vimeo.com/video/660968223]

When creating the questionnaire, first enter the basic information:

- **Name** - This is the name that appears in the online application.
- **Instructions** - An optional field which you can use to provide any instructions for the user completing the questionnaire.
- **For** - Select *Candidates* for questionnaires filled out by candidates or *Users* for questionnaires filled out by members of your organization.
- **Private** - Check if the candidate’s answers should only be available in reports and not displayed on the candidate’s record. This setting is used for data that you want to capture, but do not want it to be viewed by users of the system.

After completing the basic information, you can start adding questions.

A question needs a *Type* and *Text* :

- **Question Type** - The possible types of questions are:
  - **Label** - A field that isn't filled in by the users, but displays data; can be auto populated with system data, fields, or a merge code.
  - **Yes/No** - The user answers with a yes/no picklist.
  - **Multiple Choice** - The user is prompted to select one from a list of answers.
  - **Select Many** - The user can select more than one answer.
  - **Single-Line Text** - The user is able to type text into a single-line text box.
  - **Multi-line Text** - The user is able to type text into a multi-line text box.
  - **Date** - The user is able to select a date from a calendar.
  - **File** - The user is able to upload a file.
- **Question Text** - This is the exact wording of the question as it appears on the online application. For *Multiple Choice* and *Select Many* there is also a *Possible Answers* field where each option should be entered on a separate line.

Once you have chosen a Question Type, three additional standard check boxes need to be considered. They are:

- **Required** - Check to make this question required.
- **Side-by-side** - Check this to show the question on the left and the answer on the right.
- **Horizontal** - Check this box to show the "answers" list horizontally as opposed to the default vertical list; only applies to multiple choice and select many questions.

Some options also have an *Autofill* if you want to autofill the question for the candidate using an existing values in the system or merge codes.

Once you have completed your question, click **Apply** to add it to the questionnaire.

On the **Create Questionnaire** page, you are able to change the order of the questions by clicking on the question and dragging it to the desired position.

To create an exact duplicate of the question, use the clone option. With it, you could change some wording and have an all new question without having to reset it’s attributes. Cloning a question can be accomplished by clicking the double boxes in the **Actions** column by the question you want to clone.

[Screenshot: actions column with the clone button]

By clicking a question’s edit icon in the **Actions** column, you can edit the question while you are still creating the questionnaire.

If you need to delete a question, click the question’s delete icon in the **Actions** column by the question you want to delete.

You can enter another question by clicking the **Add Question** button. There is no limit to the number of questions that can be added to a questionnaire.

### View Questionnaires

A questionnaire is can be viewed after saving or by clicking the name of the questionnaire from the questionnaire list. This brings up the *View Questionnaire* page.

[Screenshot: viewing the questionnaire]

From this screen you can do the following:

- **Add Scoring Rules** - Filter your candidates using scoring rules (described later in this article).
- **Add Actions** - This allows you to add actions for your questionnaire (described later in this article).
- **New Questionnaire** - You can create a new questionnaire.
- **Edit** - You can edit the questionnaire that you are viewing.
- **Delete** - Allows you to delete the current questionnaire that you are viewing.
- **Preview** - Clicking this button will display the questionnaire in the format that it will appear when it is attached to your job.

### Editing a Questionnaire

There are two ways to edit a questionnaire. If you are on the **Questionnaire** screen, you can click on the questionnaire’s name in the **Questionnaire Grid**. This will take you to the **View Questionnaire** screen where you can click the **Edit button** on the right side menu. The other way to edit a questionnaire is to click the questionnaire’s edit icon on the **Questionnaire** screen, which takes you directly to the **Edit** Screen.

Both the basic fields and list of questions are available for edit. To edit a specific question, select the **Edit** icon for that question and the details will display for revision. Click **Apply** for the changes to be saved.

You may also add questions to the questionnaire by clicking the **Add Question** button.

*IMPORTANT:* When making changes to questionnaires, be aware of the impact the changes may have on the system:

- If a questionnaire is associated with more than one job, the changes made will apply to *all* jobs where the questionnaire is used.
- If a questionnaire has already been answered by candidates, you can add or reorder questions without impact but deleting questions or answers will result in lost data.

Once you have finished all of your edits, click the **Save** button on the right side menu to save your questionnaire.

### Scoring Rules

The **Scoring** module is a valuable tool that uses candidate answers, as well as words and phrases in their resume, to identify key factors that aid you in ranking applicants. The ability to score candidates based on this data allows you to quickly spot candidates that are unqualified for your jobs as well as candidates that are considered top prospects.

[Embedded video: https://player.vimeo.com/video/660970035]

There are two methods of creating scoring rules: through the Jobs tab and through the Library tab. In the case of the *Job* method, the rule is only applied to a specific job. With scoring rules created in the *Library* , they apply to any candidates who complete the selected questionnaire, regardless of the job. Both methods are described below.

#### Set Up Scoring Rules through the Jobs Tab

You can set up scoring rules for all the candidates for a specific job on its **Scoring Tab**.

[Screenshot: scoring tab]

Select **Create Rule** and choose a source for the rule:

- A questionnaire, in which case you would choose the questionnaire from your library.
- Resume, which looks for a a word or phrase that exists in a candidate’s resume.

Once you have selected your questionnaire, its questions are displayed, and you can assign points to the answers. You can assign points to as many questions as you like.

You may decide that the answers to certain questions might determine if a candidate is wholly unqualified for your job. You can indicate that this answer is a **knockout** by selecting the corresponding checkbox labeled **Knockout**. Even though an answer may be considered a knockout, these candidates are not removed from the database, but the indicator can be used for searching and sorting.

[Screenshot: assigning points]

When a rule is created with a source of **Resume**, you will need to enter a phrase that will trigger the rule and either award a certain number of points to the candidate or indicate they are unqualified if that word or phrase is found in their resume text. Enter the word or phrase in the field labeled **Phrase**. Enter the point value in the field labeled **Points**, or you can check the checkbox and make the word/phrase a **Knockout**.

[Screenshot: resume source rule]

Once all your rules have been assigned you can manage them through the **Scoring Tab** on the **Jobs Tab**. You can edit a scoring rule by clicking it’s corresponding **Edit** icon and remove a scoring rule by clicking it’s **Delete** icon.

Can I run a newly created scoring rule on previous candidates?

Yes, you can also run your newly created rules against candidates that have applied for the job previously by clicking **Run Rules** on the job's Scoring tab.

#### Set Up Scoring Rules through the Library

You can set up scoring rules for questionnaires in your Library which will apply to all candidates who answer the questionnaire. Note that the scoring for a candidate may use BOTH *Job* scoring rules AND *Questionnaire* scoring rules. Job scoring rules will take precedence in case of overlap.

To add scoring rules to a questionnaire in the library, click on the questionnaire’s name then, beside **Scoring Rules**, click **Add Rules**.

[Screenshot: scoring rules in library]

Once you click **Add Rules**, the **Create Scoring Rules** page is displayed and you can assign points to as many questions on the questionnaire as you like.

You may decide that the answers to certain questions might determine if a candidate is unqualified for your job. You can indicate that this answer is a **knockout** by selecting the corresponding checkbox labeled **Knockout**. Even though an answer may be considered a knockout, the candidates are not removed from the database because of a knockout answer, but the indicator can be used for searching and sorting.

[Screenshot: adding points to rules]

Once you have added all your scoring rules, click the **Save** button.

If you need to change any of the scores or delete the rules in their entirety you can do so by clicking the corresponding buttons.

**Questionnaire Actions** provide your ApplicantStack™ questionnaires with added functionality by sending emails to individuals automatically, sending a candidate to a new stage, or a combination of both. For example, you can add an action to your *Application for Employment* questionnaire to send a chosen email template to any of the applicant's entered references. You can use this feature to email referral questionnaires or requests for letters of recommendations to an applicant's references further automating the hiring process.

To use this feature, navigate to the **Library tab** and choose **Questionnaires** from the left-side menu. Select the questionnaire you wish to work with by clicking its name. On the *View Questionnaire* page, select **Add Actions.**

[Screenshot: questionnaire actions on the library tab]

On the **Edit Questionnaire Actions** page, you have the following options, each of which are explained below:

- Email Actions
- Stage Actions
- Candidate Email Actions

[Screenshot: editing actions]

#### Email Actions

You can create Questionnaire Email Actions to have the system send an email to a recipient entered in a questionnaire, like a reference, using an email template from your library. For each email that you want to trigger from this questionnaire, select the questions that contain the information. For example, if you were sending an email to the reference, you would select your *Reference Name* and *Reference Email* questions from the dropdowns, and then select the email template to send to the recipient.

[Screenshot: add rows for recipients]

- **Recipient Name** - Choose the field containing the email recipient's name from the drop-down.
- **Recipient Email** - Choose the field containing the recipient's email address.
- **Email Template** - Select the email template which is sent to the recipient. If you need help constructing an email template please see [Library - Email Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Email-Templates). Note that you can specify different email templates to go to different recipient types.
- **Add Row/Remove Row** - Clicking these links allow you to add additional rows so that you may add more recipients or remove rows if you need to remove recipients.
- **Send Emails** - You can set the emails to send immediately upon application submission or you can set them to send on a stage change. For example, you can have the emails send after a candidate passes the Manager Review stage. You will need to configure this in the Application Workflow Settings. These settings can be reached by clicking **Setup**, then **Configure**, then **Configure Application Workflow Stages**. Select the stage you want to have the email send by clicking its edit icon. Next check the questionnaire you need in the section labeled **Questionnaire Email Actions**. For more information on configuring workflow see [Configure - Application Workflow](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Workflow) .

#### Stage Actions

You may want to automatically move candidates from stage to stage when they answer your questionnaire. Using the stage actions, you can send the candidate to a specified stage when the questionnaire is submitted. To do so, select the stage from the drop-down.

#### Candidate Email Actions

If you need to send an email to the candidate as soon as they submit the questionnaire, you can set the trigger in this section by selecting the email you wish to send from the drop-down. The dropdown lists only *System* emails in the library—you cannot use message templates that are from a *User* , nor can you send a text if you have texting enabled.

Clicking **Save** will commit your changes.

#### Edit Actions

If you need to change the actions, click the questionnaire name and click the link Edit Actions. This will open the Edit Actions form and you may change the parameters that you have set or add additional ones.

From the Library tab you can select Forms, Questionnaires, Messages, Tasks, and Checklists:

From the Forms Template library menu, you can “Add Form”, “Import Form”, “Archive” and “Request Form”.

**Questionnaires** can be selected from the Library Tab’s left-side navigation menu to manage Questionnaires. After selecting, you can create a **New Questionnaire** using the link on the right side.

#### Create New Questionnaire

- **Add Question:** You must add at least one question in order to save this questionnaire.

  [Screenshot: Questionnaire Page]

#### Add Question to Questionnaire

Once you select **Add Question** a new menu will open where you start by choosing the **Question Type**.

[Screenshot]

For each type, a new dialogue will appears. You have the option of making any question required (the person filling out the questionnaire will not be able to submit until all required questions are complete). Choose **Apply** once you have completed setting up the question.

The question type options are:

- **Label** - A label is a text that will be displayed in the questionnaire. This requires no action from the individual filling out the questionnaire (i.e. Directions or informational text).
- **Yes/No**
- **Multiple Choice** - A Multiple Choice question is where you are given several options to choose from and the person answering the questionnaire chooses one answer. You will need to fill out the question text as well as the possible answers (one answer per line).

[Screenshot: Multiple Choice]

- **Select Many** - A Select Many question allows the person answering the questionnaire the ability to choose more than one answer. You will need to fill out the question text as well as the possible answers (one answer per line):
- **Dropdown** A Dropdown question is similar to a multiple choice question but will display in a dropdown list.
- **Single-line Text** - A Single-line Text question allows the person answering the questionnaire an area where they can add their short answer. You also have the option of validating the answers for a Single-line answer so that they match a specific format.

[Screenshot: Single Line Validation]

- **Multi-line Text** - A Multi-line Text question allows the person answering the questionnaire an area where they can add their longer answer.
- **Date** - A Date question displays a calendar for the person filling out the questionnaire to use for their answer.

Once you have added all of your questions, choose “Save” to save the questionnaire:

#### Questionnaire Actions and Options

Existing questionnaires can be modified using the ***Actions*** icons associated with each questionnaire, but please note that if you modify any of the question in a questionnaire this will affect all previous answered questions. For example, if you delete a question, it will delete it from all previous completed questionnaires. It is best to clone an existing questionnaire and make the modifications to the copy.

[Screenshot: Questionnaire Actions]

- **View Details** - Choose the “View Details” icon to see all of the questions.
- **Clone** - Choose the “Clone” icon the question. This will copy the questionnaire as well as any other values associated with this question.
- **Edit** - Choose the “Edit” icon to edit the questionnaire.
- **Delete** - Choose the “Delete” icon to “Delete” a questionnaire.

**Questionnaire Advanced Settings**, found in the right navigation menu requires knowledge of html coding to modify the appearance of your questionnaire.

- **Attachments:** Select any file(s) to attach to the email. For the text, attachments will be included as a clickable link.

## ApplicantStack Task Templates

Task Templates serve as a beginning point for tasks being created. In the **Library Tab,** click **Tasks** on the left side navigation menu.

[Screenshot]

You are presented with the **Task Templates Grid**. The following items are displayed on the grid:

- **Task Name** - The name given to the **Task Template**.
- **Object** – The task is assigned to a **Candidate** or **Job**.
- **Last Modified** - the Date and Time the template was last edited.
- **Actions** – Icons used to access, edit or delete the **Task template**.

Additionally, the ability to create a new Template or Delete one is available from the right side navigation menu.

### Create Task Template

Select **Create Template** to begin creating a Task Template from scratch:

[Screenshot]

The following options are available:

- **Object** **Type** – Select **Candidate** if this task will be performed for the purpose of evaluating specific candidates for hire. Select **Job** if this task will be performed for the purpose of working with specific jobs.
- **Task Name** – The name of the Task.
- **Notes** – A message or notes to assist the user(s) assigned to the task. These notes will appear in the email notification to the user and on the View Task screen.
- **Assigned To** – Select the users that will be assigned to complete this task. You may use the **Add Row** link to add more assignee's as desired. If you wish to select users more dynamically you may choose (Job Owners) or (Hiring Managers), and the task will be assigned to those users depending on which candidate/job the task is being added to.
- Assign Questionnaire - For candidates, a questionnaire may be added to the task or event and it will be available to answer when the task is being completed. These answers will end up on the candidate's feedback tab
- **Send Email Reminder** – You can select a frequency to send email reminders to complete the task, or choose "Never" to not send email reminders for this task. Note that these are reminders sent AFTER the task to remind users to complete the task by submitting feedback. For example, if you select "Every 3 Days" then users will get a reminder 3 days after the task date if they have not yet submitted feedback, and every 3 days until they submit feedback.

Select **Save** and the **Task Template** is now saved to the **Library**.

### Editing a Task Template

From the **Task Template Grid**, select the Task Template you wish to edit. This can be done by the following ways:

- Select the underlined name of the **Task Template** and then **Edit Template** from the right side navigation menu.
- Select the **Edit Icon** under **Actions** for the **Task Template** you wish to edit.

[Screenshot]

On the **Edit Template** screen, you will have the following options/fields:

- **Object** – Select **Candidate** if this task will be performed for the purpose of evaluating specific candidates for hire. Select **Job** if this task will be performed for the purpose of working with specific jobs.
- **Task Name** – The name of the Task or Event.
- **Notes** – A message or notes to assist the user(s) assigned to the task. These notes will appear in the email notification to the user and on the View Task screen.
- **Assigned To** – Select the users that will be assigned to complete this task. You may use the **Add Row** link to add more assignees as desired. If you wish to select users more dynamically you may choose (Job Owners) or (Hiring Managers), and the task will be assigned to those users depending on which candidate/job the task is being added to.
- Assign Questionnaire - For candidates, a questionnaire may be added to the task or event and it will be available to answer when the task is being completed. These answers will end up on the candidate's feedback tab
- **Send Email Reminder** – You can select a frequency to send email reminders to complete the task, or choose "Never" to not send email reminders for this task. Note that these are reminders sent AFTER the task to remind users to complete the task by submitting feedback. For example, if you select "Every 3 Days" then users will get a reminder 3 days after the task date if they have not yet submitted feedback, and every 3 days until they submit feedback.

Saving the edits will apply those changes to any future use of the template.

### Using Task Templates

Task Templates are available for selection by clicking the **Create Task** options under the **Candidate Tab** or the **Job Tab**. Note that once you select your template, you can change any of the task details and it will not affect the **Task Template** in the library.

## Onboard a New Hire from ApplicantStack

New hires, recruited through ApplicantStack, can be transferred to WorkforceHubPlus and onboarded. Doing so streamlines the process by transferring basic employee data, already captured by applicant tracking, into WorkforceHub. This includes select documents, like their resume, being added to their File Cabinet. This article explains the steps and points you towards articles detailing the Onboarding process.

### Who Can Do This?

In order to transfer a candidate from ApplicantStack to WorkforceHub, you'll need:

- **WorkforceHub Plus or be using the legacy HUB/ApplicantStack Integration.** If you are a current ApplicantStack user, and do not have WorkforceHub, contact ApplicantStack.
- **The ability to change a candidate's Stage in ApplicantStack.** This permission is enabled for ApplicantStack Admins and Recruiters, but not necessarily enabled for Hiring Managers.

Additionally, if you want to continue the Onboarding process, you will need Admin-level access in WorkforceHub—department managers cannot perform Onboarding.

### Transfer a Candidate to Onboarding

1. [Access ApplicantStack through WorkforceHub](https://support.swipeclock.com/workforcehub/s/article/Access-Applicant-Tracking-from-WorkforceHub).
2. Choose the *Candidates* tab.
3. For the employee you want to hire, click their *Stage.*
4. Select *Hired.*

[Screenshot: setting a candidates stage to HIRED in ApplicantStack]

5. Click Submit.
6. Review the Stage change and enter optional items like notes or notifications.

[Screenshot: stage change dialoge]

7. Click Confirm Stage Changes. You will get either a success or error message. Error messages will contain further instructions.

If successful, the candidate will be transferred to WorkforceHub with the following data:

- Name
- Address 1
- Address 2 (if used)
- City
- State
- Zip
- Email
- Ethnicity Type
- Gender
- Job Name/Position Title
- Job Code/Job ID

ApplicantStack will also transfer select documents, like the employee's resume, into WorkforceHub's employee File Cabinet.

### Onboarding in WorkforceHub

After transferring a candidate to Onboarding, the employee will be visible in WorkforceHub under New Hires.

[Screenshot: the New Hires page in WorkforceHub]

Their status will be *Candidate Pending – waiting to start onboarding* . This means the Admin needs to start the Onboarding process by clicking the employee's tile.

More information on how Onboarding works can be found in the article [Onboarding](https://support.swipeclock.com/workforcehub/s/article/onboarding).
