## Create and Launch a Job

Each search for a new hire begins by creating a job in ApplicantStack followed by launching that job to a job board. This article covers those basics in two topics: *Create a Job* and *Launch a Job* .

You will need the *Administrator* role in ApplicantStack to perform these steps.

### Create a Job

Adding a new job listing to your ApplicantStack account is done from the **Jobs** tab. It's one of the functional tabs which appears at the top of the page throughout the system. Once selected, you'll see a list of the current active jobs and a contextual menu on the right side of the page. Select **Create Job** from that menu to create a new listing.

[Screenshot: The Jobs tab in ApplicantStack listing various open job listings, the Create Job menu item is called out]

After selecting *Create Job* , a pop-up asks you to choose if you want to create a job with a blank form or use a template. Unless you've been instructed to use a specific template, you can just select *Blank Form* for now. However, you can learn more about job templates in the article [Library - Job Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Job-Templates).

[Screenshot: icon of a play button]

**Watch how it's done.**
A video on creating a job is found in the article [Create a Job - VIDEO](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Create-a-Job-VIDEO).

On the subsequent page, fill in some basic information about the position. *Job ID* , a required field, is auto-populated, but you can enter your own unique identifier for the job if you choose. All these fields can be used for filtering and sorting your various jobs throughout the system.

[Screenshot: The job information fields filled in while creating a job.]

Each job field includes a brief description of its purpose; and while not every field is required, filling them all in makes for a more effective recruitment process. Administrators can also add new fields and customize the existing job fields. Instruction on this is found in the article [Configure - Job Fields](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Job-Fields).

In addition to filling in the job fields, you'll be asked to complete the following for a new job:

- **Job Description** - Use the rich text editor to write a summary of the job for your candidates. This editor also includes a *Paste from Word* option that carries over basic formatting from your Word documents. However, not all formatting from Word is supported in ApplicantStack and you may find that the appearance doesn't match what was in your original Word document. To avoid this, use *Paste as Plain Text* instead and use the formatting options in the ApplicantStack styling bar.
- **User Access** - Determine which staff members have access to the job and its candidates. Their role can be either as a *Job Owner* or *Hiring Manager* , both of which are explained on the page. For more on adding users, check out the article [Setup - Users](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Setup-Users).
- **Workflow** - Select a specific Job and Application Workflow to be used with this job. Most companies use the default workflows, but if you want to learn more about how to customize workflows, check out the articles [Configure - Job Workflows](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Job-Workflow) and [Configure the Application Workflow](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Workflow).

After you save the job, it is in the *Draft* stage, which is indicated under the job title. Draft jobs are not visible on your job board.

[Screenshot: The Listing tab of a draft job with the Edit Job menu item called out]

A series of tabs show the details you entered in the previous steps. The job fields from the previous step are found on the *Summary* tab while the job description is found on the *Listing* tab.

Once you have set up the job, you can utilize some additional tools found on the various tabs related to the job, like Questions and Scoring Rules, or you can move on to the next step is to launch it to your job board.

#### Questions

The *Questions* tab of a job is optional, but you can use it to add an application form to the job posting or add some screener questions specific to the job. These questions are collected in a questionnaire that can be added to your library and reused. Questions can *also* be created to collect information from users within your company. For example, you could create a feedback questionnaire for the Hiring Manager assigned to the job.

To create a new questionnaire, select **New Questionnaire**.

[Screenshot: Jobs tab ith the Add Questionnaire button called out]

The Questionnaire has fields for a name, optional instructions, and whether it's completed by a candidate or user.

[Screenshot: Fields for a new questionnaire being filled in]

Three checkbox fields are also present:

- **Show on Application** adds the questionnaire to the job posting for the candidate to fill out.
- **Include in Library** saves the questionnaire to your library for future use.
- **Private**, when checked, means the the answers are not visible on the candidate record. Use this if the questions need to by anonymized and included in reports.

Select **Add Question** for each question. They can be the following types of questions:

- Label
- Yes/No
- Multiple Choice
- Select Many
- Single-line Text
- Multi-line Text
- Date
- File
- Signature

Once you've completed the questionnaire, select **Save**.

More on Questionnaires can be found in the article [Questionnaires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Questionnaires).

#### Scoring

The *Scoring* tab of a job is optional, but you can use it to quantify an applicant's qualifications based on answers to certain questions (created on the Questions tab) or keywords found in their resume.

To add scoring to a job, select **Create Rule**. When creating a Scoring Rule, you'll choose a source: Questionnaire or Resume.

With Questionnaire rules, choose a questionnaire and then assign points to certain answers. You do not need to add scoring to every question in a questionnaire.

[Screenshot: A page showing application questions with options to create points for certain answers and designate knockout questions]

You can also designate some answers as a **Knockout**, which helps quickly identify candidates that are not qualified. If a candidate provides an answer that's defined as a Knockout, a "KO" appears in their Score column on the candidate list.

[Screenshot: the candidate list where a candidate with a KO in the score column is called out]

With Resume rules, enter a word or phrase of value and assign it a point total.

Once you've completed the Scoring Rule, select **Save**. You can use **Run Rules** to retroactively apply the scoring to any candidates that have already applied.

More on Scoring can be found in the article [Scoring Rules](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Creating-Scoring-Rules).

### Launch a Job

Each job can be posted to your public and internal job boards as well as any third-party job boards you have set up. The third-party sites (which may require additional configuration), include paid job boards like Monster and CareerBuilder (account required), free sites like Indeed (with Indeed's approval), and social media sites like LinkedIn and Twitter.

*NOTE:* Posting a job to Indeed is not available to accounts in a trial period. For information about posting a job to Indeed, see [Post Your Jobs to Indeed](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Posting-Your-Jobs-to-Indeed).

[Screenshot: icon of a play button]

**Watch how it's done.**
A video on launching a job is found in the article [Post a Job - VIDEO](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Post-a-Job-VIDEO).

In the previous topic, the job was left in *Draft* status, so in order to post the job, the status has to be changed to *Open* . This is done with the green button to the right of the Job Title. The button's label indicates which stage the job will be moved to.

[Screenshot: The summary tab of a job with the OPEN button called out]

Depending on your company's configuration, selecting the Open button may result in a pop-up asking you to confirm the stage change. This pop-up also has options for adding a note and notifying other members of your organization.

Once you've changed the job's status to Open, you can post it to your job boards. Select the job's **Launch** tab and you'll see all the possible job boards for your company. Select **Edit Launch Status**.

[Screenshot: The launch tab of for a job]

On the following launch page, select the sites with the checkboxes and click **Next**.

[Screenshot: The job site selection page with the checkboxes highlighted]

Add information about the job location. See the following for information about posting remote jobs to [Indeed](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/How-to-Post-a-Remote-Job-on-Indeed) or [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a414765/post-remote-hybrid-or-on-site-jobs-with-job-wrapping#:~:text=Use%20the%20new%20auto%2Dtag,is%20turned%20ON%20by%20default).

(For important information about Indeed, please see the article [Indeed Jobs - Sponsored vs. Organic](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Jobs-Sponsored-vs-Organic).) Next, confirm that you want to post the job and click **Submit**. The job is posted to your public job board and you are ready to accept online applications!
[Screenshot]

*NOTE:* There can be a delay between the time you launch a job and when it actually posts to third-party job boards.

#### Share Your Public Job Board

Select **Open Job Board** from the Jobs tab menu to view your public job board and the posting. Your public job board is where applicants view the listing, upload a resume, and apply. If it hasn't been done already, copy the job board's web address (URL) from the address bar of your browser and add a link to it on your company's website. Once you do this, you and your team are ready to manage candidates.

Administrators have the ability to configure certain elements of a company's job boards in the *Setup* area of ApplicantStack. This includes options for enabling and setting up third-party job boards. For more on this, check out the article [Setup Job Boards - Public and Internal](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Setup-Job-Boards-Public-and).

ApplicantStack™ has partnered with CareerBuilder to enable customers to post their jobs directly to CareerBuilder with only a couple clicks, using their existing CareerBuilder inventory. The following is a walk through of posting a job to CareerBuilder, through ApplicantStack.

### Setup your CareerBuilder Account Information

Before you can use the CareerBuilder integration, you need to enable and set up the integration. Go to **Setup->Job Boards** and click **Edit Settings** for CareerBuilder.

[Screenshot]

> **Source Value**: Select a source value, to apply to all candidates who come from CareerBuilder. If you don't already have a CareerBuilder source value, go to Setup->Configure Application Fields->Source->Edit Options and add a value for CareerBuilder.
>
>
>
> **Account Username/Password**: Enter the username/password of your CareerBuilder posting account which contains your CareerBuilder purchased inventory. Note that your entire organization must use the same posting account credentials, so make sure this is an organization level account and not an individual recruiter account. You can request a separate username/password from CareerBuilder just for posting purposes at no additional charge. Please contact your CareerBuilder account representative for more details.
>
>
>
> **Status**: Set to Active to enable the CareerBuilder link on your Launch tab, or Inactive if you want hide the link and no longer post your jobs to CareerBuilder.

### Click Post Job from the Launch Tab of your job

Once you have your CareerBuilder integration set up, CareerBuilder will appear on the Launch tab of your jobs with a **Post Job** link. Note that your job must be Open in order to post your job to CareerBuilder, just like your primary job board.

[Screenshot]

### Fill in the Job Posting details

After you click Post Job, you will see a form with all the available fields for posting the job to CareerBuilder. Many of the fields, such as Job ID, Job Title and Job Description, will be pre-filled with the data you already entered for your job. The other fields will be left empty for you to assign.

[Screenshot]

> The fields, required by CareerBuilder, are indicated with a red asterisk. Fields without a red asterisk are not required. However, the more information you provide the better the chance that someone will find your job in a criteria search, so we recommend filling in all applicable fields.

### Check that Posting was successfully Queued

After you click Submit, ApplicantStack will attempt to queue the job to post to CareerBuilder. CareerBuilder uses a two-step posting mechanism, where jobs are queued to post first, and then will be posted a few minutes later. CareerBuilder will display a message indicating whether the job was successfully queued to post, or indicate any errors in the posting.

[Screenshot]

Even if CareerBuilder says that the job was successfully queued to post, that does NOT mean the job will be posted successfully. You will need to check back in a few minutes to see if the job was successfully posted, as described in the next section.

### Check the Status of the Queued Posting

When you return to the Launch tab, the **Status** of the CareerBuilder posting should say **Queued**, indicating that it is queued to post to CareerBuilder. It can take a couple minutes for the job to post to CareerBuilder, at which point the status will update to either **Posted** or **Error**. You can click **View Details** to view the details of the job posting.

[Screenshot]

In times of high traffic, it may take up to a half-hour for a queued job to post to CareerBuilder. If the status is still showing as Queued after a half-hour, please contact ApplicantStack support for help.

### View the Details of the Job Posting

Once the queued job has posted to CareerBuilder, you will be able to view the job posting details by clicking the View Details link.

[Screenshot]

> **Current Status**: Shows the current status of the job ad, i.e. Posted, Not Posted, Queued, Expired, etc.
>
>
>
> **Post URL**: The URL of the job on the CareerBuilder site. You can click this link to view the job on CareerBuilder.
>
>
>
> **Post Date**: The date the job was posted to CareerBuilder.
>
>
>
> **Expire Date**: The date the job posting will expire on the CareerBuilder site. After this date the job will come off the site and will no longer appear in the CareerBuilder search results.
>
>
>
> **Posting History**: This table shows the history of all CareerBuilder posting activity for this job in ApplicantStack, such as when the job is posted, modified, or removed. Each entry shows the Date of the activity and the User who performed the activity.
>
>
>
> **Edit Posting**: Click this to edit the information in the posting. You can edit the posting at any time while it is still posted, but the Post Date and Expire Date will remain unchanged.
>
>
>
> **Remove Posting**: Click this to remove the posting from the CareerBuilder site and search results. Note that the job will automatically be removed after the Expire Date.

### View the Posted Job on CareerBuilder

If you click the Job Posting URL you can view how the job looks on CareerBuilder. Here is an example of how the job will look posted on CareerBuilder.

[Screenshot]

When a visitor clicks the Apply link on the job posting in CareerBuilder, they will be taken to the Apply page for the job on your ApplicantStack job board where they will apply like any other applicant in your system.

### Removing the Job Posting

Once the expire date has been reached, the job posting will automatically come off of the CareerBuilder site. You don't need to remove job postings if you want them to stay on CareerBuilder for the full posting duration. However, if you want to take down a job posting from CareerBuilder before it has expired (for example if the job has been filled or you've reached your target number of applications), you can do so by clicking the **Remove Posting** link.

[Screenshot]

### Viewing Candidates from CareerBuilder

Candidates who find your job on CareerBuilder, and apply, will show up in your ApplicantStack database, just like any other candidate, but their Source will be automatically set as **CareerBuilder** (or whatever value you specified in the Job Board Settings up top). Since candidates apply directly on your ApplicantStack job board, they will go directly into your database, so there is no need to log in to CareerBuilder to retrieve your applications and manually import them into your database.

[Screenshot]

## Post Your Jobs to Indeed

This article covers the process to post your job to Indeed.

### Job Posting Standards

For information on Indeed's job posting standard, see [this article](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/115005915763). Jobs that do not meet Indeed standard may be subject to review and require additional information from the hiring company. Failure to adhere to these guidelines may impact job visibility on the site. Staffing companies should also review Indeed's [Policy - Recruitment-Based Companies](https://indeedemployers.zendesk.com/hc/en-ca/articles/360018069792-Policy-Recruitment-Based-Companies).

### Sponsor Jobs

Indeed recommends sponsoring your jobs to ensure they display at the top of search results and reach quality candidates faster. For more information on sponsoring jobs, see [Indeed Jobs - Sponsored vs Organic.](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Jobs-Sponsored-vs-Organic)

### Indeed Guidelines

For information about best practices for posting Indeed jobs, see [Indeed Job Posting Best Practices](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Job-Posting-Best-Practices)

### Posting Process

1. Create and launch your job using the process in [this article](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Post-or-Launch-a-Job).
2. Indeed is listed under *Third-Party Job Boards* on the Launch page, and you can choose it when initially launching a job. If you want to post an *already-launched* job to Indeed, just select the job from the Job tab and then select the Launch page.
  [Screenshot]
3. Selecting either **Edit Launch Status** or the **Post Job** link associated with Indeed takes you to a job board selection page where you check **Indeed Organic Postings**.
  [Screenshot]
4. These posts are added to Indeed's *organic* job feed. After they have been posted for at least eight hours, you can use [Indeed's Sponsored Job integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Sponsored-Jobs-Integration) to further optimize your recruitment for the job.
5. Select **Next**. You are then asked for additional information required by Indeed.
  [Screenshot]
6. Enter the following fields. These fields allow Indeed and other third-party job boards to correctly categorize your job for job seekers. For information on posting a remote job, see [Indeed's article](https://indeed.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/How-to-Post-a-Remote-Job-on-Indeed).
  - **Street** - Enter the street address for where the job is located.
  - **City** - You can only include **one city**, otherwise, your post may be ignored by the two sites.
  - **State** - Enter the two-letter abbreviation of the state in which the job is located.
  - Zip/Postal Code - Enter the zip code for where the job is located.
  - **Country** - Enter the country in which the job is located.
7. Select **Next**.
  The Edit Launch Status - Confirm and Submit page displays.
8. Click **Submit**. It may take up to 24 hours for your job to appear on Indeed. For brand new accounts it may take 3 to 5 business days depending on their review cycle.
9. After the job posts to Indeed, you can upgrade your job post to a sponsored listing. See [Indeed Sponsored Job Integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Indeed-Sponsored-Jobs-Integration) for the process to sponsor your job.

### Indeed Job Board Settings

Within ApplicantStack, there are some Indeed-specific job board settings. These are accessed by administrators by selecting their profile icon in the upper-right corner of any page, then completing the following:.

1. Select **Setup** to access your account setup page.
2. From the left-side setup menu, select **Job Boards** and choose the **Edit Settings** link associated with Indeed.

The settings for Indeed are described in detail on the page, but in summary, you can:

- Enable or disable posting to Indeed by setting the **Status** drop-down menu to **Active** or **Inactive**.
- Assign a **Source Value** that easily identifies candidates that apply through Indeed. The default is *Indeed* .
- Allow candidates to apply with their Indeed profile by setting **Allow Indeed Apply?** to**Mobile Only** or **Always (Desktop and Mobile)**.
- Enable or disable the Indeed Sponsored Jobs integration by setting **Allow Indeed Sponsored?** to **Yes** or **No**.
- Choose whether you want Indeed to display an estimated salary range for your posting based on similar jobs. This option is enabled by default. If you don't want Indeed to do this, use the **Indeed Salary** drop-down to choose a field on the Job Posting that includes salary information.
- Contact Indeed support through the Support Form link in the upper-right corner.

**Save** any changes to these settings with the button at the bottom of the page.

## Post Your Jobs to Local and Specialty Job Boards

ApplicantStack has partnered with many third-party job boards, such as [Monster](https://help.applicantstack.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000721034-Posting-your-Jobs-to-Monster)and [CareerBuilder](https://help.applicantstack.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000715213-Posting-your-Jobs-to-CareerBuilder) to enable automated posting of jobs. However, if you need to post your jobs to other job boards, such as local or specialty job boards, you can still do so in a way that all applications are collected in your ApplicantStack database. You can also utilize the screening questions, EEO/OFCCP identification and custom branding provided by your ApplicantStack job board.

Step 1: Create the job ad in the third-party job board.

First, you'll need to go through the normal process of creating a job ad, on your third-party job board. Follow the instructions provided by the job board, for information on how to create the job advertisement. Note that you can likely copy/paste the listing from ApplicantStack onto the third-party job board.

Step 2: Create the Job in ApplicantStack and Open the job.

If you haven't yet created and opened the job in ApplicantStack, you'll need to do that now. Follow the instructions in the [Jobs](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Jobs) guide or [Getting Started Guide (Recruit)](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Getting-Started-Guide-Recruit) to create a new job in ApplicantStack. Open the ApplicantStack job.

Step 3: Link the third-party job ad with your ApplicantStack Job.

On the Launch tab of the job, you'll see the posting links, which you can use to link the job up with the third-party job board.

[Screenshot]

Copy one of these links depending on your need:

- **Job Listing**: Use this link to send the candidate to a page that has your job listing, i.e. job description, with a button for them to click to Apply.
- **Apply Online**: Use this link to send the candidate directly to the online application for this job.
- **Apply Email**: Use this email address if you want to provide a way for the candidate to apply via email, i.e. send a message and attach a resume to the email.

In most cases you will likely want to use the Apply Online link, to direct the candidate directly to the online application for the job. If you are providing a synopsis in the job ad, and want to direct the candidate to a full job description, use the Job Listing link. If the third-party site does not allow you to add a link, you can use the Apply Email address to direct them to apply via email.

### Optional: Tracking the Source of applicants

If you want to track the Source of applications, you can select the appropriate value from the Candidate Source drop-down before you copy the link.

[Screenshot]

When you select a Candidate Source it will "tag" the links with a unique code so ApplicantStack will know that the candidate came from the source. If you are an Administrator, you can add you own options to the Candidate Source drop-down, by going to Setup-->Configure-->Configure Application Fields and editing the Source filed here:

[Screenshot]

Alternatively, you can use the Apply URL and type the source value at the end of the URL. For example, if your Apply URL was somesite.applicantstack.com/x/apply/a2fv471z86di, you would go to the end of the URL, enter a backslash and then your source. If you wanted to use CareerBuilder, your new Apply URL would look like somesite.applicantstack.com/x/apply/a2fv471z86di/CareerBuilder. Note that your source at the end of the URL should match the spelling and punctuation of the source in the source value drop down.

## Applicant Questionnaires

The ApplicantStack™ Library contains a section for your questionnaires, which can be used to collect additional information about a candidate as well as feedback about a candidate. Questionnaires stored in the **Library** can be used for any job, task, or event. For more information on the uses of questionnaires, see [Library - Questionnaires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Questionnaires) .

[Screenshot]

The **Questionnaires Grid** is accessible from the left side navigation menu and displays the name of the questionnaire, the date and time that it was last modified as well as the actions icons (including view, edit, and delete). Additionally, from this page you are able to create a new questionnaire or delete from the right side navigation menu.

### Create a Questionnaire

Questionnaires can be created from the Library as well as from the Jobs tab. When you create a new **Questionnaire** from the **Jobs Tab** you have the choice to include it in the library or make it specific to that job.

[Screenshot]

[Screenshot]

If the check box is selected, the Questionnaire is saved to the Library and can be used for any Job. Once saved to the Library, it will display in the Questionnaires List under the Library Tab. For more information on creating questionnaires see [Library - Questionnaires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Questionnaires) .

### Edit a Questionnaire from the Library

From the **Questionnaire Grid**, select the questionnaire you wish to edit. This can be done by:

- Select the underlined name of the questionnaire and then **Edit Questionnaire** from the right side navigation menu.
- Select the edit icon under the **Actions Column** for the questionnaire you wish to edit.

Saving the Edits will immediately apply to any Job for which the Questionnaire is associated. You should take special care with questionnaire editing. In cases where a Candidate has already answered the questionnaire, these edits may invalidate their answers. Often it is better to clone the existing questionnaire, make your edits to the copy you just created, then detach the old questionnaire and attach the new one to the job. See **Archive Questionnaire** for archive options and see [Library - Questionnaires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Questionnaires) for more details on editing a questionnaire.

### Archive a Questionnaire

You can **Archive** a questionnaire that you no longer want to display in selection boxes, but you don't want to delete. For example, if you create a new questionnaire to replace an old one, but you have candidates that answered the old one, you shouldn't delete the old questionnaire but rather archive it.

To archive questionnaires, select the the questionnaire(s) in the Library and then click **Archive**. You can view archived questionnaires (and unarchive them) by changing your view to show Archived questionnaires.

[Screenshot]

#### See Your Archived Questionnaires

#### [Screenshot]

To unarchive a questionnaire select it from the list and choose "Unarchive":

[Screenshot]

### Use Questionnaires from the Library

Questionnaires that are saved to the Library are available for selection on the following pages:

- Questionnaires can be added to the Apply page of a job. Under the **Jobs Tab** select the job you want to add the questionnaire to. Next select the **Questions Tab**. Select **Add From Library** from the right side navigation menu.
- When sending an Email, users have the option to **Include a link to a Questionnaire**. The Questionnaires that are available in that Picklist include those that are saved to the Library.

- **Dataset**: The data you wish to access for the Report. This selection with determine the fields that are available for selection in the **Fields** section of the report. These datasets are as follows:
  - Hires
  - Tasks

- **Type**: The level of detail and focus of the report.
  - **Detail**: Provides details on individual records for the selected data elements.
  - **Summary**: Provides a high level view of statistics.
  - **Chart**: Gives the ability to display your report as a chart. This type of report uses the same engine as the **Summary** type and is useful for visually representing counts and aggregate data. You can choose between Pie, Bar, Column or Line Graphs.
- **Draft**: Clicking **Draft** puts the report in draft mode. The report will be available to you, but not other users. You can remove it from **Draft** by clicking the **Draft** icon again.
- **Favorite**: Clicking the heart icon marks the report as a favorite.

##### Fields

- **Primary Field**: The main focus of a Summary Report. The Primary field is only available when Summary Type is selected for a Report.
  - **Select Category**: This dropdown will determine which fields will be available for selection.
  - **Select Field**: Select the field that you wish to make the primary field in the Report. The Category selected will determine what fields are available for selection. You can use the up and down arrows on the side of this text box to switch the order of the fields. Note that this is only available for **Detail** type reports.

- **Secondary Field(s)**: These are additional fields that can be included in the report. If **Detail** is selected for the **Type** of the report, then this field is called **Fields** and there is no primary or secondary fields.
  - **Fields**: These can be expanded by clicking the plus icon on the right side of the box. This will show you each field that is available in each grouping. To close the fields, click the minus icon. To select a field, click on the field and hold the left mouse button, then drag the field to the box labeled **Selected Fields**.
  - **Selected Fields**: This list contains the fields that you selected from the fields box. You can remove these fields by clicking them and holding the left mouse button, then drag the field to the Fields box. You can rearranged these fields within this box as well by clicking the field you want to move and holding the left mouse button, then dragging the field to your desired position.

*Note: Fields can be selected from multiple Categories in the Data Set, you are not limited to selecting fields from one Category - you can also pull in fields from Forms &* *Questionnaires*

[Screenshot: adding fields]

##### Grouping

ApplicantStack™ gives you the ability to group your reports by up to 3 categories. By selecting a Category and corresponding Field(s), you can Group the data on the report by those fields. The Categories and Fields available for groupings are the same as those in the fields section.

##### Filters

Not only can you group by data, you can also set up filters for reports to filter the data in more meaningful ways. Much like you can do with grouping, you can filter a report by selecting fields.

The filters categories can be expanded by clicking the plus icon on the right side of the box. This will show you each field that is available in each category. To close the categories, click the minus icon. To select a field, click on the field and hold the left mouse button, then drag the field to the box labeled **Selected Fields**.

You can remove these fields from the **Selected Fields** box by clicking them and holding the left mouse button, then drag the field to the Fields box. You can rearranged these fields within this box as well by clicking the field you want to move and holding the left mouse button, then dragging the field to your desired position.

When you are finished editing the report, you click **Save** to commit your changes or you can click **Save and Preview** to save your changes and preview your report with the first 100 results. Note that in preview filters have been disabled.

## ApplicantStack Recruit Reports Tab

ApplicantStack™ Reports offers your organization flexible and powerful reporting capabilities. The Report module offers features that range from a simple report that shows how many Jobs are being managed per month, to a detailed listing of candidates that can be exported from the system to a .csv file.

[Embedded video: https://player.vimeo.com/video/661018553]

### Report Grid

You can access the **Report Grid** by clicking the **Reports Tab**.

The layout of the Reports Grid has been divided into two sections. The first section is labeled Dashboard Reports. These reports are turn-key reports that display various recruiting metrics. The Dashboard Reports consist of:

1. Source Performance - The number of applicants and hires from each source
2. Time in Stage for Active Candidates – The average number of days active candidates have been in the workflow. You can use this report to determine if candidates are getting "stuck" in any of the stages of your workflow.
3. Hire Metrics - The summary of hire metrics for your jobs or departments. You can use this report to track hire metrics like % Hired and determine what percent of candidates are still Active in your workflow.
4. Stage Conversion - The number and percent of candidates that passed key stages of your workflow. You can use this report to determine where candidates are dropping out of your workflow.

These reports are advanced metrics reports and cannot be customized.

The **Dashboard Reports Section** contains the following fields:

- **Name**: The name of the report.
- **Description**: A detailed description of the report.
- **Actions**: Only one action is available for these reports and that is open.

The second section is **My Reports** and contains standard account level reports that can be altered as well as reports that you have created.

[Screenshot: reports grid]

The **My Reports Section** contains the following fields:

- **Favorites**: The report will have a red heart if it has been marked as a favorite.
- **Name**: The name of the report.
- **Description**: A detailed description of the report.
- **Last Modified**: The date the report was last modified or changed.
- **Actions**: The Actions column contains the following options:
  - **View Details**: Selecting this icon allows you to view the selected report.
  - **Clone**: Clicking this icon will create a copy or clone of a report.
  - **Edit**: Edit the report (Note that custom reports built by ApplicantStack cannot be edited by the user. The user will need to contact support for any changes. Depending on the scope of the change, there could be a charge to implement the change).
  - **Export**: Export the report to csv format.
  - **Delete**: Delete the report from the **Report Grid**.

The right side menu also contains the option to delete reports by selecting the check box by the report that you wish to delete. This menu also contains the option to create a report as well.

#### View Details

When you click **View Details** you are presented with the results of the report that you selected.

[Screenshot: details of a report]

The **Report Details** page contains the name of the report, a report description, when the dataset was generated as well as any filters that may be available and the fields that were chosen for the report.

If you have any filters on the report, you can use these to filter the report’s data in different ways. The example below shows the report filtered by the Job Stage Type. The report will change dynamically with a different selection from this Picklist.

[Screenshot: filtering a report]

For any report that has a Date Filter, a custom date range can be used by selecting **Custom** from the Date Filter’s dropdown menu.

[Screenshot: custom date range]

When a Filter is applied to a report, you are also able to set that Filter to be the default view by selecting the default Icon while the Filter is activated. “No Filter" will be applied if no other is selected.

You can also edit the report and export the report by selecting **Edit Report** and **Export CSV** from the right side menu. Clicking the link [Refresh] will refresh the report and display the latest data that the report is requesting.

#### Edit

You may find that you need to include more or less fields, apply groupings, or create/change filters in a report. You can edit any of the reports included in ApplicantStack™ as well as any reports that you create by clicking the edit icon. Clicking this icon opens the following page:

[Screenshot: report edit page 1] [Screenshot: report edit page 2][Screenshot: report edit page 3][Screenshot: report edit page 4]

There are many options that are available for each report.

##### Report Information

- **Name**: The name of the report.
- **Description**: A detailed description of the selected report.
- **Dataset**: The data you wish to access for the Report. This selection will determine the fields that are available for selection in the **Fields** section of the report. These datasets are as follows:
  - **Jobs**: Job data elements.
  - **Candidate**: Candidate and Application data elements.
  - **Tasks**: Task and Event data elements.
  - **Feedback**: Feedback/Questionnaire data elements.
  - **Job Board Accounts**: Job Board Account Data Elements, i.e. names of applicants and application status, usernames, etc.
  - **History**: Candidate Search data elements.
- **Type**: The level of detail and focus of the report.
  - **Summary**: Provides a high level view of statistics.
  - **Detail**: Provides details on individual records for the selected data elements.
  - **Chart**: Gives the ability to display your report as a chart. This type of report uses the same engine as the **Summary** type and is useful for visually representing counts and aggregate data. You can choose between Pie, Bar, Column or Line Graphs.
- **Draft**: Clicking **Draft** puts the report in draft mode. The report will be available to you, but not other users. You can remove it from **Draft** by clicking the **Draft** icon again.
- **Favorite**: Clicking the heart icon marks the report as a favorite.

##### Fields

- **Primary Field**: The main focus of a Summary Report. The Primary field is only available when Summary Type is selected for a Report.
  - **Select Category**: This dropdown will determine which fields will be available for selection.
  - **Select Field**: Select the field that you wish to make the primary field in the Report. The Category selected will determine what fields are available for selection. You can use the up and down arrows on the side of this text box to switch the order of the fields. Note that this is only available for **Detail** type reports.

- **Secondary Field(s)**: These are additional fields that can be included in the report. If **Detail** is selected for the **Type** of the report, then this field is called **Fields** and there is no primary or secondary fields.
  - **Fields**: These can be expanded by clicking the plus icon on the right side of the box. This will show you each field that is available in each grouping. To close the fields, click the minus icon. To select a field, click on the field and hold the left mouse button, then drag the field to the box labeled **Selected Fields**.
  - **Selected Fields**: This list contains the fields that you selected from the fields box. You can remove these fields by clicking them and holding the left mouse button, then drag the field to the Fields box. You can rearranged these fields within this box as well by clicking the field you want to move and holding the left mouse button, then dragging the field to your desired position.

*Note: Fields can be selected from multiple Field Groups in the Current Data Set. You are not limited to selecting fields from one Category*

##### Grouping

ApplicantStack™ gives you the ability to group your reports by up to 3 categories. By selecting a Category and corresponding Field(s), you can Group the data on the report by those fields. For example you can group by Job Name, Date, Source, Disposition, Score, etc. The Categories and Fields available for groupings are the same as those in the fields section.

##### Filters

Not only can you group by data, you can also set up filters for reports to filter the data in more meaningful ways. Much like you can do with grouping, you can filter a report by selecting fields.

The filters categories can be expanded by clicking the plus icon on the right side of the box. This will show you each field that is available in each category. To close the categories, click the minus icon. To select a field, click on the field and hold the left mouse button, then drag the field to the box labeled **Selected Fields**.

You can remove these fields from the **Selected Fields** box by clicking them and holding the left mouse button, then drag the field to the Fields box. You can rearranged these fields within this box as well by clicking the field you want to move and holding the left mouse button, then dragging the field to your desired position.

[Screenshot: selecting fields for filters]

Once you have your filters selected, you can set default filters. This is a good option to use when you are working with reports that display a large amount of candidates as this reduces the amount of time that it takes for the report to complete. This allows you to set filters that you use often as defaults. Your report will have these filters automatically applied on it's first run. You can use these filters as one time setting or you can elect to use them always and hide the filter field on the report. Click the link [Set Default] by the filter's name, then select an option(s) from the drop down menu. You can also check "Always use this value (hide filter)" to have this be the default setting every time the report runs.

[Screenshot: default filters]

When you are finished editing the report, you click **Save** to commit your changes or you can click **Save and Preview** to save your changes and preview your report with the first 100 results. Note that in preview filters have been disabled.

Example of a report in preview mode:

[Screenshot: report preview]

#### Exporting Data

Sometimes you may have a need to place your data into a spreadsheet. ApplicantStack™ provides a way for you to move data that you select out of ApplicantStack™ and into your favorite spreadsheet program.

You can export data by selecting the **Export** icon as well as from the **View Details** page. Selecting this option will export the report to a csv format where each field in the report is represented by a column and each record is represented by a row.

Any grouping that you have in place in the report will remain in the csv file, so your rows of data will be grouped as they are in the report. When you export from the report, the filter that is applied when the export is run will be used.

### Creating an Ad-Hoc Report

You can create a new report in ApplicantStack by selecting **Create Report** from the right side menu on the **Report Grid** screen. When creating an Ad Hoc report, users are able to decide which data they wish to report on (Job or Candidate data), choose Summary or Detail report and finally decide what data fields you wish to bring into the report.

The **Create Report** screen is very similar to the **Edit Report** screen and contains the same options to help create your new report. For more information see **Edit Report** above.

## Reset Your ApplicantStack Password

If you forget your password or want to change it, ApplicantStack makes it easy to reset. Follow the steps below based on whether you can log in or not.

**Note:** If you have multi-factor authentication enabled for your account, you will need to authenticate again when signing into ApplicantStack after changing your password.

## Password Requirements

Passwords must:

- Be at least 12 characters long
- Contain:
  - a number
  - an upper-case character
  - a lower-case letter
  - a special character

### Can’t Log In

1. On the **Login** page, select *click **here** if you forgot your login* .
2. Enter the **Email** you use for your ApplicantStack account.

3. Select**Submit**.
4. You will receive an email with a link to reset your password. Select the link.
5. Your username displays at the top of the page. Below, enter and confirm a new password.
6. Select **Submit**.

### Can Log In

You can change your password at any time if you are already logged in.

1. At the top right, open the **profile** menu.
2. Select **My Account**.
3. From the right pane, select **Edit Account**.
4. Enter your **current password**.
5. Enter and confirm a **new password**.

b:
## Integrate ADP with ApplicantStack Onboard

ApplicantStack Onboard can be integrated with ADP Workforce Now to pass new hire data to payroll.

***IMPORTANT:*** Integrations are free to use within ApplicantStack but require an account and/or subscription directly from the individual partners.

### 1 - Find the App on the ADP Marketplace

The first step is to acquire the ApplicantStack Payroll Connector from ADP Marketplace, which is found at [https://apps.adp.com/home](https://apps.adp.com/home). Make sure you are signed into your ADP account and then type "ApplicantStack" into the search box.

Choose **ApplicantStack Payroll Connector** from the results and click the **Buy now** button**.**

[Screenshot: ADP Marketplace]

Follow the prompts as the system connects to your ApplicantStack account and asks for your consent to send data through the integration.

### 2 - Configure Workforce Now

ADP has provided the following documentation indicating how to set up Workforce Now for the integration (see link below). Once you have finished the steps under *Create Applicant Onboard New Hire Template* , then return to this article for a tour of the integration and its configuration with ApplicantStack.

***IMPORTANT:*** The guide below indicates that you must name the template **Applicant Onboard**. This **MUST** be done in order for the integration to work.

**[ADP Workforce Now - Applicant Onboard - New Hire Template.pdf](https://swipeclock.my.salesforce.com/sfc/p/U0000000LfDu/a/0P000000LiOa/7ilLUwKLaV.o.XD.Fh4.8WxOxHZX0g5Jb85RjPuI8AI)**

### 3 - Configure the Integration

We have provided a very flexible system for configuring your integration and making sure that you can get the fields you need over to Workforce Now. You will need to be an Administrator in your ApplicantStack account to do this.

1. Log in to your ApplicantStack account and go to onboarding module. This is done by clicking the grid icon near your avatar and selecting **Onboarding** from the dropdown.

[Screenshot: Switch to Onboarding]

2. Click your avatar and choose **Setup.**
3. Choose **Settings** from the options on the left.
4. Click the new **ADP Payroll Settings** button on the right side and configure the following features of the integration.

#### Automatic Payroll Data Push

The integration can be set up to push your hire's details to ADP automatically. To turn this feature on, simply choose the stage using the **Push Stage** dropdown and select when you would like this to happen. As soon as the hire is set to that stage, they will be pushed into WorkForceNow.

[Screenshot: Select Auto Push Stage]

You may leave this field set to "(None)" to turn off the automatic push.

Note that there is a manual push that may be used as well.

#### Employee Field Settings

The ADP Workforce Now integration will accept a large number of fields from your system. The rest of the ApplicantStack ADP Payroll Settings page is dedicated to these fields. Note that all of the fields are set to "(Auto)" to begin with. This means that our system will do its best to find the right field to send over to ADP. You may ignore all of these settings and the automatic system will do a fair job of finding your info.

However, you will save more time and get the most out of the integration by properly configuring as many fields as you can. Simply click on the blue edit button next to any field to edit it.

[Screenshot: ADP Field Settings]

A box will open up showing you the name of the field in Workforce Now. Use the **Set from** dropdown to choose a source for the data. You can use and field, questionnaire, or form in onboard or recruit. The system operates in real-time to find the fields in your account so expect a several second delay in some cases while making choices.

[Screenshot: Field Mapping]

Remember to Save the page using the button at the bottom when you are done making changes.

Once you have finished with configuration, give it a try! Go to any hire on the Hires tab and click on their name. Scroll down to the ADP Payroll section and click **Manually Push to ADP Payroll.**

[Screenshot: Onboarding Button]

Once the push is complete the hire's history will have a new entry that says, **Hire data pushed to ADP Payroll**.

You may view/submit the new hire in WorkForceNow by logging into your ADP WorkForceNow account and clicking on **Process ⇒ HR ⇒ Hire/Rehire** and choosing the tab for **In-Progress Hires**.

See the following configure articles:

- [Configure - Job Fields](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Job-Fields)
- [Configure - Job Stages](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Job-Stages)
- [Configure - Job Workflow](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Job-Workflow)
- [Configure - Candidate Fields](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Candidate-Fields)
- [Configure - Application Fields](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Fields)
- [Configure - Application Stages](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Stages)
- [Configure - Application Workflow](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Configure-Application-Workflow)

[Screenshot]

### Setting the Account to Use as the Sender

ApplicantStack™ allows you to choose whom you would like the email to come from. This can be either the System or a User. If you do not want the applicant to reply back to the email, then you should select System to use in the **From** field. If you want to correspond with the applicant, then User would be the appropriate option to choose. The **From** field takes on a different name depending on whether the System or User is chosen as the sender of the email. These settings can be changed in the two areas below.

#### Account Settings

When you are creating an email within ApplicantStack™ and select “System" in the “From" field, the Organization Name is what will appear in “From" field when the email is sent to the recipient. Also note that this field will appear in the body of the email by **Company Name**.
In order to find and / or change the Organization Name, select **Update Settings** from the top right menu:

[Screenshot]

You will see the Company Settings screen:

[Screenshot]

Under the Account Settings header you will see the Organization Name. If you need to change this name, click **Edit Settings** from the right side menu.

[Screenshot]

Type in your Company Name in the **Organization Name** field. Scroll down and click **Save**.

#### User Settings

When you set an email to come from the user, then the email uses the users **Name** in the “From" field.
If you need to change the user’s **Name**, select **Setup** in the top right of the screen, click **Users** from the left side menu.

[Screenshot]

Under the **Name** column is the user’s **Name**. To change this, click the **Edit** icon under the **Actions** column.

Under the Contact Information header, you will see the **Name** field. Also note the **Email** field. This email address is used for all system correspondence for this user. Once you make your changes, scroll down and click **Save**.

For more information about using the features **Email Candidate** see [Candidates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Candidates)

### Notifications

#### Setting Notifications for Users

Another important email setting in ApplicantStack™ is the **Notifications** setting. This setting allows you to turn email notifications on or off for the users. When users are assigned to jobs, they can receive notifications about not only a job’s stage change, but an applicant that has applied for that job as well. When the **Notifications** setting is set to **On** users receive email notifications as applicants move through stages or if notes are submitted about an applicant. If it is set to **Off** the system logs the movement through stages and note submission in the applicant’s history, but does not send a notification to the user.

To set the **Notifications** to **On**, click **Setup** in the top right corner of your screen. Next click **Users** on the left side menu. Click the **Edit Icon** for the user that you want to turn **Notifications** on or off.

[Screenshot]

In the **Notification** dropdown select **On** or **Off** for the user. When you are finished, click **Save**.

#### Setting Notifications for Stages

You can set a notification on a stage. This will send an email out to the users that are associated with a particular job and/or candidate(s) whenever the job or candidate(s) enter a particular stage. To do set this notification click **Setup** from the dropdown in the top right corner, then click **Configure** on the left side menu. Next you want to choose either **Configure Job Workflow Stages** or **Configure Application Workflow Stages** depending on whether the stage is for applicants or jobs. Click the **Edit Icon** for the workflow (if you have multiple workflows setup in your account) then select the stage that you want to set the notification.

[Screenshot]

Select the account that you want to have notifications turned on or off by selecting the checkbox in the **Notify** column. If you want to turn on notifications for an account, that account must have the checkbox checked in the **Owner** column as well.

**Note**: It is a good idea to use the Job Owner and Hiring Manager for notifications. If you select a **Named User Account**, this account will receive notifications for all jobs and candidates entering this stage.

For more information on configuration options for stages see [Jobs](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Jobs) and [Candidates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Candidates).

The job boards are divided into multiple sections:

- **Your Job Boards** - Includes your Public Job Board and Internal Job Board.
- **Third-Party Job Boards** - Includes the following:

The column headings on the configuration page indicate the following for each board:

### Public Job Board Settings

To change the settings on your **Public Job Board**, click **Edit Settings** under the *Actions* column. This takes you to a configuration page. The link to your job board is listed at the top of the page. This link differs between your Public and Internal job boards.

[Screenshot: public job board settings]

Your Public job board's status is always Active—you cannot change that setting.

The **Job Board Settings** section contains the following:

- **Source Value** - Select a value that indicates, on the Candidate tab, that the application came from this job board. If you need to add values to this list, click the link in the associated descriptive text to the right of the field. Information on how to edit this field and other picklists is found in the article [Candidates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Candidates).
- **Resume** - Choose whether to prompt applicants to attach a resume when submitting an online application. The options for this dropdown menu are:
  - **Show, Required** - Applicants must submit their resumes.
  - **Show, Optional** - Applicants can submit their resumes but are not required to do so.
  - **Hide** - Applicants are not prompted to submit resumes. The field is hidden on the online application.
- **Cover Letter** - Choose whether you want applicants to submit a cover letter, as text, through the online application. This is accomplished by copy and pasting the cover letter into the supplied text box on the application. There are three options available for this setting:
  - **Show, Required** - Applicants must submit their cover letter.
  - **Show, Optional** - Applicants can submit their cover letter, but are not required to do so.
  - **Hide** - Applicants are not prompted to submit cover letter. The field is hidden on the online application.
- **EEOC Questions** - Option to include the system-supplied EEOC questionnaire in the online application. These are optional questions to collect Federal EEOC data. By default, any data collected is hidden on the application and can only be viewed through the reports available under the **Reports Tab**. The article [Reports Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Reports-Tab) has instructions on how to generate reports. The options available for this setting are:
  - **Show** - Shows the system supplied EEOC questionnaire and allows the applicant to answer it if they so choose.
  - **Show by Job** - Allows you to specify on the *Add/Edit Job* page whether to show EEOC questions.
  - **Hide** - Hides the system supplied EEOC questionnaire from the applicant.
- **Breadcrumbs** - Choose whether to show or hide the breadcrumbs (navigation at the top of the page) on job board pages. For example, if you plan to only use the *Apply* page of your job board, choose Hide so applicants are not be able to navigate to other pages.
- **Applicant Login** - Choose whether to require the applicant to create an account on your job board in order to apply. Setting the Applicant Login field to **No** means applicants must apply and submit their application in one sitting and fill out a separate application for each job that they wish to apply for. Setting this field to **Yes** allows applicants to:
  - Complete an application in more than one sitting.
  - Edit an application after submission.
  - Save a copy of their last application with their account.
- **Allow Edit** - Used in conjunction with the **Applicant Login** field and only has an effect if set to **Yes**. When Allow Edit is set to **Yes**, the applicant can edit their application after it has been submitted and update their profile in your database, which ensures that the most current information is available to you. Any change is documented in the candidate's history and an email notification to users in your organization can be set up as well. See [Candidates Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Candidates-Tab) for more information on setting email notifications.
- **General Job** - An optional field that provides a way for applicants to submit a general application to your organization. Select a job from the dropdown menu and a link is added to the job board allowing applicants to submit a general application.
  [Screenshot: submit a general application link]
- **Employment Application** - Optional field that allows you to select an employment application from your library to include for every job on this job board. This is useful if your company uses one standard application for all jobs, which means you would not have to add the application on a per-job basis. However, if you have different applications for different jobs, you will want to leave this field blank and add the applications on a per-job basis.
- **Google Analytics Tracking ID** - Capture page view data by entering your Google Analytics tracking ID.
- **Allow Referrals** - Choose **Yes** to enable a referrals page where employees (or others) can submit candidates for jobs and track Referred By. If enabled, the referral URL will be in the description for the field. Provide this link to employees for referring candidates.
- **Parse Resume** - When set to **Yes**, the resume field is moved to the top of the application and the applicant's contact information will pre-fill the contact fields on the application.
- **Show Search Filters** - You can set this to **Yes** to show Search Filters on the job board. Job Fields that are set to *Show on Job Board* , show as filters. Supported field types for filters include Text, Pick List, and MultiSelect Fields.
- **Use SSL** - Only available for sites that were originally set up with HTTP. Set this to **Yes** if you want to use SSL/HTTPS to encrypt traffic. Once enabled, you do not have the ability to revert back to HTTP. Using SSL/HTTPS means that all your application data will be encrypted, which is recommended when capturing confidential information like **Social Security Numbers**. If your company website utilizes SSL/HTTPS, then it is recommended that you change this setting to **Yes**.

The **Job Board Skin** section contains settings related to the appearance of your job board:

- **Job Board Skin** - Select which skin or template to use for your job board. ApplicantStack™ comes with a default skin, but you can request a custom skin that more closely matches your current website. To request a custom skin, contact your ApplicantStack™ representative.
- **Header Logo** - If you are not using a custom skin, you can upload your logo to show in the header of the default skin. The logo can be in jpg, gif, png, and bmp. The logo is shown at full size to ensure that the dimension will fit in the job board header.
- **Header Return URL** - You can enter a URL in this text box that allows the user to click on the header image and go to the URL that you specify. Often this is simply the URL for your company site.

The **Messages** section is where you can customize the messages and text that appear on the various pages of your job board. This is helpful when you need to supply specific instructions to an applicant or want to align your page with your organizations branding. Each field has a sample message that you can customize. A description of where the message appears is listed to the right of each field.

Some message fields contained HTML code. You can use basic HTML to format or change the color of text. You can also add hyperlinks to other pages. There is also some code enclosed in square brackets ([ ]). This code is used for links to applications and pages, and can display usernames and other system data. Below is a list of available codes and what they are used for:

- **[:orgname:]**: Your organization name
- **[:jbmyaccount_link:]**: Opens the My Account Page
- **[:jbgeneralapply_link:]**: Opens the General Application Page
- **[:jbcreateaccount_link:]**: Opens the Create an Account Page
- **[:jbforgotaccount_link:]**: Opens the Retrieve your Login Page
- **[:jbopenings_url:]**: Displays the URL for your job board
- **[:username:]**: Displays the applicant’s password
- **[:password:]**: Displays the applicant’s password
- **[:jbsearchagain_link:]**: Opens the Job Board Search Page

When you are finished, click **Save** to commit your changes. Otherwise, click **Cancel**

## Setup - Users

Adding users and changing their roles is done through ApplicantStack's *Setup* and can be managed by those with the *Administrator* role. There are two ways to get to the *Users* page:

- *On the Home page,* select **Manage Users** from the right-side menu.
  [Screenshot: Manage Users menu item on the Home page]
- *From any page,* select **Setup** from your avatar menu in the upper right and then choose **Users** from the left-side menu in Setup.
  [Screenshot: Setup in avatar menu shown with a separate image of the Users link in the Setup menu]

[Screenshot: icon of play button]

**Watch how it's done.**
A video on User Management is found in the article [My Account and User Management - VIDEO](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/My-Account-and-User-Management-VIDEO).

There are three levels of user in ApplicantStack:

- **Administrator** - A role typically assigned to one ore more persons in Human Resources that sets up and configures ApplicantStack. They are able to perform any action in the system.
- **Recruiter** - This level is intended for internal and external recruiters for your company. They have access to all candidates and jobs and can perform most actions in the system. The main difference between Recruiter and Administrator is that Recruiters cannot setup or configure the ApplicantStack account. Also, they must be set as a Job Owner in order to receive notifications about a job or candidate’s stage change.
- **Hiring Manager** - These are users who are responsible for hiring and are involved in reviewing and moving candidates through the application process, but they don't necessarily need to use all the components of ApplicantStack. A Hiring Manager does not have access to all jobs and candidates—only to those which they've been assigned. They also cannot edit or create candidates and jobs, nor can they setup or configure the ApplicantStack account.

The following grid summarizes the access levels available for users.

[Screenshot: grid image summarizing the permissions explained above for each user level]

### Add a User

Create a new user on the *Users* page by selecting **New User** from the right-side contextual menu.

[Screenshot: Users page with the new user menu item called out]

The following fields and options are available for a user's account:

- **Username** - This does not need to be an email and can contain spaces, but it must be unique.
- **Send the welcome email to the user** - When checked, the user gets an email with a link instructing them to log in and set their password. If you are not ready to send an invite email to the user yet, you can leave it unchecked and do it at a later time.
- **Name** - Enter the user’s full name here. This is how the user's name will appear in the *From* field for any emails sent via ApplicantStack.
- **Email Address** - Used for all system correspondence with the user. When sending an email through ApplicantStack, if *User* is selected as the sender (instead of *System* ), then the recipients will reply back to this address.
- **Title** - Used for job title.
- **Phone**
- **Timezone** - Used for the display of all system dates and times.
- **Security Level** - Choose the user's role in ApplicantStack (see above).
- **Notification** - When set to "On", this enables email notifications to the user related to jobs and candidates to which they are assigned.
- **Text Email Notification** - This setting only appears for accounts using the Texting feature. When set to "On", the user receives an email notifying them that a candidate or new hire has responded to a text sent by ApplicantStack. The email lets them know they can log into ApplicantStack and view the message.
- **Products** - If you are using both ApplicantStack Recruit and Onboarding, you can choose which products the user can access.
- **Email Signatures** - Customize the user's email signature for outgoing emails sent through ApplicantStack

When setting up a user, you can also define their **Event User Availability**. This availability window is referenced when Events are used to schedule job related meetings and interviews. Learn more about how it works in the article [Event Scheduling](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Event-Scheduling).

Once you have finished entering your new user, click **Save**. If you chose to send the welcome email, the user gets an email from **@applicantstack.com**. They should check their clutter and spam boxes if it does not appear.

## ApplicantStack Tasks Tab

You can create Tasks in ApplicantStack to track and manage activities for yourself and other users. Tasks help streamline the recruiting activities by providing a simple mechanism for users to view the candidate or job details and submit feedback, which could include a questionnaire from your library.

[Screenshot]

For example, you can create an **Executive** or **Candidate Review** task for a hiring manager to request that they review a job or candidate and provide feedback.

Tasks allow you to set up automatic email reminders to make sure key activities get completed. You can also run reports to determine which tasks and users are requiring the most time to complete.

### Create a Task

All tasks in ApplicantStack™ are associated with a Job or Candidate. Some examples of common Job Tasks are:

- Executive Review
- Hiring Manager Review

Examples of common Candidate tasks are:

- Candidate Review
- Phone Screen
- Reference Checks

To create a new task for a Job or Candidate, check the job or candidate in the Jobs or Candidates list and then click the **Create Task** button on the right side menu. This will open the Create Task form.

[Screenshot]

You can also create a new Task by going to your Library, then select the Tasks, then choose "Create Template" here:

[Screenshot]

[Screenshot]

#### Create a Task for a Job

The Create Task screen for a job contains the following information:

- **Created By**: Shows the person or user that created the task.
- **Job(s)**: This label lists the job(s) that the task has been created for.
- **Template**: You may choose a **Template** and it will auto-populate the form below. If this option does not appear, it means that there are no templates in your Library with Type set to **Task** and Object set to **Job**. See [Library Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Tab) for more information.
- **Task Name**: The name of the task.
- **Task Notes**: A message or notes to assist the user(s) assigned to the task. These notes will appear in the email notification to the user and on the View Task screen.
- **Assigned To**: This is where you assign the users that will need to complete the task. If you want to assign more than one user, then you can use the **Add Row** command to assign multiple users to the tasks.
- **Send Email Reminder**: You can select a frequency to send email reminders to complete the task, or choose Never to not send email reminders for this task. Note that these are reminders sent AFTER the task to remind users to complete the task by submitting feedback. For example, if you select "Every 3 Days" then users will get a reminder 3 days after the task date if they have not yet submitted feedback, and every 3 days until they submit feedback.

[Screenshot]

#### Create a Task for a Candidate

The Create Task screen for a candidate contains the following information:

- **Created By**: Shows the person or user that created the task.
- **Candidate(s)**: The names of the candidate(s) that the task has been created for.
- **Template**: You may choose a **Template** and it will auto-populate the form below. If this option does not appear, it means that there are no templates in your Library with Type set to **Task** and Object set to **Candidate**. See [Library Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Tab) for more information.
- **Job(s)**: This label lists the job(s) that the task has been created for.
- **Task Name**: The name of the task.
- **Task Notes**: A message or notes to assist the user(s) assigned to the task. These notes will appear in the email notification to the user and on the View Task screen.
- **Assigned To**: This is where you assign the users that will need to complete the task. If you want to assign more than one user, then you can use the **Add Row** command to assign multiple users to the tasks.
- **Send Email Reminder**: You can select a frequency to send email reminders to complete the task, or choose Never to not send email reminders for this task. Note that these are reminders sent AFTER the task to remind users to complete the task by submitting feedback. For example, if you select "Every 3 Days" then users will get a reminder 3 days after the task date if they have not yet submitted feedback, and every 3 days until they submit feedback.
- **Assign a Questionnaire**: You can select a questionnaire from your library to attach to your task for assigned users to complete. Once you click **Save**, ApplicantStack will send an email to each assigned user which contains the task details and a link to complete the task.

### Task Email Reminders

When you create a task, you can select a frequency to send automatic email reminders to the assigned user(s) until they complete the task and submit feedback. For example, if you select to send email reminders "Every 3 days", on the third day after the user receives the task notification they will receive an automatic reminder email to finish the task.

[Screenshot]

You can also send a manual email reminder to a user assigned to a task by clicking the **View Emails** command for a task. This command takes you to the Emails page for the task showing all emails to the assigned user for this task. At the bottom of the page you can send a reminder or follow-up email to the assigned user.

[Screenshot]

The **View Task** page for a candidate contains the Task Information, Candidate Information, Cover Letter (if applicable), Resume (if applicable), all questionnaire/form submissions (if applicable) and a place for the user to enter task feedback or a questionnaire for the user to submit if one was attached to the task.
