### Viewing All Tasks

Tasks are easily managed in ApplicantStack™ under the **Tasks Tab**.

[Screenshot]

"Expand Filters" at the top of the page can be used to filter the tasks page. For example, you can filter to see just the tasks that are Not Complete, or all tasks for a particular job.

On the Tasks main tab, Administrators and Recruiters will be able to view all tasks in the system, but Hiring Managers will only be able to view tasks to which they are assigned.

The columns on the grid are:

- **Name**: Name of the task. Clicking this will take you to a detail page for that task.
- **Job**: The job that the task is associated with. Clicking this will take you to that job’s summary page.
- **Candidate**: If a task has been created for a specific candidate, that candidate’s name will appear here. Clicking the candidate’s name will display that candidate’s summary page.
- **Assigned To**: The person that the task is assigned.
- **Status**: Indicates whether the task has been completed or is incomplete.
- **Created**: Displays the date the task was created.
- **Completed**: Displays the date that the task was completed.
- **Actions**: Lists additional actions that can be initiated on the selected task. These options are as follows:
  - **View Details**: Go to the View Task page and view the details of the selected Taskas well as submit feedback for, edit, delete or print the Task.
  - **Edit**: Clicking this will allow you to edit the task.
  - **View Emails**: Allows you to view the emails/notifications that have been sent and received about the selected task. You can also send emails to the task creator or assigned user(s).
  - **Delete**: You can delete the task.

## Text to Apply

Text-to-Apply sends your job posting to a candidate via text. The candidate texts a designated code word to your ApplicantStack text number and receives a link in the automated response. With that link, they can apply.

[Screenshot: text received by candidate with link to apply]

This feature is included with the Premium Texting plan, which can be [activated through the billing page](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack).

With Premium Texting enabled, each job has a **Text-To-Apply** button which appears above the job boards on the Launch tab.

[Screenshot: Text to apply on Launch]

To enable a job for Text to Apply:

1. Select the **Create Text Code Word** on the job’s Launch tab.
2. Enter a unique code word. This is the world the applicant will text to you ApplicantStack number to receive the job posting.
3. Select **Activate** to link the word to that job. This closes the code word dialogue.

You can now include this code word, along with your ApplicantStack texting number, in any marketing and outreach you do connected to this job. Applicants receive a message similar to this:

Hello! Thanks so much for your interest in working at <company name>. To start an application, just follow this link <link>

If you want to change the code word, or cease using text-to-apply, return to the job’s Launch tab and select the same button you used when creating the code word.

## Texting Candidates and Hires

This article explains how to text applicants directly from ApplicantStack with the texting feature, which can be used with both ApplicantStack Recruit and ApplicantStack Onboard. This feature is only available for US and Canadian customers and needs to be enabled by an Administrator. For instructions on how to *activate* texting, see the article [Activate Texting for ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack).

### Text a Candidate/Hire

Once activated, any ApplicantStack user can text a candidate or hire by selecting the mobile icon next to the phone number. There is also a **Text Candidate** option in the right-side candidate menu. If the candidate's number is not a valid mobile number, you will not see the icon.

[Screenshot: candidate text info]

Options for texting a candidate directly from the candidate page

Once you click one of these options, you can compose your message in a pop-up window. In addition to typing the message directly into the text box, you can also use the **Template** dropdown to select a message template from your library. See the article [Library - Message Templates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Email-Templates) for more on how to create text templates. You can also insert a link to one of your pre-made questionnaires.

[Screenshot: Compose a text]

The text composition box with options to use a template and include a questionnaire

Click **Send** to text the candidate or hire.

Character Limits and Attachments

ApplicantStack's texting service does support messages greater than 160 characters, however, it is recommended to keep text messages brief. Wireless carriers and the devices themselves can behave differently, and a large text may be received in segments. Also images are not supported through texting, and any attachments are converted to a clickable link.

Once you a send a message via ApplicantStack's text messaging, the candidate or hire receives the text message immediately via their mobile device and can respond.

[Screenshot: text example]

A text to a candidate

When you receive a response to a text message, the notification icon in the banner menu indicates the number of new messages for the account.

[Screenshot: text notification]

Notification on the dashboard that a text has been received

Clicking the notification icon expands the menu where you can choose to view all messages.

[Screenshot: view all messages]

View All Messages after clicking the notifications

Selecting **View All Messages** displays all interactions with the recipient.

[Screenshot: message history]

Candidate text history

A complete history of the text messages can also be viewed via the candidate’s History tab, where you can filter the texts.

Are text messages visible to all ApplicantStack users?

It depends on the user's role. Hiring Managers can only view messages for their candidates. Administrators and Recruiters can view all messages.

### Texting "Opt-Out"

Candidates and hires have the option to "opt out" of receiving text messages by replying to any message with "STOP".

[Screenshot: opt-out response]

Opting out of text messages

 If they do so, a notification appears in the text alerts near your avatar explaining that a text recipient responded with STOP.

[Screenshot: opt-out notification]

Notification a candidate opted out of texting

 You will also see the "STOP" message in the text thread. If you do try and text a recipient who has opted out of texting, you will get a **Delivery Failure** error message explaining that the user opted out of texting.

[Screenshot: delivery failure message]

Failure message when texting a candidate that opted out

If a recipient opts out of text messaging, you will need to communicate via email or by calling them. Candidates and hires that opt out of text messages can also restart the service by texting "START" to your text messaging number.

### Text Multiple Candidates the Same Message

A single text message can be sent to multiple candidates at once. From the Candidates list, select multiple candidates using the checkboxes or select the top-most checkbox to select *all* candidates. The "P" column indicates which candidates have a mobile phone number listed.

[Screenshot: Candidate list with mobile numbers]

From the Candidates list, you can text individual candidates or multiple candidates at once

Once the recipients are selected, choose **Text Candidate** from the right-side menu and you can compose a message in the same manner as if you were texting an individual candidate.

Each candidate receives their own unique text message; this is **NOT** a group text message.

If you try to send a text message to a non-mobile number, the following error message is displayed.

[Screenshot: Texting error message]

Error message for a text sent to a non-mobile number

### Email Notifications for a Text Response

When a candidate or hire responds to a text, there are two ways you will know that you have an incoming message. One is by logging into ApplicantStack where a notification icon near your avatar in the upper-right corner indicates one or more messages have been received.

[Screenshot: text notification]

New text dashboard alert

You can also receive an email whenever a text response is received, which is set up in *My Account.**

To enable incoming text notifications:

1. Click your avatar in the upper right corner.
2. Select **My Account**.
3. Click **Edit Account**.
4. Under *User Information* locate **Text Email Notification** and set it to on.
  [Screenshot: Text notification in My Account]
  Enabling Text notification in My Account
5. Click **Save**

*This feature requires that **Text Notification** is enabled at the company-level first. If you don't see an option for Incoming Text Notifications in *My Account* then it needs to be enabled by an Administrator for the account. For instructions on this process, see the topic [Incoming Text Notifications](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack#incoming-text-notifications) in the article Activate Texting for ApplicantStack.

t: Tips for Using Copy/Paste in the Formatted Text Editor
b:
When creating a **Job Listing** or **Listing Template**, you will have a formatted text editor where you can create formatted text (e.g. bold, bullets, font size, etc), just like a word processing program. If you already have your text in an existing document, such as a Microsoft Word document or web page, you can copy/paste from the document into the editor using the standard copy / paste clipboard commands.

If you do copy from an existing document source, it is recommended that you paste into the ApplicantStack editor using the **Paste as Text** command button.

[Screenshot][Screenshot]

The **Paste as Text** command will paste in the text and line breaks, but will NOT bring over any of the formatting from the source. You will then need to apply the desired formatting using the toolbar (bold text, bullet lists, etc). Although this is an extra step, this is the recommended method because it ensures your job description will look clean and consistent on your website.

The problem with copying over formatting from a source document is that the formatting is often different from the formatting of your website, where the job description will appear. For example, you may have Arial font in your document but your website uses Verdana. Or your website text might have a slightly different color or size. And once you bring the formatting over it can be hard or impossible to fix using the toolbar, which can only override some styling. This is especially true of Microsoft Word documents which copy formatting with the intent of recreating the exact printed document, which is not what you want on a web page.

Note that if your source is a relatively "clean" Microsoft Word document, you can try using the **Paste from Word** command button. This does a reasonable job of trying to remove the physical formatting from a Word document while retaining the key formats like bold and bullet lists.

b:
Sometimes you might run into strange behavior in ApplicantStackthat might affect performance (such as getting an error message.) Often times this is localized to your browser. Here are a few steps we recommend going through to help you to help troubleshoot what might be going on.

**1) TRY A DIFFERENT BROWSER OR GET THE LATEST VERSION OF YOUR BROWSER**

If you a currently in [Chrome](https://www.google.com/chrome/browser/), it might be worth it to see if you experience the same behavior in a different browser such as [Mozilla Firefox](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/products/). Does using an alternative browser help alleviate the situation? You might also want to make sure you're on the latest version of your browser and install an update.

**2) TRY CLEARING YOUR BROWSER CACHE AND COOKIES**

Sometimes clearing your browser's cache and cookies will help alleviate the issue. You can view instructions for different browsers below:

- Chrome: [https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?hl=en](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050)
- Firefox: [https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-clear-firefox-cache](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-clear-firefox-cache)
- Internet Explorer: [https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/products/internet-explorer](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/products/internet-explorer)
- Safari: [https://support.apple.com/kb/PH21411?viewlocale=en_US&locale=en_US](https://support.apple.com/kb/PH21411)
- Opera: [http://help.opera.com/opera/Mac/2393/en/private.html#deleteData](http://help.opera.com/opera/Mac/2393/en/private.html#deleteData)

**3) TRY DISABLING BROWSER EXTENSIONS**

Sometimes browser extensions can interfere with activity within your browser. You can view instructions for below:

- Firefox: [https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/disable-or-remove-add-ons](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/disable-or-remove-add-ons)
- Chrome: [https://support.google.com/chrome_webstore/answer/2664769?hl=en](https://support.google.com/chrome_webstore/answer/2664769)

**4) TRY INCOGNITO MODE**

Sometimes using ApplicantStackin an Incognito Window within Chrome will help with strange behavior within ApplicantStack. You can learn about Incognito Mode in Chrome by visiting here: [https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95464?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform=Desktop](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95464)

## Upgrade to Premium Texting

Premium Texting offers ApplicantStack users additional texting functionality for managing candidates and new hires. It includes all the features of Basic Texting, as well as the following:

- **Text to apply** - Candidates can text a code word to your ApplicantStack text number and receive a link to your job posting.
- **Texting in workflows** - Text messages are automatically sent to candidates and new hires* based on status changes. Select a message template from your library and incorporate it into the selected workflow.

**NOTE:* New hire workflows apply only to companies using ApplicantStack Onboard.

How much does Premium Texting cost?

Both Basic and Premium Texting plans incur additional monthly fees. These fees are shown when activating or upgrading your texting plan.

### Change Your Texting Plan

Administrators can upgrade their Basic Texting plan to Premium Texting on their billing page.

1. Select **Manage Billing** from the ApplicantStack home page.
2. Under *Current Texting Plan Details* , select **Change Texting Plan**.
3. Select **Get Premium Texting**.
4. Review the details and select **ACTIVATE**.

If you do not already have Basic Texting enabled, you may want to read the article [Activate Texting for ApplicantStack](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Activate-Texting-for-ApplicantStack) for more information on the initial setup.

If you receive resumes from applicants via email, it is easy to import these resumes into your ApplicantStack account. Follow the steps below to forward an email from an applicant into your ApplicantStack account.

First, login to your account, go to the **Home** tab, and click the **Upload Emails** command on the right menu. Then, select a Job from the list where you would like the resume(s) to go. The Job list shows **Open** jobs in your account. If you have not yet created any jobs, or none of your jobs are open, you will first need to create and open a job.

[Screenshot]

Then select a job to which you would like to upload the resumes:

[Screenshot]

When you click a job, it should open up a new email, which is addressed to a special recruiter email address for your account.

[Screenshot]

You may attach, to this email, each email that you would like to import into ApplicantStack. The method to attach an email will depend on which email client you are using. For Microsoft Outlook®, you should be able to click the **Attach Item** command, and then select emails from your inbox. For other email clients, please consult the user manual, to attach an email to another email. Although it is acceptable to do so here, the preferred method to upload actual resumes is **Upload Resumes** (on the right hand command menu).

Once all emails and/or resumes are attached, click **Send** to send the email to ApplicantStack.

Note that there is no limit to the number of emails/resumes that can be attached to an email when it's imported from ApplicantStack, but your ISP may impose a limit on the size of an email that you can send. Also, if an email is very large, it may take longer to reach our server. For that reason we recommend importing no more than 20 emails/resumes at a time through the email method.

It may take a few minutes for the email to reach our server, but once it does, ApplicantStack will create a candidate record from each email or resume.

[Screenshot]

The following are the rules that ApplicantStack uses, when importing candidates from email, using this method:

1. Each attachment (whether an email or resume) will result in 1 new candidate record in your database.
2. For resumes, ApplicantStack will read the resume and populate the contact information (name, address, phone, email) of the record, from the content of the email.
3. For emails that have attachments, ApplicantStack will use the body of the email as the cover letter and add the attachments (including resume) to the record.
4. For emails without attachments, ApplicantStack will use the body of the email as the resume, and the cover letter will be blank.
5. For all emails, ApplicantStack will use the email address of the email sender as the candidate email, and then pull the rest of the contact information (name, address, phone) from the resume.

ApplicantStack™ allows complex searching of resume text using Boolean logic, which uses the following syntax:

| OPERATOR | EXPLANATION |
| --- | --- |
| (no operator) | The default operator is AND, that is all words must exist for a record to match |
| / | OR operator, used to indicate that word1 OR word2 must exist for a record to match |
| ! | NOT operator, used to indicate that a word must NOT exist for a record to match |
| ( ) | Parentheses group words into subexpressions. Parenthesized groups can be nested. |
| " | A phrase that is enclosed within double quote ("") characters matches only records that contain the phrase literally, as it was typed. |

### Boolean Search Examples

The following are examples of Boolean search phrases:

| SEARCH PHRASE | EXPLANATION |
| --- | --- |
| engineering mechanical | Find resumes that contain BOTH **engineering** AND **mechanical**. |
| engineering / mechanical | Find resumes that contain EITHER **engineering** OR **mechanical**. |
| engineering !mechanical | Find resumes that contain the word **engineering** but not **mechanical**. |
| engineering (mechanical / electrical) | Find resumes that contain the words **engineering** and either **mechanical** or **electrical**. |
| "mechanical engineering" | Find resumes that contain the exact phrase **mechanical engineering**. |

b:
## Using Merge Fields in Message Templates

You can use mail merge fields in email and text templates to personalize the messages for applicants and insert dynamic content from your ApplicantStack database. To insert a mail merge field, you just type in the mail merge code for the field you would like to insert into the body of your message. For example, here is the body of an email template that will be personalized with the first name of the candidate to whom it is sent:

Hi {!candidate-firstname}. I have reviewed your resume and would like to talk with you further about your experience. Please reply back with some upcoming times you are available for a 10-15 minute phone conversation.

### Mail Merge Code Reference

Here is the list of mail merge codes that are available to use in a message template.

#### Job Fields

| CODE | DESCRIPTION |
| --- | --- |
| {!job-title} | The title of the job (e.g. Account Manager) |
| {!job-name} | The full name of the job, including ID (e.g. Account Manager [1024]) |
| {!job-location} | The value of the Location field of the job |
| {!job-department} | The value of the Department field of the job |
| {!job-*fieldname* } | You can get the value of any custom field by using this syntax. For example, for a field named "Close Date" you would use the code {!job-closedate}. |

#### Candidate Fields

| CODE | DESCRIPTION |
| --- | --- |
| {!candidate-name} | The full name of the candidate (e.g. John Doe) |
| {!candidate-firstname} | The first name of the candidate (e.g. John) |
| {!candidate-*fieldname* } | You can get the value of any custom field by using this syntax. For example, for a field named "Country" you would use the code {!candidate-country}. |

#### Application Fields

| CODE | DESCRIPTION |
| --- | --- |
| {!application-score} | The calculated score of the application (e.g. 10) |
| {!application-stage} | The name of the current stage of the application (e.g. Phone Screen) |
| {!application-source} | The value of the Source field (e.g. Website) |
| {!application-rating} | The value of the Rating field (e.g. Potential) |
| {!application-*fieldname* } | You can get the value of any custom field by using this syntax. For example, for a field named "Interview Date" you would use the code {!application-interviewdate}. |

#### Questionnaire Fields

| CODE | DESCRIPTION |
| --- | --- |
| {!qelink-*questionnaire_id* } | You can use this code to insert a link to a questionnaire such that the submission will be associated with the candidate. For more details see the article on [Including a Questionnaire Link in a Message Template](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Including-a-Questionnaire-Link-in-an-Email-Template). |

ApplicantStack™ has a robust **Questions** module that enables you to present a specific set(s) of questions to the applicant as part of the online application process. Using questionnaires can help you collect data on candidates that will allow you to sort through candidates more efficiently.

Internal users will find the **Questions** module helpful as it provides them the ability to give feedback on candidates throughout the application process.

There is no limit on how many questionnaires can be created and associated with jobs or used for candidate feedback.

### Adding Questionnaires to a Job

When a candidate applies for a job, they will generally fill out some basic demographic information and possibly attach a resume or cover letter. You can collect more detailed information from a candidate by attaching one or more questionnaires.

Adding a questionnaire to a job can be accomplished by navigating to the desired job’s detail view and then by selecting **New Questionnaire** or **Add From Library** from the **Questions Tab**.

[Screenshot]

If you wish to create a new questionnaire, please refer to [Questionnaires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Questionnaires)

When selecting **Add from Library**, you are presented with a list of existing questionnaires from the **Library**. A questionnaire can be added by clicking on or highlighting the name of the questionnaire. To select more than one at a time, hold down the **CTRL** key and click each desired questionnaire.

[Screenshot]

In the drop down choose **Share** if you want to use the questionnaire as is from the library and not make any modifications to the questionnaire. If you want to make modifications to the questionnaire for this specific job, choose **Copy**. This will make a copy of the questionnaire and associate it with this job only. Any changes you make will not modify this questionnaire in the library or this questionnaire that is attached to another job. When you have selected your questionnaire(s), click **Submit** to commit your selections or **Cancel** to discard your selections.

### Viewing Questionnaires submitted by Candidates

You can access any questionnaires submitted by a candidate by clicking on the candidate’s name, then clicking the **Answers Tab**. From the **Answers Tab**, you can access answers that candidates have provided to Questionnaires as well as edit them and submit new ones on their behalf.

[Screenshot]

For more information see [Candidates](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Candidates) .

### Submitting Questionnaires as Feedback

Clicking the **Feedback Tab** allows you to access questionnaire answers that other users have submitted regarding the candidate. Questionnaires can be attached to emails (see [Email Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Email-Tab) ), as well as tasks and events (see [Tasks Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Tasks-Tab) and [Events Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Events-Tab) ).

[Screenshot]

The questionnaires can be sent to multiple managers/reviewers to collect responses and each response set indicates the user who provided the answers.

You can edit the feedback submission by clicking the edit icon in the feedback name bar. This will open another screen allowing you to make your modifications and commit your changes. Clicking the trashcan icon will delete the questionnaire.

### Scoring Rules

You can set up scoring rules for all the candidates for a specific job. This is a valuable tool that can help you sort candidates in a more meaningful way. These rules can help you decide whether a candidate is unqualified for the position or a top prospect.

A Candidate’s score is displayed in the Candidate Grid and can be sorted by score. Knockout scores are displayed as **KO**. If no rules triggered for the candidate (i.e. there are no scoring rules for the job/questionnaire), the score will not display.

A filter can be applied to only show Candidates that have a score (or no score) or have a knockout indicator (or have not been knocked out). Score is also available as a data element for Reporting. See [Reports Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Reports-Tab) for more information.

[Screenshot]

You can create and view scoring rules in two places. The first is on the Job details page under the **Scoring Tab**.

[Screenshot]

Creating rules here will only apply to the selected job and will override any rules that you may have on an existing questionnaire. You will notice two buttons on the right side of the screen. The first is **Create Rule**. This is used to create a scoring rule for any given questionnaire or for words/phrases contained in resumes. The second button is **Run Rules**. Anytime an Online application is submitted to the system, the rules run and the candidate’s scoring is calculated. Rules can also be run manually from the Job Scoring tab by selecting **Run Rules**, which is especially useful if you have changed any of the scoring rules for a questionnaire as it will recalculate all candidates’ scores.

You can also create rules for questionnaires under the **Library Tab**. These rules will apply to every instance of the questionnaire no matter the job. For example, if the General Questions questionnaire had scoring rules attached and the questionnaire was attached to six jobs, all six jobs would use the same scoring rules unless overridden by creating rules for the particular job described above.

To learn more about how to create these rules, please see [Library - Questionnaires](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Library-Questionnaires) .

## Using the "Edit Launch Status" Button

When your job is ready to be posted/launched to your public job board, your internal job board, and/or third-party job boards (such as Google For Jobs, Indeed, JuJu, LinkedIn Limited Postings).

...Wait! What does *"ready"* mean?

Your job is ready to be posted when you have done the following:

- Created the job with a unique job ID - see [Creating a Job](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Creating-a-Job) for more information
- Added a complete job description - see [Write a Job Description](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Write-a-Job-Description) for more information
- Attached any optional pre-screener questions and/or application for employment - see [Creating a Questionnaire](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Creating-a-Questionnaire) for more information
- You have changed the job status to "Open"

Once you have done all of the above items, you are now ready to post your job.

From the jobs Launch tab, select "Edit Launch Status":

[Screenshot]

Then select/deselect any of the job boards listed on this screen, then select "Next":

[Screenshot: Launch Job to Job Board]

See [Setup - Job Boards - Public and Internal](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Setup-Job-Boards-Public-and) for more information about your public and internal job boards.

[Screenshot]

The following page is extremely important!

This is what gets sent to the third-party job boards!!! The job title on this page will be what the job boards use for your posting. This title can be different from the ApplicantStack job title used when you originally created the job. Make sure to follow the guidelines listed on the page to ensure your job will not be rejected by the third-party job boards!

[Screenshot]

Make sure to include only one location for the job. If your job has multiple locations, you will need to create a job for each location.

Note: Some job boards such as Indeed might want to charge you for location blasting. Location blasting is posting a job for free to multiple job locations. Contact your Indeed representative if you have any questions.

Then choose "Next" for the Confirm and Submit page:

[Screenshot: Confirm and Submit Job]

***IMPORTANT:*** When posting your job(s) from ApplicantStack to any of the third-party job boards in this section, you are submitting a legitimate job which follows the individual job board rules and requirements. ApplicantStack will post the job(s) on your behalf but we can't guarantee organic placement on sites like Indeed. Typically these sites only include jobs from Direct Employers in their organic feed. All new clients are subject to a review period which could delay your initial posting.

Once you hit "Submit", your job will be instantly available on your public job board and internal job board (if those were selected) and can take anywhere from a few hours to a few business days to appear on the third-party job boards.

## Screen With Verified First in ApplicantStack

Verified First is a background-screening solution that offers multiple products such as drug, social media, and occupational health screenings. It integrates with ApplicantStack through a browser extension and can be used during the Recruit and Onboard processes to screen candidates and new hires. See [Enable the Verified First Integration](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Enable-the-Verified-First-Integration) for installation instructions.

**NOTE:** You must have an account with Verified First for this process to be available. Refer to [verifiedfirst.com](https://verifiedfirst.com/) for more information.

To screen a candidate or new hire:

1. Open ApplicantStack.
2. Select the **Candidate** tab in Recruit or the **Hires** tab in Onboard and choose the employee.
3. Select the **Screen with Verified First** button that displays on the candidate or new hire’s *Summary* tab.
4. Log into Verified First.
  [Screenshot: Verified First Login page]
5. The following options display in ApplicantStack:
  - **Place New Order** opens a screening request form that you can complete or send to the candidate or new hire to fill out.
  - **Initiate Form I-9** opens the Verified First extension where you can enter your i9Advantage credentials and send section 1 of the I-9 to the employee.
  - **Open Menu** displays the Verified First Dashboard on the right side of your screen.
6. Select **Place New Order** to initiate a screening. The form populates with the candidate or new hire’s information. From this option, you can select a screening package for the candidate or new hire and add other users as subscribers to the results.
  [Screenshot: Verified First new order form]
7. Choose either of the following:
  - Select **SEND INVITE** to email an invitation to the candidate or new hire to complete their screening. After the screening is complete, they can print both their authorization and confirmation of the screening. The following is an example of the email sent to the candidate or new hire:
    [Screenshot: Email sent to new hire or candidate, notifying them that their background screening has been initiated]
  - Select **NEXT** to complete the screening questionnaire yourself.
8. Verified First emails you, and any subscribers, a confirmation when the screening is complete. You'll be able to access the report from the email as well as in ApplicantStack. On the candidate or new hire’s *Summary* tab, REPORT COMPLETE displays in place of the Screen with Verified First button. Select **REPORT COMPLETE** to view the report or make additional requests.
  [Screenshot: REPORT COMPLETE option with View Report highlighted]

t: What is the Difference between an Event and a Task?
b:
## Event

An event is anything that needs to be sent to another user and/or candidate that has a calendar date and time. For example, an interview or meeting that has a specific calendar date and time will be an event.

[Screenshot]

You have the ability to schedule events for a Candidate (such as a phone screen and/or interview) as well as an event for a Job (such as a meeting for internal employees to review a job).

See [Events Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Events-Tab) for more information.

## Task

A task is a to-do which needs to be completed. A task is used to track and manage activities for yourself and/or other users. Similarly to an event, a task can be associated with either a candidate or a Job.

For example, you might want to schedule a task for a candidate review or for a reference check. An example of a job task might be an executive review or a hiring manager review.

A task does not have a specific date and/or time associated with it.

[Screenshot]

See [Tasks Tab](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Tasks-Tab) for more information about a task.

t: Who in my organization will need a user login to our ApplicantStack account?
b: A user login is necessary for anyone who will be logging in to your account to post/manage jobs, administer the system or review candidates. Typically, this includes HR staff and recruiters, administrators, and hiring managers. ApplicantStack has flexible roles and permissions built into the system that allows you to give users access to only the functionality, jobs and candidates that they need to perform their job.

A clearly written job description is the first thing a potential new employee will see about your company.

Make sure you have a clear job title and follow the best practices article here:

- [Job Title Best Practices and ATS Quality Guidelines](https://helpas.payrollservers.info/s/article/Job-Title-Best-Practices-and-ATS-Quality-Guidelines)

Indeed offers some useful advice on how to write a job description:

- [How to Write a Job Description](https://www.indeed.com/hire/how-to-write-a-job-description)

## **ApplicantStack Hosted Job Board Skins**

The look and feel of your company's website can be closely matched on your job board using a custom skin. This skin is created by, and hosted on, ApplicantStack's servers. The skin also degrades elegantly to be compatible with mobile devices.

Because the skin is hosted on servers other than your own, ApplicantStack can also switch on a Secure Sockets Layer (SSL), which is the standard technology for keeping an internet connection secure and safeguarding any sensitive data being sent between two systems.

However, ApplicantStack can’t always match your site exactly. For example, purchased fonts are not possible due to licensing issues. Similarly, drop down menus often use proprietary code. So in that case, ApplicantStack offers the main menu without drop downs.

If you need changes made to your job board, like to the menu links for example, you’ll have to contact ApplicantStack. Those changes can be made for you--usually within the hour.

Lastly, the URL for your job board is typically *[customer]* .applicantstack.com, but ApplicantStack can place it in a custom domain, such as jobs.*[customer]* .com so that it feels more like a part of your site.

If you're interested in a job board skin, please contact your account manager.
